options: the cathode gains mass and the anode loses mass|both electrodes gain mass|both electrodes lose mass|the cathode dissolves
answer: the cathode gains mass and the anode loses mass
rubric: Impure Cu anode dissolves (Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻); pure Cu deposits at cathode. Net purification.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is a non-electrolyte?
options: Dilute H₂SO₄|Molten NaCl|Glucose solution|NaOH solution
answer: Glucose solution
rubric: Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) does not ionise in water; it is a non-electrolyte that does not conduct electricity.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The chlor-alkali industry produces which three products from electrolysis of brine?
options: H₂, O₂, NaOH|Cl₂, H₂, NaOH|Cl₂, O₂, Na|H₂, Na, Cl₂
answer: Cl₂, H₂, NaOH
rubric: Electrolysis of brine: cathode gives H₂, anode gives Cl₂, and NaOH forms in the bulk solution.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The quantity of electricity in coulombs is calculated as
options: Q = V/R|Q = I × t|Q = P × t|Q = V × I
answer: Q = I × t
rubric: Charge (coulombs) = current (amperes) × time (seconds): Q = It.

subject: Chemistry
stem: During the electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid, oxygen is produced at the
options: cathode|anode|salt bridge|both electrodes
answer: anode
rubric: At the anode: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻. Oxygen is released at the positive electrode.

subject: Chemistry
stem: In anodising, aluminium is made the anode to
options: make it thinner|grow a thicker, protective oxide layer on its surface|remove all impurities|make it magnetic
answer: grow a thicker, protective oxide layer on its surface
rubric: Anodising oxidises the Al surface to build a thick Al₂O₃ layer that protects against corrosion.

subject: Chemistry
stem: If 0.5 A flows for 3 hours, the charge passed in coulombs is

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following increases the rate of electrolysis?
options: Decreasing the voltage|Increasing the electrode distance|Increasing the concentration of the electrolyte|Lowering the temperature
answer: Increasing the concentration of the electrolyte
rubric: Higher electrolyte concentration provides more ions, increasing ionic conductivity and rate of deposition.

subject: Chemistry
stem: During electrolysis of molten sodium chloride (NaCl), sodium is deposited at the
options: anode|cathode|both electrodes|neither electrode
answer: cathode
rubric: Na⁺ ions migrate to the cathode: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na (reduction). Na metal is deposited.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The rate of a chemical reaction is defined as the
options: mass of product formed|change in concentration of reactant or product per unit time|temperature at which reaction occurs|activation energy of the reaction
answer: change in concentration of reactant or product per unit time
rubric: Reaction rate = Δ[concentration] / Δt, expressed in mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Increasing the temperature speeds up a reaction primarily because
options: it increases the activation energy|it increases the frequency and energy of collisions|it increases the concentration|it lowers the activation energy
answer: it increases the frequency and energy of collisions
rubric: Higher temperature → more particles have kinetic energy ≥ activation energy → more successful collisions.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A catalyst increases reaction rate by
options: raising the activation energy|providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy|increasing the concentration|increasing the temperature
answer: providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
rubric: Catalysts offer a different mechanism with a lower Eₐ; more molecules can react at any given temperature.

subject: Chemistry
stem: According to the collision theory, a reaction can only occur when
options: molecules collide with any energy|molecules collide with sufficient energy and correct orientation|temperature is high|pressure is low
answer: molecules collide with sufficient energy and correct orientation
rubric: Successful collisions require energy ≥ activation energy AND correct geometric orientation.

subject: Chemistry
stem: In the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), increasing pressure will
options: decrease the yield of NH₃|shift equilibrium to the left|shift equilibrium to the right (more NH₃)|have no effect
answer: shift equilibrium to the right (more NH₃)
rubric: 4 moles gas → 2 moles gas; Le Chatelier: increased pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The equilibrium constant Kc for a reaction is
options: always greater than 1|unchanged by temperature|dependent only on concentration|changed when temperature changes
answer: changed when temperature changes
rubric: Kc depends on temperature only (not on concentration changes or catalysts).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Le Chatelier's principle states that if a system at equilibrium is disturbed,
options: the reaction stops|the system will shift to oppose the change|the temperature must rise|all equilibrium concentrations change equally
answer: the system will shift to oppose the change
rubric: Le Chatelier: a system at equilibrium responds to a disturbance by shifting to minimise that disturbance.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following does NOT affect the position of equilibrium?
options: Temperature change|Concentration change|Addition of a catalyst|Pressure change (for gases)
answer: Addition of a catalyst
rubric: A catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally; it does not change equilibrium position or Kc.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The Haber process operates at a moderate temperature (~450°C) rather than a lower one because
options: lower temperatures give lower yield|the catalyst is inactive at low temperatures|lower temperatures would be too dangerous|the reaction is exothermic at low temperatures
answer: the catalyst is inactive at low temperatures
rubric: While lower T would favour NH₃ yield, the catalyst (Fe) works effectively only above ~400°C; rate is too slow otherwise.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The activation energy of a reaction is the
options: energy released when bonds break|minimum energy needed for a collision to result in a reaction|total energy of reactants|average kinetic energy of molecules
answer: minimum energy needed for a collision to result in a reaction
rubric: Activation energy (Eₐ) is the minimum energy threshold for a collision to produce a reaction.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following increases the rate of reaction between marble chips and dilute HCl?
options: Using larger marble chips|Decreasing the acid concentration|Using powdered marble instead of chips|Decreasing the temperature
answer: Using powdered marble instead of chips
rubric: Powder has a much greater surface area than chips; more surface → more collisions per second → faster rate.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution shows that
options: all molecules have the same energy at a given temperature|most molecules have the maximum possible energy|there is a spread of molecular energies with a peak at the most probable energy|temperature does not affect molecular energy
answer: there is a spread of molecular energies with a peak at the most probable energy
rubric: The Maxwell-Boltzmann curve shows energy distribution; most molecules cluster near the most probable energy.

subject: Chemistry
stem: For the reaction A + B ⇌ C + D, if Kc > 1, then at equilibrium
options: reactants predominate|products predominate|concentration of A = concentration of C|no reaction occurs
answer: products predominate
rubric: Kc > 1 means the numerator (products) is larger than the denominator (reactants) at equilibrium.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A homogeneous equilibrium is one in which
options: no catalysts are used|all species are in the same phase|the forward reaction is faster|the equilibrium constant is 1
answer: all species are in the same phase
rubric: Homogeneous equilibrium: all reactants and products exist in the same phase (e.g. all gases or all aqueous).

subject: Chemistry
stem: The rate of reaction can be monitored by measuring
options: the colour change if applicable|only the mass|only the volume|only the temperature
answer: the colour change if applicable
rubric: Rate can be followed by colour change, gas volume, mass change, conductivity, or pH — multiple methods apply.

subject: Chemistry
stem: When a small amount of HCl is added to a buffer solution of CH₃COOH/CH₃COO⁻Na⁺,
options: the pH drops sharply|the pH remains nearly constant|the solution becomes strongly acidic|all the buffer is consumed
answer: the pH remains nearly constant
rubric: The CH₃COO⁻ ion reacts with the added H⁺; the buffer resists large pH changes.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The Contact process for manufacturing H₂SO₄ uses SO₂ + ½O₂ ⇌ SO₃. The catalyst used is
options: iron|vanadium(V) oxide|platinum|nickel
answer: vanadium(V) oxide
rubric: The Contact process uses V₂O₅ (vanadium pentoxide) as catalyst at ~450°C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which factor does NOT affect the value of the equilibrium constant (Kc)?
options: Temperature|Changing concentration|Changing pressure (Kp is affected, Kc may not)|Addition of a catalyst
answer: Addition of a catalyst
rubric: Kc depends only on temperature. Concentration, pressure changes shift equilibrium but do not change Kc at constant T.

subject: Chemistry
stem: A reaction with a very large activation energy will be
options: very fast at room temperature|very slow at room temperature|unaffected by temperature change|spontaneous
answer: very slow at room temperature
rubric: Large Eₐ means very few molecules have enough energy to react at room temperature → very slow rate.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Increasing the concentration of a reactant increases the reaction rate because
options: the activation energy decreases|there are more collisions per unit time|the temperature increases|the catalyst becomes more active
answer: there are more collisions per unit time
rubric: Higher concentration → more molecules per unit volume → more frequent collisions → faster reaction.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Organic chemistry is primarily the study of compounds containing
options: nitrogen|oxygen|carbon|sulphur
answer: carbon
rubric: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon-containing compounds (with exceptions like CO₂, carbonates).

subject: Chemistry
stem: The general formula for alkanes is
options: CₙH₂ₙ|CₙH₂ₙ₋₂|CₙH₂ₙ₊₂|CₙH₂ₙ₊₁
answer: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
rubric: Alkanes (saturated hydrocarbons): CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (e.g. CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Alkenes differ from alkanes in that alkenes contain
options: only single bonds|a triple bond|at least one C=C double bond|a benzene ring
answer: at least one C=C double bond
rubric: Alkenes are unsaturated; they have at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C).

subject: Chemistry
stem: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₃ is
options: methane|ethane|propane|butane
answer: propane
rubric: Three carbon chain with single bonds only: propane (prop = 3 carbons; ane = alkane).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which functional group is present in alcohols?
options: −COOH|−OH|−CHO|−NH₂
answer: −OH
rubric: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group (−OH) attached to a carbon atom.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is produced commercially by
options: cracking crude oil|fermentation of sugars|oxidation of ethane|reduction of ethanoic acid
answer: fermentation of sugars
rubric: Fermentation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (using yeast/zymase). Also produced by hydration of ethene.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol to form an ester is called
options: saponification|esterification|condensation polymerisation|hydrolysis
answer: esterification
rubric: Esterification is a reversible reaction: acid + alcohol gives ester + water, catalysed by concentrated H2SO4.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Isomers are compounds that have
options: the same molecular formula but different structural formulas|different molecular formulas|different molecular masses|the same structural formula
answer: the same molecular formula but different structural formulas
rubric: Structural isomers share molecular formula but differ in arrangement of atoms.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Addition polymerisation is a process in which
options: monomers with double bonds join to form a polymer losing small molecules|monomers join by condensation|a polymer is broken into monomers|a single monomer reacts with a catalyst only
answer: monomers with double bonds join to form a polymer losing small molecules
rubric: In addition polymerisation, alkene monomers open their C=C double bonds and join with no by-product.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The simplest aromatic compound is
options: benzene|toluene|naphthalene|aniline
answer: benzene
rubric: Benzene (C₆H₆) is the parent aromatic compound with a delocalized π electron ring system.

subject: Chemistry
stem: What type of reaction is the combustion of a hydrocarbon?
options: Addition|Substitution|Oxidation|Esterification
answer: Oxidation
rubric: Combustion is rapid oxidation: CₓHᵧ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O (+ energy). Complete combustion is full oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The functional group −COOH is characteristic of
options: aldehydes|carboxylic acids|ketones|esters
answer: carboxylic acids
rubric: The carboxyl group (−COOH) is the defining functional group of carboxylic acids.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which reagent is used to test for unsaturation in organic compounds?
options: Universal indicator|Bromine water|Benedict's solution|Fehling's solution
answer: Bromine water
rubric: Bromine water is decolourised by alkenes (addition across the C=C): Br₂ adds to the double bond.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The process of breaking large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones by heating is called
options: polymerisation|saponification|cracking|distillation
answer: cracking
rubric: Cracking (thermal or catalytic) breaks large alkane molecules into smaller, more useful alkenes and alkanes.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Nylon is an example of a condensation polymer formed from
options: alkene monomers|diamine and dicarboxylic acid monomers|alcohol monomers|benzene units
answer: diamine and dicarboxylic acid monomers
rubric: Nylon-6,6 forms from hexane-1,6-diamine + hexanedioic acid; water is lost (condensation) at each peptide-like amide link.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The homologous series of alkynes has the general formula
options: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂|CₙH₂ₙ|CₙH₂ₙ₋₂|CₙH₂ₙ₋₄
answer: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂
rubric: Alkynes (triple bond): CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (e.g. ethyne C₂H₂).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Saponification is the
options: fermentation of ethanol|alkaline hydrolysis of an ester to form a soap and glycerol|formation of an ester from an acid and alcohol|addition of water across a double bond
answer: alkaline hydrolysis of an ester to form a soap and glycerol
rubric: Saponification: fat/oil + NaOH → sodium soap (fatty acid salt) + glycerol.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The molecular formula of ethanoic acid (acetic acid) is
options: CH₄O|C₂H₄O|C₂H₄O₂|C₃H₆O₂
answer: C₂H₄O₂
rubric: Ethanoic acid: CH₃COOH = C₂H₄O₂ (2C, 4H, 2O).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which test would distinguish an aldehyde from a ketone?
options: Bromine water test|Tollens' (silver mirror) test|Iodine test|Litmus test
answer: Tollens' (silver mirror) test
rubric: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) is reduced by aldehydes to give a silver mirror; ketones do not reduce it.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The reaction of ethene with HBr is an example of
options: substitution|elimination|addition|condensation
answer: addition
rubric: HBr adds across the C=C double bond of ethene: CH₂=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CH₂Br.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Proteins are natural polymers made up of
options: glucose units|amino acid units|nucleotide units|fatty acid units
answer: amino acid units
rubric: Proteins are polypeptides formed by condensation polymerisation of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The dehydration of ethanol produces
options: ethane|ethene|methane|propene
answer: ethene
rubric: C₂H₅OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. Dehydration over Al₂O₃ or concentrated H₂SO₄ removes water to give ethene.

subject: Chemistry
stem: What is the structural formula of propan-2-ol?
options: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH|CH₃CH(OH)CH₃|CH₃COCH₃|CH₃CH₂CHO
answer: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃
rubric: Propan-2-ol has the OH group on the second carbon: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The empirical formula gives the
options: molecular mass of a compound|actual number of atoms in a molecule|simplest whole number ratio of atoms|structural arrangement of atoms
answer: simplest whole number ratio of atoms
rubric: Empirical formula shows the simplest ratio of elements, e.g. CH₂ for ethylene (actual C₂H₄).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Margarine is produced from vegetable oil by
options: saponification|cracking|hydrogenation|fermentation
answer: hydrogenation
rubric: Hydrogenation adds H₂ across C=C double bonds in unsaturated vegetable oils, converting them to saturated fats (margarine).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are harmful because
options: they are toxic to humans|they are flammable|they catalyse the breakdown of stratospheric ozone|they cause acid rain
answer: they catalyse the breakdown of stratospheric ozone
rubric: Cl radicals from CFCs catalyse ozone depletion: Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂ (repeated catalytic cycle).

subject: Chemistry
stem: In a condensation polymerisation reaction, the by-product released is usually
options: carbon dioxide|hydrogen|water|methane
answer: water
rubric: Condensation polymerisation (e.g. polyesters, polyamides) releases H₂O at each monomer linkage.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Ethanol is a primary alcohol because
options: it has one OH group|the OH group is on a primary carbon (bonded to only one other carbon)|it has the formula CH₄O|it is the smallest alcohol
answer: the OH group is on a primary carbon (bonded to only one other carbon)
rubric: Primary alcohol: −OH on C attached to only one other C. Ethanol: CH₃−CH₂OH — the CH₂ is bonded to one C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The reaction of benzene with a halogen in the presence of a halogen carrier catalyst is called
options: addition|free radical substitution|electrophilic substitution|nucleophilic addition
answer: electrophilic substitution
rubric: Benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution (e.g. halogenation with AlCl₃ as Lewis acid catalyst) — not addition, to preserve aromaticity.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following represents a primary amine?
options: R₂NH|R₃N|RNH₂|R₄N⁺
answer: RNH₂
rubric: A primary amine has one alkyl/aryl group on the nitrogen: RNH₂ (one N−H₂).

subject: Chemistry
stem: The main cause of the greenhouse effect is
options: oxygen|nitrogen|carbon dioxide and methane|argon
answer: carbon dioxide and methane
rubric: CO₂ and CH₄ trap outgoing infrared radiation from Earth (greenhouse gases), causing warming.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Acid rain is caused primarily by the emission of
options: CO₂ and CH₄|SO₂ and NOₓ|O₃ and CFC|HCl and HF
answer: SO₂ and NOₓ
rubric: SO₂ (from coal combustion) and NOₓ (from car engines) react with rainwater to form H₂SO₄ and HNO₃.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Eutrophication of lakes is caused by excessive
options: carbon dioxide|phosphate and nitrate fertilisers|industrial solvents|heavy metals
answer: phosphate and nitrate fertilisers
rubric: Run-off of nitrates/phosphates feeds algal blooms; algae die, bacteria decompose them, depleting O₂ → killing fish.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The ozone layer is important because it
options: provides oxygen for breathing|absorbs harmful UV radiation from the sun|reflects infrared radiation|provides nitrogen for plants
answer: absorbs harmful UV radiation from the sun
rubric: Stratospheric O₃ absorbs UV-B and UV-C radiation, protecting living organisms from DNA damage.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Carbon monoxide is a dangerous pollutant because
options: it is acidic|it reacts with ozone|it binds strongly to haemoglobin, blocking O₂ transport|it causes acid rain
answer: it binds strongly to haemoglobin, blocking O₂ transport
rubric: CO binds to Hb ~200× more strongly than O₂, reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity, causing asphyxiation.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Heavy metal pollution of water bodies is most commonly associated with
options: agriculture|industrial effluents and mining|burning coal|evaporation
answer: industrial effluents and mining
rubric: Industrial waste and mining discharge Pb, Hg, Cd and As into waterways — heavy metal pollution.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The most effective long-term solution to reducing SO₂ emissions from power stations is
options: building taller chimneys|using unleaded petrol|switching to cleaner fuels or fitting flue-gas desulphurisation units|increasing engine efficiency
answer: switching to cleaner fuels or fitting flue-gas desulphurisation units
rubric: Flue-gas desulphurisation (scrubbing) removes SO₂ before emission; switching to gas or renewables reduces it at source.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which gas is mainly responsible for global warming?
options: Oxygen|Carbon dioxide|Nitrogen|Hydrogen
answer: Carbon dioxide
rubric: CO₂ from burning fossil fuels is the dominant anthropogenic greenhouse gas driving recent warming.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Photochemical smog is formed when
options: water vapour reacts with dust|hydrocarbons and NOₓ react under sunlight to form ozone and PAN|coal is burned|sea spray evaporates
answer: hydrocarbons and NOₓ react under sunlight to form ozone and PAN
rubric: UV light drives reactions between VOCs and nitrogen oxides, producing ground-level ozone, PANs and other irritants.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Biodegradable pollutants are those that
options: persist in the environment for many years|can be broken down by microorganisms into harmless substances|cannot be dissolved in water|are always gaseous
answer: can be broken down by microorganisms into harmless substances
rubric: Biodegradable pollutants are decomposed by bacteria/fungi into CO₂, H₂O and simple minerals.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Iron is extracted from haematite (Fe₂O₃) in a blast furnace using
options: electrolysis|carbon monoxide as a reducing agent|hydrogen as a reducing agent|direct heating
answer: carbon monoxide as a reducing agent
rubric: In the blast furnace: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. CO reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The main ore of aluminium is
options: haematite|bauxite|galena|malachite
answer: bauxite
rubric: Bauxite (mainly Al₂O₃·2H₂O) is the principal ore from which aluminium is extracted by electrolysis.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with
options: copper and zinc|chromium and nickel|carbon only|tungsten and vanadium
answer: chromium and nickel
rubric: Stainless steel is Fe alloyed with ~10–20% Cr and ~8% Ni, which resist oxidation/corrosion.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which non-metal is a liquid at room temperature?
options: Carbon|Iodine|Bromine|Sulphur
answer: Bromine
rubric: Bromine (Br₂) is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature (mercury is the metallic liquid).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Sodium reacts with water to produce
options: sodium hydroxide and oxygen|sodium oxide and hydrogen|sodium hydroxide and hydrogen|sodium chloride and water
answer: sodium hydroxide and hydrogen
rubric: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. This reaction is vigorous for sodium.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The property of metals that allows them to be drawn into wires is called
options: malleability|ductility|conductivity|hardness
answer: ductility
rubric: Ductility is the ability to be drawn into thin wires without breaking; malleability is being hammered into sheets.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following is the most reactive metal?
options: Gold|Copper|Potassium|Iron
answer: Potassium
rubric: In the reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Chlorine is a non-metal that can be prepared by the oxidation of HCl using
options: NaOH|MnO₂|Na₂SO₄|water
answer: MnO₂
rubric: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O. MnO₂ oxidises HCl to Cl₂ on heating.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Galvanising is the process of coating iron with
options: copper|aluminium|zinc|nickel
answer: zinc
rubric: Galvanising coats iron/steel with zinc to protect it from corrosion; even when scratched, Zn acts as a sacrificial anode.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The test for hydrogen gas is that it
options: relights a glowing splint|gives a squeaky pop with a lighted splint|turns limewater milky|turns damp litmus red
answer: gives a squeaky pop with a lighted splint
rubric: A lighted splint produces a squeaky pop in the presence of H₂ — the characteristic test.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon. In graphite, carbon atoms are arranged in
options: a tetrahedral lattice|parallel layers of hexagonal rings|a face-centred cubic lattice|chains
answer: parallel layers of hexagonal rings
rubric: Graphite: flat hexagonal layers held by weak van der Waals forces; electrons are delocalised, making it conduct.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The transition metal used as catalyst in the Haber process is
options: nickel|vanadium|iron|copper
answer: iron
rubric: The Haber process catalyst is iron (Fe), often promoted with K₂O and Al₂O₃.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which metal is used in thermite welding because of its reaction with metal oxides?
options: Copper|Zinc|Aluminium|Sodium
answer: Aluminium
rubric: Thermite: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. Al has a higher affinity for oxygen, displacing Fe.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The test for oxygen gas is that it
options: gives a squeaky pop|turns limewater milky|relights a glowing splint|turns damp litmus red
answer: relights a glowing splint
rubric: A glowing splint that is placed in oxygen will reignite — the standard oxygen test.

subject: Chemistry
stem: An amalgam is an alloy of a metal with
options: iron|aluminium|mercury|zinc
answer: mercury
rubric: An amalgam is any alloy containing mercury (Hg) as one of its metals.

subject: Biology
stem: The basic unit of life is the
options: tissue|organ|cell|organism
answer: cell
rubric: The cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

subject: Biology
stem: The organelle responsible for energy production (ATP synthesis) in a cell is the
options: nucleus|ribosome|mitochondrion|chloroplast
answer: mitochondrion
rubric: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration, producing ATP — hence called the powerhouse of the cell.

subject: Biology
stem: Which organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
options: Mitochondrion|Ribosome|Golgi apparatus|Vacuole
answer: Ribosome
rubric: Ribosomes translate mRNA into proteins using transfer RNAs and amino acids.

subject: Biology
stem: The cell membrane is described as a fluid mosaic model because
options: it is solid and rigid|it has a fluid lipid bilayer with embedded proteins|it is made only of proteins|it has no lipids
answer: it has a fluid lipid bilayer with embedded proteins
rubric: The fluid mosaic model (Singer & Nicolson, 1972) describes a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded at various depths.

subject: Biology
stem: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of
options: high solute concentration to low solute concentration|low water potential to high water potential|high water potential to low water potential|high pressure to low pressure
answer: high water potential to low water potential
rubric: Osmosis: water moves down its water potential gradient (from dilute to concentrated solution) through a semi-permeable membrane.

subject: Biology
stem: The process by which cells engulf large particles is called
options: pinocytosis|exocytosis|phagocytosis|diffusion
answer: phagocytosis
rubric: Phagocytosis ("cell eating") is endocytosis of large solid particles, e.g. neutrophils engulfing bacteria.

subject: Biology
stem: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
options: Mitochondria|Ribosomes|Cell wall|Cell membrane
answer: Cell wall
rubric: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose outside the cell membrane; animal cells do not.

subject: Biology
stem: The nucleus controls cell activities mainly through its
options: lipid bilayer|chromosomes containing DNA|mitochondria|vacuoles
answer: chromosomes containing DNA
rubric: The nucleus contains DNA which encodes instructions for all cell activities and protein synthesis.

subject: Biology
stem: Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from a region of
options: low concentration to high concentration|equal concentration|high concentration to low concentration|high pressure to high concentration
answer: high concentration to low concentration
rubric: Diffusion occurs down a concentration gradient (from high to low) until equilibrium is reached.

subject: Biology
stem: A turgid plant cell is one that is
options: dehydrated and shrinks|fully inflated with water due to osmotic uptake|undergoing mitosis|losing water to a hypotonic solution
answer: fully inflated with water due to osmotic uptake
rubric: When a plant cell absorbs water by osmosis, its vacuole expands and pushes against the cell wall, making the cell turgid.

subject: Biology
stem: The Golgi apparatus is responsible for
options: energy production|photosynthesis|packaging and secreting proteins|DNA replication
answer: packaging and secreting proteins
rubric: The Golgi body modifies, sorts, and packages proteins into vesicles for secretion or transport to other organelles.

subject: Biology
stem: Chromosomes are found in the
options: cytoplasm|nucleus|cell membrane|mitochondria
answer: nucleus
rubric: Chromosomes (condensed chromatin/DNA) are housed in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.

subject: Biology
stem: The endoplasmic reticulum (rough ER) has ribosomes on its surface and is involved in
options: lipid synthesis|carbohydrate storage|protein synthesis and processing|DNA replication
answer: protein synthesis and processing
rubric: Rough ER bears ribosomes and processes proteins destined for secretion or membrane insertion.

subject: Biology
stem: Active transport differs from diffusion in that active transport
options: requires no energy|moves substances from high to low concentration|moves substances against a concentration gradient using ATP|occurs through a non-selective membrane
answer: moves substances against a concentration gradient using ATP
rubric: Active transport pumps molecules against their concentration gradient; it requires metabolic energy (ATP).

subject: Biology
stem: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes and are involved in
options: protein synthesis|intracellular digestion of worn-out organelles and foreign particles|photosynthesis|energy storage
answer: intracellular digestion of worn-out organelles and foreign particles
rubric: Lysosomes (suicide bags) digest unwanted materials, cellular debris, and pathogens using their enzymes.

subject: Biology
stem: Prokaryotic cells differ from eukaryotic cells in that prokaryotes
options: have a nucleus|have mitochondria|lack a membrane-bound nucleus|are always multicellular
answer: lack a membrane-bound nucleus
rubric: Prokaryotes (bacteria, archaea) have no nuclear envelope — their DNA floats free in the cytoplasm.

subject: Biology
stem: The process of mitosis results in
options: four haploid daughter cells|two genetically identical diploid cells|two genetically different cells|four diploid cells
answer: two genetically identical diploid cells
rubric: Mitosis produces two daughter cells with the same chromosome number and genetic content as the parent cell.

subject: Biology
stem: During meiosis, the number of chromosomes in the daughter cells is
options: the same as the parent cell|doubled|halved|quadrupled
answer: halved
rubric: Meiosis is reductive division; it produces four haploid cells (n) from one diploid (2n) cell.

subject: Biology
stem: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells and are responsible for
options: respiration|active transport|photosynthesis|protein synthesis
answer: photosynthesis
rubric: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis, converting light energy into chemical energy.

subject: Biology
stem: The cell cycle stage during which DNA replication occurs is
options: G1 phase|S phase|G2 phase|M phase
answer: S phase
rubric: DNA is replicated during the synthesis (S) phase of interphase, before mitosis begins.

subject: Biology
stem: Which of the following is a function of the cell vacuole in plants?
options: Protein synthesis|Storage of water, sap and waste products|Energy production|DNA storage
answer: Storage of water, sap and waste products
rubric: Plant central vacuoles store water (maintaining turgor), waste products, sugars, and pigments.

subject: Biology
stem: The semi-permeable nature of the cell membrane means it
options: allows all molecules to pass freely|allows no molecules to pass|allows only certain molecules to pass|is made of cellulose
answer: allows only certain molecules to pass
rubric: Semi-permeability: some molecules (e.g. water, small nonpolar molecules) pass freely; others are blocked or transported.

subject: Biology
stem: Centrioles are involved in
options: photosynthesis|cell respiration|formation of the spindle fibres during cell division|protein synthesis
answer: formation of the spindle fibres during cell division
rubric: Centrioles (found in animal cells) organise spindle fibres that pull chromosomes apart during mitosis/meiosis.

subject: Biology
stem: A cell placed in a hypertonic solution will
options: swell and burst|shrink (plasmolysis in plants / crenation in animals)|remain unchanged|undergo mitosis
answer: shrink (plasmolysis in plants / crenation in animals)
rubric: In hypertonic solution, water leaves the cell by osmosis; plant cells plasmolyse, animal cells crenate.

subject: Biology
stem: The molecular components of DNA are
options: amino acids, sugars and phosphate|nucleotides (deoxyribose, phosphate, nitrogenous bases)|fatty acids and glycerol|ribose, phosphate and bases
answer: nucleotides (deoxyribose, phosphate, nitrogenous bases)
rubric: DNA is a polymer of nucleotides, each consisting of deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base.

subject: Biology
stem: Photosynthesis converts light energy into
options: kinetic energy|thermal energy|chemical energy stored in glucose|electrical energy
answer: chemical energy stored in glucose
rubric: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Energy is stored as glucose.

subject: Biology
stem: The site of the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis is the
options: stroma of the chloroplast|thylakoid membrane|cytoplasm|matrix of the mitochondrion
answer: thylakoid membrane
rubric: Light-dependent reactions (photolysis, photophosphorylation) occur on the thylakoid membranes (grana).

subject: Biology
stem: The raw materials for photosynthesis are
options: oxygen and glucose|water and carbon dioxide|nitrogen and oxygen|glucose and oxygen
answer: water and carbon dioxide
rubric: Photosynthesis uses CO₂ (from air via stomata) and H₂O (from soil via roots) as raw materials.

subject: Biology
stem: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of
options: glucose|fats|starch|proteins
answer: starch
rubric: The iodine test: iodine solution (KI/I₂) turns blue-black when starch is present.

subject: Biology
stem: A balanced diet must contain
options: only carbohydrates and proteins|carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre|only vitamins and minerals|only water and carbohydrates
answer: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre
rubric: A balanced diet contains all seven nutrient classes in the right proportions for good health.

subject: Biology
stem: Enzymes involved in digestion are primarily
options: nucleic acids|lipids|biological catalysts (proteins)|vitamins
answer: biological catalysts (proteins)
rubric: Digestive enzymes are proteins that catalyse the hydrolysis of food macromolecules into absorbable units.

subject: Biology
stem: Amylase is the enzyme that breaks down
options: proteins|lipids|starch into maltose|DNA
answer: starch into maltose
rubric: Salivary and pancreatic amylase hydrolyse starch to maltose (disaccharide).

subject: Biology
stem: The vitamin required to prevent scurvy is
options: Vitamin A|Vitamin B12|Vitamin C|Vitamin D
answer: Vitamin C
rubric: Scurvy is caused by vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency; symptoms include bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

subject: Biology
stem: Lipase enzymes break down fats into
options: amino acids|glycerol and fatty acids|glucose and fructose|maltose
answer: glycerol and fatty acids
rubric: Lipase catalyses the hydrolysis of triglycerides (fats/oils) into glycerol and three fatty acids.

subject: Biology
stem: The final products of protein digestion are
options: fatty acids|monosaccharides|amino acids|glycerol
answer: amino acids
rubric: Proteases (pepsin, trypsin, chymotrypsin, peptidases) hydrolyse proteins to amino acids for absorption.

subject: Biology
stem: Which mineral is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
options: Calcium|Iron|Phosphorus|Iodine
answer: Iron
rubric: Haemoglobin contains four iron (Fe²⁺) ions at its haem groups, each binding one O₂ molecule.

subject: Biology
stem: The light-independent (Calvin cycle) reactions of photosynthesis occur in the
options: thylakoid membrane|stroma of the chloroplast|nucleus|cytoplasm
answer: stroma of the chloroplast
rubric: The Calvin cycle (CO₂ fixation by RuBisCO, reduction to G3P) occurs in the stroma.

subject: Biology
stem: Proteins are digested primarily in the
options: mouth|oesophagus|small intestine and stomach|large intestine
answer: small intestine and stomach
rubric: Pepsin (stomach) begins protein digestion; trypsin and chymotrypsin (pancreas, acting in small intestine) complete it.

subject: Biology
stem: The Benedict's test is used to detect
options: starch|reducing sugars|proteins|fats
answer: reducing sugars
rubric: Benedict's reagent turns from blue to brick-red precipitate in the presence of reducing sugars (e.g. glucose, maltose).

subject: Biology
stem: Chlorophyll absorbs light primarily in which colours of the spectrum?
options: Green|Red and blue|Yellow and green|Orange only
answer: Red and blue
rubric: Chlorophyll a and b absorb mainly red (~660-700 nm) and blue (~430-450 nm) light; green is reflected.

subject: Biology
stem: Mineral salt deficiency leading to stunted growth and yellowing of leaves in plants is caused by lack of
options: nitrogen|chlorine|oxygen|argon
answer: nitrogen
rubric: Nitrogen is needed for amino acids and chlorophyll; deficiency causes chlorosis (yellowing) and stunted growth.

subject: Biology
stem: The role of bile in digestion is to
options: digest fats chemically|emulsify fats into small droplets|absorb glucose|produce HCl
answer: emulsify fats into small droplets
rubric: Bile (from the liver, stored in the gallbladder) emulsifies fats into tiny droplets, increasing surface area for lipase.

subject: Biology
stem: The absorption of digested food mainly occurs in the
options: stomach|oesophagus|small intestine (ileum)|large intestine
answer: small intestine (ileum)
rubric: The ileum has villi and microvilli providing a huge surface area for absorbing glucose, amino acids and fatty acids.

subject: Biology
stem: Rickets in children is caused by deficiency of
options: Vitamin C|Vitamin A|Vitamin D and calcium|Vitamin B12
answer: Vitamin D and calcium
rubric: Vitamin D deficiency impairs Ca²⁺ absorption, causing soft and deformed bones (rickets in children, osteomalacia in adults).

subject: Biology
stem: The Biuret test is used to detect the presence of
options: starch|reducing sugars|lipids|proteins
answer: proteins
rubric: Biuret reagent (NaOH + dilute CuSO₄) turns violet/purple in the presence of peptide bonds (proteins).

subject: Biology
stem: Which of the following is the correct equation for photosynthesis?
options: CO₂ + H₂O → CH₄ + O₂|6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂|C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O|6CO₂ + 6O₂ → C₆H₁₂O₆ + H₂O
answer: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
rubric: Photosynthesis (overall): 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

subject: Biology
stem: The factor that most limits the rate of photosynthesis under normal conditions in shade is
options: water|CO₂ concentration|light intensity|temperature
answer: light intensity
rubric: In shady conditions, low light intensity is the limiting factor for the rate of photosynthesis.

subject: Biology
stem: Kwashiorkor is a disease caused by
options: vitamin A deficiency|protein deficiency|excess fat intake|iodine deficiency
answer: protein deficiency
rubric: Kwashiorkor results from severe protein deficiency, typically seen in young children weaned onto low-protein diets.

subject: Biology
stem: In holozoic nutrition, the sequence of feeding stages is
options: ingestion, egestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation|ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation, egestion|digestion, ingestion, absorption, egestion, assimilation|assimilation, ingestion, digestion, absorption, egestion
answer: ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation, egestion
rubric: Holozoic feeding sequence: ingestion → digestion → absorption → assimilation → egestion.

subject: Biology
stem: Saprophytic nutrition refers to organisms that
options: make their own food|eat other animals|obtain food by secreting enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorbing the products|live as parasites
answer: obtain food by secreting enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorbing the products
rubric: Saprophytes (e.g. fungi, some bacteria) secrete enzymes externally to decompose dead matter, then absorb the products.

subject: Biology
stem: The main function of red blood cells is to
options: fight infection|transport oxygen|produce antibodies|initiate clotting
answer: transport oxygen
rubric: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) contain haemoglobin, which binds and transports O₂ from lungs to tissues.

subject: Biology
stem: The liquid component of blood (excluding cells) is called
options: serum|plasma|lymph|haemolymph
answer: plasma
rubric: Plasma is the straw-coloured liquid that makes up ~55% of blood; it transports nutrients, hormones, CO₂ and waste.

subject: Biology
stem: The heart chambers that pump blood into the arteries are the
options: atria|ventricles|auricles|valves
answer: ventricles
rubric: Ventricles are the lower, thick-walled chambers: the right ventricle pumps to lungs, the left to the body.

subject: Biology
stem: Arteries carry blood
options: to the heart|from the heart (usually oxygenated)|only in veins|only deoxygenated blood
answer: from the heart (usually oxygenated)
rubric: Arteries carry blood away from the heart (the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs — an exception).

subject: Biology
stem: The main vessel carrying oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart is the
options: aorta|pulmonary artery|pulmonary vein|vena cava
answer: pulmonary vein
rubric: The pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart.

subject: Biology
stem: In plants, xylem vessels transport
options: sugars and amino acids|water and mineral salts|oxygen only|enzymes
answer: water and mineral salts
rubric: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves (transpiration stream). Movement is one-way, upward.

subject: Biology
stem: Phloem transports organic substances (sugars) in plants by a process called
options: transpiration|translocation|osmosis|diffusion
answer: translocation
rubric: Translocation is the movement of sugars (mainly sucrose) in the phloem from source (leaves) to sink (roots, fruits, seeds).

subject: Biology
stem: The opening and closing of stomata is controlled by
options: mesophyll cells|guard cells|xylem|root hair cells
answer: guard cells
rubric: Guard cells change shape by gaining or losing water; when turgid they open the stoma; when flaccid they close it.

subject: Biology
stem: White blood cells (leucocytes) function mainly to
options: transport oxygen|defend the body against infection|clot blood|produce red blood cells
answer: defend the body against infection
rubric: Leucocytes (neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes) combat pathogens through phagocytosis and antibody production.

subject: Biology
stem: Platelets (thrombocytes) are important for
options: oxygen transport|fighting infection|blood clotting (haemostasis)|producing hormones
answer: blood clotting (haemostasis)
rubric: Platelets aggregate at wound sites and initiate the clotting cascade, sealing damaged blood vessels.

subject: Biology
stem: The bicuspid (mitral) valve is located between the
options: right atrium and right ventricle|left atrium and left ventricle|aorta and left ventricle|pulmonary artery and right ventricle
answer: left atrium and left ventricle
rubric: The bicuspid (mitral) valve separates the left atrium and left ventricle, preventing backflow during ventricular systole.

subject: Biology
stem: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plants mainly through the
options: roots|bark|stomata on leaves|xylem vessels
answer: stomata on leaves
rubric: Most transpiration occurs through stomata; some occurs through the cuticle (cuticular transpiration).

subject: Biology
stem: Blood pressure is highest in the
options: veins|capillaries|arteries|lymph vessels
answer: arteries
rubric: Blood is pumped at high pressure into arteries from the heart; pressure decreases through capillaries and veins.

subject: Biology
stem: The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the
options: heart to the liver|small intestine to the liver|liver to the heart|lungs to the heart
answer: small intestine to the liver
rubric: The hepatic portal vein transports nutrient-rich blood from the gut to the liver for processing.

subject: Biology
stem: The condition known as anaemia is caused by a deficiency of
options: haemoglobin or red blood cells|white blood cells|platelets|plasma proteins
answer: haemoglobin or red blood cells
rubric: Anaemia results from reduced oxygen-carrying capacity due to insufficient Hb or too few RBCs (iron deficiency is common cause).

subject: Biology
stem: Capillaries are important in exchange because
options: they have thick walls|they have walls only one cell thick (thin) and large combined surface area|they carry blood at high pressure|they are the largest vessels
answer: they have walls only one cell thick (thin) and large combined surface area
rubric: Capillary walls are one cell thick, facilitating diffusion of O₂, nutrients, CO₂ and waste between blood and tissue fluid.

subject: Biology
stem: Transpiration rate increases when
options: humidity is high and temperature is low|wind speed decreases|light intensity, temperature and wind increase while humidity drops|it is raining
answer: light intensity, temperature and wind increase while humidity drops
rubric: Light opens stomata; higher temperature and wind increase evaporation rate; low humidity maintains the diffusion gradient.

subject: Biology
stem: The lymphatic system returns excess tissue fluid to the
options: liver|kidneys|blood circulation (via lymph ducts)|lungs
answer: blood circulation (via lymph ducts)
rubric: Lymph is collected from tissues and returned to the bloodstream via the thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct.

subject: Biology
stem: The blood type (ABO) is determined by
options: the protein in haemoglobin|antigens on the surface of red blood cells|the number of white blood cells|the plasma protein concentration
answer: antigens on the surface of red blood cells
rubric: ABO blood groups are determined by the presence or absence of A and B antigens on the RBC surface.

subject: Biology
stem: The vena cava carries blood from the
options: heart to the lungs|body back to the right atrium|left ventricle to the aorta|liver to the kidneys
answer: body back to the right atrium
rubric: The superior and inferior venae cavae return deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium.

subject: Biology
stem: The overall equation for aerobic respiration is
options: C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O|C₆H₁₂O₆ → C₂H₅OH + CO₂|6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂|CO₂ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂
answer: C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O
rubric: Aerobic respiration: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ~38 ATP.

subject: Biology
stem: The main site of aerobic respiration in cells is the
options: nucleus|ribosome|mitochondrion|cell membrane
answer: mitochondrion
rubric: The Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation occur in the mitochondria; glycolysis is in the cytoplasm.

subject: Biology
stem: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
options: lactic acid|ethanol and carbon dioxide|water and carbon dioxide|acetic acid
answer: ethanol and carbon dioxide
rubric: Yeast fermentation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. This is exploited in brewing and baking.

subject: Biology
stem: Anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells during intense exercise produces
options: ethanol|lactic acid|carbon dioxide|oxygen
answer: lactic acid
rubric: In oxygen debt: glucose → lactic acid (no CO₂ produced). Lactic acid accumulates causing muscle fatigue.

subject: Biology
stem: Glycolysis takes place in the
options: mitochondrial matrix|nucleus|cytoplasm|endoplasmic reticulum
answer: cytoplasm
rubric: Glycolysis (first stage of respiration) converts glucose to pyruvate in the cytoplasm, producing 2 net ATP.

subject: Biology
stem: The net ATP yield from one molecule of glucose in aerobic respiration is approximately
rubric: Aerobic respiration produces ~38 ATP per glucose (2 from glycolysis + 2 from Krebs + 34 from oxidative phosphorylation).

subject: Biology
stem: During the Krebs cycle, the carbon skeleton of pyruvate is broken down to produce
options: glucose|NADH, FADH₂ and CO₂|oxygen|glycerol
answer: NADH, FADH₂ and CO₂
rubric: The Krebs cycle oxidises acetyl-CoA, producing reduced coenzymes (NADH, FADH₂) and CO₂.

subject: Biology
stem: Which gas is used in aerobic respiration and which is produced?
options: CO₂ used; O₂ produced|O₂ used; CO₂ produced|H₂O used; O₂ produced|N₂ used; CO₂ produced
answer: O₂ used; CO₂ produced
rubric: Aerobic respiration uses O₂ as the final electron acceptor and produces CO₂ as a waste product.

subject: Biology
stem: The respiratory quotient (RQ) for carbohydrate is
rubric: RQ = CO₂ produced / O₂ consumed. For glucose: 6CO₂ / 6O₂ = 1.0.

subject: Biology
stem: The enzyme ATP synthase catalyses the production of ATP from
options: NADH|ADP and inorganic phosphate|glucose|pyruvate
answer: ADP and inorganic phosphate
rubric: ATP synthase uses the proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane to phosphorylate ADP + Pi → ATP.

subject: Biology
stem: Limewater turns milky when
options: breathed on due to water vapour|CO₂ passes through it (forming CaCO₃)|O₂ passes through it|H₂S passes through it
answer: CO₂ passes through it (forming CaCO₃)
rubric: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ (white precipitate) + H₂O. Limewater is the standard test for CO₂.

subject: Biology
stem: The process of breathing (ventilation) moves air into and out of the lungs by changes in
options: blood pressure only|chest volume and pressure|diaphragm muscle only|lung surface tension only
answer: chest volume and pressure
rubric: Inspiration: diaphragm contracts + ribs rise → volume ↑ → pressure ↓ → air flows in. Reverse for expiration.

subject: Biology
stem: The organ that takes carbon dioxide from the blood and removes it from the body is the
options: kidney|liver|lungs|skin
answer: lungs
rubric: In the lungs, CO₂ diffuses from blood into the alveoli along a concentration gradient and is exhaled.

subject: Biology
stem: Haemoglobin releases oxygen to tissues because
options: oxygen concentration in tissues is higher than in blood|tissues are cooler|oxygen concentration in tissues is lower than in blood|haemoglobin breaks down in tissues
answer: oxygen concentration in tissues is lower than in blood
rubric: Oxygen partial pressure is lower in respiring tissues; Hb releases O₂ (Bohr effect/dissociation at low pO₂).

subject: Biology
stem: Fermentation in baking uses yeast to produce
options: oxygen|CO₂ to make bread rise|lactic acid|starch
answer: CO₂ to make bread rise
rubric: Yeast ferments glucose → ethanol + CO₂; CO₂ bubbles make the dough rise. The ethanol evaporates during baking.

subject: Biology
stem: The stage of aerobic respiration that produces the most ATP is
options: glycolysis|Krebs cycle|oxidative phosphorylation (electron transport chain)|fermentation
answer: oxidative phosphorylation (electron transport chain)
rubric: The electron transport chain + chemiosmosis (oxidative phosphorylation) produces ~34 ATP per glucose.

subject: Biology
stem: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle that
options: digests food|pumps blood|aids ventilation of the lungs|filters blood
answer: aids ventilation of the lungs
rubric: The diaphragm contracts (flattens) during inspiration to increase thoracic volume, drawing air into the lungs.

subject: Biology
stem: Gaseous exchange in the alveoli relies on
options: active transport of gases|diffusion across moist, thin alveolar walls|osmosis|breathing muscles
answer: diffusion across moist, thin alveolar walls
rubric: O₂ and CO₂ exchange by diffusion across the one-cell-thick alveolar epithelium; moist surfaces aid dissolution of gases.

subject: Biology
stem: Oxygen debt after vigorous exercise is repaid by
options: eating more glucose|breathing faster to oxidise accumulated lactic acid back to glucose or CO₂|drinking water|resting without breathing
answer: breathing faster to oxidise accumulated lactic acid back to glucose or CO₂
rubric: Post-exercise, extra O₂ consumption oxidises lactic acid: much is converted to glucose in the liver; some is oxidised fully.

subject: Biology
stem: The substrate that is primarily used in respiration during normal activity is
options: fats|proteins|carbohydrates (glucose)|nucleic acids
answer: carbohydrates (glucose)
rubric: Glucose is the primary respiratory substrate; fats and proteins are used when carbohydrates are depleted.

subject: Biology
stem: Excretion is defined as
options: the removal of undigested food (egestion)|the removal of metabolic waste products from the body|the intake of food|the breakdown of glucose
answer: the removal of metabolic waste products from the body
rubric: Excretion: elimination of waste products of metabolism (not egestion, which removes undigested material).

subject: Biology
stem: The main excretory organ in mammals is the
options: skin|liver|lung|kidney
answer: kidney
rubric: Kidneys excrete urea (from amino acid catabolism), excess salts and water in urine.

subject: Biology
stem: Urea is produced in the liver by the
options: oxidation of glucose|deamination of excess amino acids|hydrolysis of fats|reduction of CO₂
answer: deamination of excess amino acids
rubric: Excess amino acids are deaminated in the liver: the amino group (−NH₂) forms ammonia → urea (ornithine cycle).

subject: Biology
stem: The functional unit of the kidney is called the
options: glomerulus|nephron|Bowman capsule|ureter
answer: nephron
rubric: Each kidney contains ~1 million nephrons; each nephron filters blood, reabsorbs useful substances, and produces urine.

subject: Biology
stem: The process of removing useful substances from the filtrate back into the blood is called
options: filtration|secretion|selective reabsorption|excretion
answer: selective reabsorption
rubric: Selective reabsorption in the proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle and DCT recovers glucose, amino acids, water and salts.

subject: Biology
stem: Which gas is a waste product of respiration excreted by the lungs?
options: Oxygen|Nitrogen|Carbon dioxide|Argon
answer: Carbon dioxide
rubric: CO₂ produced in cellular respiration diffuses into the blood and is excreted via the lungs during exhalation.

subject: Biology
stem: Osmoregulation refers to
options: the regulation of body temperature|the control of the water and salt balance of the body|the digestion of food|the removal of CO₂
answer: the control of the water and salt balance of the body
rubric: Osmoregulation maintains the osmotic pressure of body fluids; the kidneys are the primary osmoregulatory organ.

subject: Biology
stem: Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) acts on the kidney to
options: increase urine volume|decrease water reabsorption|increase water reabsorption from the collecting duct|increase salt excretion
answer: increase water reabsorption from the collecting duct
rubric: ADH (vasopressin) increases the permeability of the collecting duct and DCT to water, reducing urine volume.

subject: Biology
stem: Bile pigments (bilirubin) are waste products of the breakdown of
options: excess amino acids|old red blood cells|glucose|fatty acids
answer: old red blood cells
rubric: Haemoglobin from worn-out RBCs is broken down in the liver; the haem group is converted to bilirubin, excreted in bile.

subject: Biology
stem: In plants, excess carbon dioxide and oxygen from photosynthesis/respiration are removed by diffusion through
options: roots|bark fissures|stomata and lenticels|flowers
answer: stomata and lenticels
rubric: Gaseous exchange (O₂, CO₂) in plants occurs through stomata in leaves and lenticels in stems.

subject: Biology
stem: The Malpighian tubules of insects serve the function of
options: digestion|excretion (removing nitrogenous waste as uric acid)|blood circulation|gas exchange
answer: excretion (removing nitrogenous waste as uric acid)
rubric: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects, removing nitrogenous waste as insoluble uric acid (conserves water).

subject: Biology
stem: Dialysis mimics the function of the kidney by removing waste from blood using the principle of
options: osmosis only|active transport|diffusion across a semipermeable membrane|filtration under pressure
answer: diffusion across a semipermeable membrane
rubric: In haemodialysis, blood is passed against a dialysis fluid across a semipermeable membrane; waste diffuses out.

subject: Biology
stem: The glomerulus is a network of capillaries where
options: selective reabsorption occurs|urine is stored|ultrafiltration of blood occurs|ADH is released
answer: ultrafiltration of blood occurs
rubric: The glomerulus (in Bowman capsule) is the site of ultrafiltration: blood pressure forces small molecules into the filtrate.

subject: Biology
stem: Which substance is NOT normally present in urine?
options: Urea|Uric acid|Glucose|Water
answer: Glucose
rubric: Glucose is normally fully reabsorbed by the kidneys; its presence in urine (glucosuria) indicates diabetes mellitus.

subject: Biology
stem: Excretion by sweat glands in the skin removes
options: only heat|urea, salts and water|CO₂|only water
answer: urea, salts and water
rubric: Sweat contains small amounts of urea, sodium chloride and water — it has minor excretory function (mainly thermoregulation).

subject: Biology
stem: Sexual reproduction involves
options: the fusion of one gamete|no gametes|the fusion of two gametes (fertilisation)|asexual budding
answer: the fusion of two gametes (fertilisation)
rubric: Sexual reproduction requires fertilisation: the fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote.

subject: Biology
stem: In flowering plants, the male gametes are contained in the
options: ovule|carpel|pollen grain|sepal
answer: pollen grain
rubric: Pollen grains carry the male gametophyte (and male gametes/sperm nuclei) of flowering plants.

subject: Biology
stem: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from
options: the ovule to the stigma|the anther to the stigma|the stamen to the carpel|the petal to the sepal
answer: the anther to the stigma
rubric: Pollination: pollen grains are transferred from the anther (male) to the stigma (female) by wind, insects or water.

subject: Biology
stem: After fertilisation in plants, the ovule develops into the
options: fruit|seed|flower|petal
answer: seed
rubric: The fertilised ovule (with zygote inside) develops into a seed containing the embryo.

subject: Biology
stem: The placenta in mammals serves to
options: filter urine|exchange nutrients and gases between mother and foetus|produce hormones for digestion|remove CO₂ from the mother
answer: exchange nutrients and gases between mother and foetus
rubric: The placenta allows diffusion of O₂, nutrients and antibodies from mother to foetus, and CO₂ and waste in return.

subject: Biology
stem: Asexual reproduction produces offspring that are genetically
options: identical to the parent|different from each parent|a mix of two parents|completely different from all parents
answer: identical to the parent
rubric: Asexual reproduction (mitosis, budding, binary fission) produces genetically identical clones.

subject: Biology
stem: The menstrual cycle in humans is approximately how long?
options: 7 days|14 days|28 days|56 days
answer: 28 days
rubric: The average human menstrual cycle is ~28 days, regulated by FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone.

subject: Biology
stem: Fertilisation in humans normally occurs in the
options: uterus|vagina|fallopian tube (oviduct)|ovary
answer: fallopian tube (oviduct)
rubric: The sperm meets the egg in the fallopian tube; the resulting zygote travels to the uterus for implantation.

subject: Biology
stem: The hormone responsible for the development of secondary sexual characteristics in males is
options: oestrogen|progesterone|testosterone|FSH
answer: testosterone
rubric: Testosterone (produced by Leydig cells in testes) drives male secondary sexual development at puberty.

subject: Biology
stem: Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction in plants that uses
options: seeds|pollen|bulbs, cuttings, runners, tubers|flowers
answer: bulbs, cuttings, runners, tubers
rubric: Vegetative propagation uses non-reproductive parts (bulbs, rhizomes, cuttings, grafts) to produce genetically identical plants.

subject: Biology
stem: Seed dispersal is important for plants because it
options: increases pollination|prevents competition between parent and offspring and colonises new areas|reduces genetic diversity|helps fertilisation
answer: prevents competition between parent and offspring and colonises new areas
rubric: Wide dispersal reduces intraspecific competition and allows plants to colonise new habitats.

subject: Biology
stem: The process by which the embryo attaches to the uterine lining is called
options: ovulation|gestation|implantation|menstruation
answer: implantation
rubric: After fertilisation, the blastocyst travels to the uterus and implants into the endometrium (~6–10 days post-fertilisation).

subject: Biology
stem: In insects with complete metamorphosis, the stages are
options: egg → larva → pupa → adult|egg → nymph → adult|egg → adult|larva → egg → adult
answer: egg → larva → pupa → adult
rubric: Complete metamorphosis (holometabolism) has four stages: egg → larva → pupa → adult.

subject: Biology
stem: Cross-pollination (compared to self-pollination) leads to
options: less genetic variation|no seeds|greater genetic variation in the offspring|identical offspring
answer: greater genetic variation in the offspring
rubric: Cross-pollination introduces pollen from a different individual, leading to new genetic combinations — greater variation.

subject: Biology
stem: The male gametes in humans are produced in the
options: ovary|testes|prostate|epididymis
answer: testes
rubric: Spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes, producing sperm.

subject: Biology
stem: Wind-pollinated flowers are adapted by having
options: large, brightly coloured petals|light pollen and feathery stigmas|nectar for insects|sticky pollen
answer: light, feathery stigmas and light pollen
rubric: Wind-pollinated flowers have small/no petals, produce abundant light pollen, and have large feathery stigmas to catch pollen.

subject: Biology
stem: The outer seed coat (testa) functions to
options: provide nutrients to the embryo|protect the seed and prevent water loss|carry out photosynthesis|attract animals for dispersal
answer: protect the seed and prevent water loss
rubric: The hard testa protects the embryo from physical damage, desiccation, and pathogens.

subject: Biology
stem: In binary fission (e.g. Amoeba), one cell divides into
options: two unequal cells|four cells|two genetically identical cells|eight cells
answer: two genetically identical cells
rubric: Binary fission: one parent cell divides into two equal, genetically identical daughter cells (asexual reproduction).

subject: Biology
stem: Ovulation in the human female is triggered by a surge in
options: FSH|progesterone|LH (luteinising hormone)|oestrogen only
answer: LH (luteinising hormone)
rubric: A mid-cycle LH surge triggers release of the secondary oocyte from the Graafian follicle (ovulation ~day 14).

subject: Biology
stem: Hydrophily refers to pollination by
options: wind|insects|water|birds
answer: water
rubric: Hydrophily is pollination by water currents, seen in aquatic plants like Vallisneria.

subject: Biology
stem: Identical (monozygotic) twins arise from
options: two separate eggs fertilised by two sperm|a single fertilised egg that splits into two embryos|two eggs fertilised by the same sperm|asexual reproduction
answer: a single fertilised egg that splits into two embryos
rubric: Identical twins form when a single zygote splits into two embryos after fertilisation — genetically identical.

subject: Biology
stem: The function of the cotyledons in a seed is to
options: anchor the seed|carry out photosynthesis|store food for the germinating embryo|attract pollinators
answer: store food for the germinating embryo
rubric: Cotyledons (seed leaves) store nutrients (starch, proteins, fats) that fuel the seedling before it can photosynthesize.

subject: Biology
stem: The structure in the female reproductive system that produces eggs is the
options: uterus|fallopian tube|ovary|cervix
answer: ovary
rubric: Oogenesis (egg production) occurs in the ovaries; mature eggs are released at ovulation.

subject: Biology
stem: Parthenogenesis is a form of reproduction in which
options: fertilisation occurs without sperm|sperm fertilises an egg normally|an unfertilised egg develops into a new individual|a plant reproduces from a cutting
answer: an unfertilised egg develops into a new individual
rubric: Parthenogenesis: development of an unfertilised egg. Seen in bees (drones), aphids and some reptiles.

subject: Biology
stem: The gestation period in humans is approximately
options: 3 months|9 months|12 months|6 months
answer: 9 months
rubric: Human gestation is approximately 40 weeks (9 months) from last menstrual period to birth.

subject: Biology
stem: The unit of inheritance responsible for transmitting traits from parent to offspring is the
options: chromosome|ribosome|mitochondrion|gene
answer: gene
rubric: A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a specific protein and determines a heritable trait.

subject: Biology
stem: In Mendel's first law (Law of Segregation), alleles separate during
options: fertilisation|mitosis|meiosis (gamete formation)|DNA replication
answer: meiosis (gamete formation)
rubric: Alleles segregate (separate) into different gametes during meiosis I; each gamete carries only one allele.

subject: Biology
stem: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (Aa × Aa), the expected phenotypic ratio is
rubric: Aa × Aa → 1AA : 2Aa : 1aa → 3 dominant : 1 recessive phenotype = 3:1.

subject: Biology
stem: The physical appearance of an organism resulting from its genetic makeup is its
options: genotype|phenotype|allele|locus
answer: phenotype
rubric: Phenotype is the observable trait (appearance, physiology); genotype is the genetic composition.

subject: Biology
stem: An organism that has two identical alleles for a trait (e.g. AA or aa) is described as
options: heterozygous|homozygous|dominant|recessive
answer: homozygous
rubric: Homozygous: both alleles at a locus are the same. Heterozygous: two different alleles (e.g. Aa).

subject: Biology
stem: Sickle cell anaemia is an example of
options: an X-linked recessive disorder|an autosomal recessive disorder|an autosomal dominant disorder|a chromosomal disorder
answer: an autosomal recessive disorder
rubric: Sickle cell anaemia (HbS/HbS) is caused by a recessive allele on chromosome 11; both copies must be defective.

subject: Biology
stem: The expected genotypic ratio from a cross Tt × Tt is
options: 1TT:1tt|1TT:2Tt:1tt|3Tt:1tt|2TT:1tt
answer: 1TT:2Tt:1tt
rubric: Tt × Tt produces: 1/4 TT, 2/4 Tt, 1/4 tt → genotypic ratio 1:2:1.

subject: Biology
stem: Which of the following is correct about sex determination in humans?
options: Females are XY; males are XX|Females are XX; males are XY|Both sexes are XY|Sex is determined by the egg only
answer: Females are XX; males are XY
rubric: Human sex: females have two X chromosomes (XX); males have one X and one Y chromosome (XY).

subject: Biology
stem: Colour blindness in humans is an X-linked recessive trait. A colour-blind man (X^c Y) × normal carrier woman (X^C X^c) will give offspring in what ratio?
options: All normal sons|1 normal female:1 carrier female:1 normal male:1 colour-blind male|All colour-blind|1 normal:3 colour-blind
answer: 1 normal female:1 carrier female:1 normal male:1 colour-blind male
rubric: X^C X^c × X^c Y → X^C X^c (carrier female), X^c X^c (colour-blind female), X^C Y (normal male), X^c Y (colour-blind male).

subject: Biology
stem: In incomplete dominance, the heterozygous phenotype is
options: identical to the dominant parent|intermediate between the two homozygous phenotypes|identical to the recessive parent|absent
answer: intermediate between the two homozygous phenotypes
rubric: In incomplete dominance (e.g. red × white snapdragons → pink), the F1 heterozygote shows a blended intermediate phenotype.

subject: Biology
stem: A mutation is
options: a change in phenotype only|a permanent heritable change in the DNA sequence|a change in protein function only|the death of a gene
answer: a permanent heritable change in the DNA sequence
rubric: Mutations are changes in nucleotide sequence of DNA; they may be substitutions, insertions or deletions.

subject: Biology
stem: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) results from
options: a gene mutation|deletion of chromosome 21|having three copies of chromosome 21|a sex-linked defect
answer: having three copies of chromosome 21
rubric: Down syndrome is caused by non-disjunction during meiosis resulting in three chromosome 21s (2n+1=47).

subject: Biology
stem: Mendel's second law (Law of Independent Assortment) states that
options: alleles always stay together|genes on the same chromosome always assort independently|alleles of different genes assort independently of each other during gamete formation|all offspring resemble the mother
answer: alleles of different genes assort independently of each other during gamete formation
rubric: Independent assortment applies to genes on different (non-homologous) chromosomes; they segregate independently during meiosis I.

subject: Biology
stem: The dihybrid cross AaBb × AaBb produces the phenotypic ratio
rubric: For two independently assorting genes, AaBb × AaBb gives the classic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio.

subject: Biology
stem: Codominance occurs when
options: one allele masks the other|both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote|the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype|one allele is lethal
answer: both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote
rubric: In codominance (e.g. AB blood group, roan coat), both alleles contribute equally to the phenotype.

subject: Biology
stem: The ABO blood group system has how many alleles?
rubric: ABO has three alleles: I^A, I^B (codominant) and i (recessive). Three alleles, but only two can be present in an individual.

subject: Biology
stem: A test cross (back cross) involves crossing a dominant phenotype individual with a
options: homozygous dominant individual|heterozygous individual|recessive homozygous individual|any random individual
answer: recessive homozygous individual
rubric: A test cross uses a homozygous recessive individual to determine whether the dominant phenotype individual is AA or Aa.

subject: Biology
stem: Haemophilia is caused by a deficiency in
options: red blood cells|clotting factor VIII or IX (X-linked recessive)|bone marrow|white blood cells
answer: clotting factor VIII or IX (X-linked recessive)
rubric: Haemophilia A (factor VIII) and B (factor IX) are X-linked recessive bleeding disorders, more common in males.

subject: Biology
stem: An organism is said to be a carrier of a recessive allele when
options: it expresses the recessive trait|it is homozygous dominant|it is heterozygous and does not express the trait|it has two recessive alleles
answer: it is heterozygous and does not express the trait
rubric: A carrier has one copy of a recessive allele (Aa) but shows the dominant phenotype; they can pass the allele to offspring.

subject: Biology
stem: Crossing over during meiosis I results in
options: chromosome duplication|genetic recombination (new combinations of alleles)|doubling of chromosome number|cell death
answer: genetic recombination (new combinations of alleles)
rubric: Crossing over between non-sister chromatids shuffles alleles, generating new combinations and increasing genetic diversity.

subject: Biology
stem: The law that states "like begets like" is violated by the occurrence of
options: mitosis|mutations|meiosis without crossing over|replication
answer: mutations
rubric: Mutations create heritable variation that breaks the rule that offspring exactly resemble parents.

subject: Biology
stem: In plants, the genotype TT (tall) crossed with tt (dwarf) gives all Tt offspring. This illustrates
options: incomplete dominance|codominance|complete dominance|multiple allelism
answer: complete dominance
rubric: All F1 offspring are Tt and show the tall phenotype — T is completely dominant over t.

subject: Biology
stem: Polygenic inheritance refers to traits controlled by
options: one gene with multiple alleles|several genes each contributing to the phenotype|mitochondrial genes only|X-linked genes only
answer: several genes each contributing to the phenotype
rubric: Polygenic traits (height, skin colour, intelligence) are influenced by two or more genes whose effects are cumulative.

subject: Biology
stem: If a man is heterozygous for blood group A (I^A i) and a woman is heterozygous for blood group B (I^B i), the probability of their child having blood group O is

subject: Biology
stem: Linkage in genetics means that
options: two genes are on different chromosomes|two genes on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together|crossing over does not occur|all genes are dominant
answer: two genes on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together
rubric: Linked genes are on the same chromosome (autosome or sex chromosome) and tend to be inherited together unless crossing over separates them.

subject: Biology
stem: An ecosystem includes
options: only living organisms|only non-living factors|all living organisms and their non-living environment interacting together|plants only
answer: all living organisms and their non-living environment interacting together
rubric: An ecosystem is the community of organisms (biotic) plus the physical environment (abiotic) in a defined area.

subject: Biology
stem: Producers in a food chain are organisms that
options: feed on other animals|decompose dead matter|synthesise their own food by photosynthesis|feed on producers
answer: synthesise their own food by photosynthesis
rubric: Producers (green plants, algae, phytoplankton) are autotrophs that convert solar energy into organic matter.

subject: Biology
stem: A food chain shows
options: where energy is stored|how energy and nutrients are transferred from one trophic level to the next|how animals reproduce|how plants use sunlight
answer: how energy and nutrients are transferred from one trophic level to the next
rubric: A food chain: producer → primary consumer → secondary consumer → tertiary consumer — each step transfers energy.

subject: Biology
stem: The term "niche" refers to an organism's
options: physical location in the ecosystem|role and position in the ecosystem (including food, interactions, behaviour)|total biomass|preferred temperature range
answer: role and position in the ecosystem (including food, interactions, behaviour)
rubric: An ecological niche is the functional role an organism plays — what it eats, how it lives, what it competes with.

subject: Biology
stem: Decomposers are important in ecosystems because they
options: produce oxygen|recycle nutrients back into the soil by breaking down dead organic matter|compete with producers|make glucose
answer: recycle nutrients back into the soil by breaking down dead organic matter
rubric: Decomposers (fungi, bacteria) mineralise organic matter, releasing nutrients (N, P, K) back into the soil for plant uptake.

subject: Biology
stem: Energy flow in an ecosystem is
options: cyclic (energy returns to the sun)|unidirectional (one-way, from sun through trophic levels)|random|equal at all trophic levels
answer: unidirectional (one-way, from sun through trophic levels)
rubric: Energy flows in one direction: sun → producers → consumers → decomposers. It cannot be recycled; only nutrients cycle.

subject: Biology
stem: The approximately 10% rule in ecology states that
options: 10% of organisms survive in each ecosystem|only 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level|10% of species are decomposers|all ecosystems lose 10% of water each year
answer: only 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level
rubric: Only ~10% of energy at one trophic level is available to the next; ~90% is lost as heat, excretion and respiration.

subject: Biology
stem: Interspecific competition occurs between
options: individuals of the same species|individuals of different species|predator and prey only|plants only
answer: individuals of different species
rubric: Interspecific competition: two or more different species compete for the same resource (food, space, water).

subject: Biology
stem: The total number of individuals of the same species occupying a defined area at a given time is the
options: community|ecosystem|population|biome
answer: population
rubric: A population is all the individuals of one species in a defined area. Community = all species together.

subject: Biology
stem: Mutualism is a type of symbiosis in which
options: one organism benefits and the other is harmed|one organism benefits and the other is unaffected|both organisms benefit|both organisms are harmed
answer: both organisms benefit
rubric: Mutualism: both partners benefit. E.g. legume roots + Rhizobium bacteria (plants get N; bacteria get C).

subject: Biology
stem: Parasitism is a relationship in which
options: both organisms benefit|the parasite benefits at the expense of the host|neither organism benefits|both organisms are harmed equally
answer: the parasite benefits at the expense of the host
rubric: In parasitism the parasite gains (nutrients, shelter) while the host is harmed, though usually not killed immediately.

subject: Biology
stem: Eutrophication of water bodies is caused by
options: excess carbon dioxide|excess nutrients (nitrates and phosphates) causing algal blooms and oxygen depletion|predator reduction|acid rain only
answer: excess nutrients (nitrates and phosphates) causing algal blooms and oxygen depletion
rubric: Nutrient run-off fertilises algae → blooms → die → bacteria decompose them → O₂ depleted → aquatic organisms die.

subject: Biology
stem: The nitrogen cycle includes processes such as
