options: a charge to the profit and loss account|a reduction in the net book value of the asset|an actual cash outflow|a credit to accumulated depreciation
answer: an actual cash outflow
rubric: Depreciation is a non-cash expense: it reduces profit and asset value but involves no cash payment in the period charged.

subject: Accounting
stem: A partnership is a business owned by
options: one person only|two or more persons (maximum 20 in Nigeria for general partnerships) who share profits and losses|the government|shareholders via share capital
answer: two or more persons (maximum 20 in Nigeria for general partnerships) who share profits and losses
rubric: Partnership: minimum 2, maximum 20 partners (for business; some professions may differ); they share profits per agreement.

subject: Accounting
stem: In the absence of a partnership agreement, profits and losses are shared
options: in proportion to capital contributed|equally among partners|in proportion to work done|according to seniority
answer: equally among partners
rubric: Without a deed, the Partnership Act applies: profits/losses shared equally regardless of capital contribution.

subject: Accounting
stem: A partnership appropriation account shows
options: the calculation of gross profit|how net profit is divided among partners (interest on capital, salaries, profit share)|the balance sheet total|cash flow
answer: how net profit is divided among partners (interest on capital, salaries, profit share)
rubric: Appropriation account: starts with net profit, deducts partner salaries and interest on capital, then shares residue in profit ratio.

subject: Accounting
stem: Interest on capital is allowed to partners to
options: reward them for long service|compensate partners who contributed more capital for the opportunity cost of their investment|reduce tax|increase drawings
answer: compensate partners who contributed more capital for the opportunity cost of their investment
rubric: Interest on capital (at agreed rate) rewards larger capital contributions before sharing residual profits equally.

subject: Accounting
stem: Interest on drawings is charged to partners to
options: reward them|discourage partners from withdrawing excess funds from the business|cover bank charges|pay employees
answer: discourage partners from withdrawing excess funds from the business
rubric: Interest on drawings reduces the partner's share; it is an income to the partnership, discouraging large early withdrawals.

subject: Accounting
stem: A partner's current account records
options: their capital invested|day-to-day movements: share of profit, salary, interest on capital (credit) versus drawings and interest on drawings (debit)|only cash|only loans
answer: day-to-day movements: share of profit, salary, interest on capital (credit) versus drawings and interest on drawings (debit)
rubric: Current account: fluctuates each year. Capital account: fixed (original investment). Current account = profit entitlements minus drawings.

subject: Accounting
stem: A partner's capital account is kept fixed (constant) when
options: all movements go through the capital account|the fluctuating current account method is used — routine items go to current account; capital account shows only the original investment|both accounts are merged|there is only one partner
answer: the fluctuating current account method is used — routine items go to current account; capital account shows only the original investment
rubric: Under the fixed capital account method, only permanent changes (additional capital, agreed capital reductions) affect the capital account.

subject: Accounting
stem: The admission of a new partner may require an existing goodwill to be revalued; the journal entry to create (raise) goodwill is
options: Dr Capital accounts (old ratio); Cr Goodwill|Dr Goodwill; Cr Capital accounts (old profit-sharing ratio)|Dr Cash; Cr Goodwill|Dr Goodwill; Cr Cash
answer: Dr Goodwill; Cr Capital accounts (old profit-sharing ratio)
rubric: Raising goodwill: Dr Goodwill (asset); Cr Capital accounts of existing partners in old profit-sharing ratio.

subject: Accounting
stem: After admitting a new partner, if goodwill is to be written off (not maintained in the accounts), the entry is
options: Dr Goodwill; Cr Capital|Dr Capital accounts (new ratio); Cr Goodwill|Dr Cash; Cr Capital|Dr Goodwill; Cr Cash
answer: Dr Capital accounts (new ratio); Cr Goodwill
rubric: Write off goodwill: Dr Capital accounts of ALL partners (new ratio); Cr Goodwill — reduces each partner's capital.

subject: Accounting
stem: On dissolution (winding up) of a partnership, a realisation account is prepared to record
options: daily sales|the proceeds and costs of selling assets and settling liabilities, leading to a profit or loss on realisation|employee wages only|tax due
answer: the proceeds and costs of selling assets and settling liabilities, leading to a profit or loss on realisation
rubric: Realisation account: Dr assets (at book value); Cr proceeds received; the balance = profit or loss on realisation, shared in profit ratio.

subject: Accounting
stem: A partner's loan to the firm at dissolution is repaid
options: before outside creditors|after outside creditors but before repaying capital to partners|after capital|at the same time as capital
answer: after outside creditors but before repaying capital to partners
rubric: Priority on dissolution: outside creditors first, then partner loans, then capital repayment to partners.

subject: Accounting
stem: Goodwill in a partnership is valued when
options: any routine transaction occurs|a partner joins, retires or dies, and the business is revalued at a different amount|the bank requires it|tax is calculated
answer: a partner joins, retires or dies, and the business is revalued at a different amount
rubric: Goodwill arises on changes in partnership composition; it compensates existing partners for the reputation they built.

subject: Accounting
stem: The profit-sharing ratio determines
options: how capital is contributed|in what proportion partners share residual profits/losses after other appropriations|interest on capital only|salary paid
answer: in what proportion partners share residual profits/losses after other appropriations
rubric: The profit-sharing ratio (PSR) governs allocation of residual (net) profit after interest on capital, salaries and interest on drawings.

subject: Accounting
stem: Partners A and B share profits 3:2. Net profit is N500,000 after salaries and interest on capital. A's share is
rubric: 3:2 ratio means A gets 3/5 and B gets 2/5. A = 3/5 x N500,000 = N300,000.

subject: Accounting
stem: When a partner retires, any goodwill created is shared among
options: all partners in the new ratio|old partners in old profit-sharing ratio; retiring partner's share compensates their goodwill entitlement|only the retiring partner|only the remaining partners equally
answer: old partners in old profit-sharing ratio; retiring partner's share compensates their goodwill entitlement
rubric: Retiring partner receives their share of goodwill as compensation; remaining partners adjust for the new ratio.

subject: Accounting
stem: Interest on capital is treated in the partnership appropriation account as
options: a revenue income|a deduction from net profit before sharing in the profit ratio|an addition to net profit|a direct capital increase
answer: a deduction from net profit before sharing in the profit ratio
rubric: Interest on capital reduces the profit available for sharing: it is deducted from net profit in the appropriation account.

subject: Accounting
stem: The net profit to be appropriated in the partnership appropriation account is the profit
options: before interest on capital and salaries|after interest on capital and salaries|after all appropriations|after taxation only
answer: before interest on capital and salaries
rubric: Appropriation starts with net profit from P&L, then deducts partner salaries and interest on capital to find residual profit.

subject: Accounting
stem: A partnership deed (agreement) typically contains
options: a list of customers|details of capital, profit-sharing ratio, salaries, interest rates on capital and drawings, procedures for admission/retirement|tax rates|employee contracts
answer: details of capital, profit-sharing ratio, salaries, interest rates on capital and drawings, procedures for admission/retirement
rubric: The partnership deed is the governing document: it prevents disputes by specifying all financial arrangements.

subject: Accounting
stem: A debit balance on a partner's current account means
options: the partner is owed money by the firm|the partner has withdrawn more than their entitlement and effectively owes the firm money|the partner has not drawn anything|the firm is profitable
answer: the partner has withdrawn more than their entitlement and effectively owes the firm money
rubric: A debit balance on a current account = the partner has over-drawn; they effectively owe the partnership the excess.

subject: Accounting
stem: Revaluation of assets at admission of a new partner results in gains/losses credited or debited to existing partners' accounts in their
options: new profit-sharing ratio|old profit-sharing ratio|equal shares always|the new partner's capital account
answer: old profit-sharing ratio
rubric: Revaluation gains/losses affect those who owned the assets before the change — existing partners in their OLD ratio.

subject: Accounting
stem: A limited company is distinguished from a partnership in that
options: it has unlimited liability|its shareholders have limited liability — they can lose only what they invested|it has fewer than 20 members|it is run by the government
answer: its shareholders have limited liability — they can lose only what they invested
rubric: Limited liability: shareholders risk only their investment; personal assets are protected from the company's debts.

subject: Accounting
stem: Authorised share capital is
options: the capital actually issued to shareholders|the maximum share capital the company is permitted to issue under its memorandum|capital borrowed from a bank|total assets of the company
answer: the maximum share capital the company is permitted to issue under its memorandum
rubric: Authorised capital is the legal ceiling on shares that can be issued; issued capital is the amount actually allotted.

subject: Accounting
stem: Ordinary shares (equity shares) carry
options: a fixed rate of dividend|variable dividends and voting rights, entitling holders to residual profit after preference shareholders|no voting rights|guaranteed dividends
answer: variable dividends and voting rights, entitling holders to residual profit after preference shareholders
rubric: Ordinary shareholders are the residual owners: they vote at AGMs and receive dividends only after preference holders.

subject: Accounting
stem: Preference shares carry
options: variable dividends|a fixed rate of dividend, paid before ordinary dividends, with limited or no voting rights|majority voting rights|the same rights as ordinary shares always
answer: a fixed rate of dividend, paid before ordinary dividends, with limited or no voting rights
rubric: Preference shares: fixed dividend (e.g. 10% of par value), paid before ordinary; often non-voting or limited voting.

subject: Accounting
stem: A debenture is a
options: type of share|long-term loan issued by a company, carrying a fixed interest rate, secured or unsecured|government bond only|current liability always
answer: long-term loan issued by a company, carrying a fixed interest rate, secured or unsecured
rubric: Debentures (loan notes) are debt instruments; holders are creditors, not owners; interest is paid regardless of profit.

subject: Accounting
stem: The appropriation account of a limited company distributes net profit after tax into
options: partners' salaries|corporation tax, dividends and retained earnings|drawings and interest on capital|only dividends
answer: corporation tax, dividends and retained earnings
rubric: Company appropriation: start with net profit → deduct corporation tax → deduct dividends → balance = retained earnings (reserves).

subject: Accounting
stem: Share premium arises when
options: shares are issued below par value|shares are issued above their par (nominal) value; the excess over par is the share premium|the company makes a profit|dividends are declared
answer: shares are issued above their par (nominal) value; the excess over par is the share premium
rubric: Share premium = issue price - par value. It goes to the share premium account in the equity section.

subject: Accounting
stem: Retained earnings (reserves) in a company balance sheet represent
options: the total issued capital|profits accumulated over the years after tax and dividends, retained in the business|loans from banks|debenture interest
answer: profits accumulated over the years after tax and dividends, retained in the business
rubric: Retained earnings build up year after year; they represent reinvested profits and form part of shareholders' equity.

subject: Accounting
stem: Issued share capital appears in the balance sheet under
options: non-current liabilities|current assets|equity (shareholders funds)|current liabilities
answer: equity (shareholders funds)
rubric: Issued share capital is part of equity (shareholders' funds), alongside share premium and retained earnings.

subject: Accounting
stem: The income statement of a limited company shows profit in the order
options: Gross Profit → Net Profit → Profit before tax → Tax → Profit after tax|Tax → Gross Profit → Net Profit|Dividends → Tax → Net Profit|Revenue → Tax → Gross Profit
answer: Gross Profit → Net Profit → Profit before tax → Tax → Profit after tax
rubric: Company income statement: Revenue - COGS = Gross Profit; - Expenses = Operating Profit; - Finance costs = PBT; - Tax = PAT.

subject: Accounting
stem: Dividend per share is calculated as
options: Total dividends / Net profit|Total dividends declared / Number of shares issued|Share price / Earnings|Net profit / Revenue
answer: Total dividends declared / Number of shares issued
rubric: DPS = Total Dividends / Number of Shares. It shows how much each shareholder receives per share held.

subject: Accounting
stem: Earnings per share (EPS) is calculated as
options: Gross Profit / Shares|Profit after tax / Number of ordinary shares|Dividends / Shares|Revenue / Shares
answer: Profit after tax / Number of ordinary shares
rubric: EPS = PAT / Number of ordinary shares. A key measure of profitability on a per-share basis.

subject: Accounting
stem: A rights issue allows existing shareholders to
options: vote for a new director|buy new shares at a discount proportional to their existing holding before the public|receive extra dividends|sell their shares back to the company
answer: buy new shares at a discount proportional to their existing holding before the public
rubric: A rights issue raises new equity capital by giving current shareholders the right to purchase additional shares at a below-market price.

subject: Accounting
stem: Bonus (scrip) shares are issued to existing shareholders
options: as a cash payment|as free additional shares funded by converting retained earnings into share capital (not raising new cash)|in exchange for new investment|from a new stock market listing
answer: as free additional shares funded by converting retained earnings into share capital (not raising new cash)
rubric: Bonus issue: capitalises reserves — Dr Reserves; Cr Share Capital. Shareholders get more shares; no cash is raised.

subject: Accounting
stem: The par (nominal) value of a share is
options: its market price|the face value stated on the share certificate (e.g. N1 or 50k)|the dividend paid|the earnings per share
answer: the face value stated on the share certificate (e.g. N1 or 50k)
rubric: Par (nominal) value is the minimum issue price recorded on the certificate; market price usually differs from par.

subject: Economics
stem: Economics is primarily concerned with
options: producing as much as possible|how individuals, firms and governments make choices to allocate scarce resources among unlimited wants|maximising government revenue|eliminating poverty only
answer: how individuals, firms and governments make choices to allocate scarce resources among unlimited wants
rubric: Economics: the social science studying how scarce resources (land, labour, capital, enterprise) are allocated among competing uses.

subject: Economics
stem: Scarcity in economics means
options: goods are very expensive|resources are limited relative to unlimited human wants|the government controls production|goods cannot be produced
answer: resources are limited relative to unlimited human wants
rubric: Scarcity is the fundamental economic problem: wants are infinite but the resources to satisfy them are finite.

subject: Economics
stem: The opportunity cost of a decision is
options: the money paid|the value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made|the total cost|the profit made
answer: the value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made
rubric: Opportunity cost: choosing one option means giving up the next best option — its value is the true cost of the choice.

subject: Economics
stem: Which of the following is NOT a factor of production?
options: Land|Labour|Capital|Money
answer: Money
rubric: Factors of production: Land, Labour, Capital, Enterprise. Money is a medium of exchange, not a factor of production itself.

subject: Economics
stem: The reward for entrepreneurship is
options: wages|rent|interest|profit
answer: profit
rubric: Factor rewards: Land = Rent; Labour = Wages/Salary; Capital = Interest; Enterprise = Profit.

subject: Economics
stem: A production possibility frontier (PPF) shows
options: the maximum combinations of two goods an economy can produce with given resources and technology|only one good|unlimited output|future production only
answer: the maximum combinations of two goods an economy can produce with given resources and technology
rubric: PPF: boundary between attainable and unattainable combinations; any point inside = inefficiency; on PPF = efficiency.

subject: Economics
stem: A point inside the production possibility frontier indicates
options: maximum efficiency|underutilisation of resources (inefficiency)|impossible production|maximum output
answer: underutilisation of resources (inefficiency)
rubric: Points inside the PPF mean resources are unemployed or used inefficiently — the economy can produce more.

subject: Economics
stem: Microeconomics studies
options: the economy as a whole|individual economic units — consumers, firms and markets|government budgets only|international trade only
answer: individual economic units — consumers, firms and markets
rubric: Microeconomics: individual choices, prices, markets, firm behaviour, consumer theory.

subject: Economics
stem: Macroeconomics studies
options: individual markets only|the economy as a whole — national income, inflation, unemployment, growth, balance of payments|single firms|household spending only
answer: the economy as a whole — national income, inflation, unemployment, growth, balance of payments
rubric: Macroeconomics: aggregate variables — GDP, price level, employment, monetary policy, fiscal policy.

subject: Economics
stem: The basic economic problem arises because of
options: too many resources|scarcity — unlimited wants cannot all be satisfied with limited resources, requiring choices|poor management|government policies
answer: scarcity — unlimited wants cannot all be satisfied with limited resources, requiring choices
rubric: The economic problem (scarcity) means all economies must answer: what to produce, how, and for whom.

subject: Economics
stem: A free good is one that is
options: provided by the government|available in unlimited supply at zero price (e.g. air, sunlight)|very cheap|produced with no cost
answer: available in unlimited supply at zero price (e.g. air, sunlight)
rubric: Free goods are not scarce — they are available without sacrifice. Economic goods are scarce and have a price.

subject: Economics
stem: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that
options: utility never decreases|as a consumer consumes more units of a good, the additional (marginal) utility from each extra unit eventually falls|all goods have equal utility|utility always increases
answer: as a consumer consumes more units of a good, the additional (marginal) utility from each extra unit eventually falls
rubric: Diminishing marginal utility: the 1st slice of pizza is most satisfying; each additional slice gives less extra satisfaction.

subject: Economics
stem: Utility in economics means
options: usefulness or the ability of a good/service to satisfy a want|the cost of a good|the quality of a good|government value
answer: usefulness or the ability of a good/service to satisfy a want
rubric: Utility is the satisfaction or benefit a consumer derives from consuming a good or service.

subject: Economics
stem: Which of the following is an example of a positive economic statement?
options: Taxes should be higher|The government ought to reduce inequality|An increase in money supply leads to inflation in the long run|Everyone deserves free healthcare
answer: An increase in money supply leads to inflation in the long run
rubric: Positive statements are factual/testable (what IS). Normative statements involve value judgements (what OUGHT to be).

subject: Economics
stem: Division of labour leads to all of the following EXCEPT
options: higher productivity|greater efficiency through specialisation|complete self-sufficiency for each worker|greater interdependence
answer: complete self-sufficiency for each worker
rubric: Division of labour creates specialisation and interdependence — the opposite of self-sufficiency.

subject: Economics
stem: Economies of scale refer to
options: increases in average cost as output rises|reductions in average cost per unit as a firm grows larger (long-run)|constant costs|only financial savings
answer: reductions in average cost per unit as a firm grows larger (long-run)
rubric: Economies of scale: larger output spreads fixed costs, enables bulk buying, specialisation — all reducing average cost.

subject: Economics
stem: Diseconomies of scale occur when
options: a firm grows and its average cost falls|a firm grows too large and average costs begin to rise|costs are fixed|production stops
answer: a firm grows too large and average costs begin to rise
rubric: Diseconomies: management complexity, communication breakdowns and coordination problems push up average costs beyond the optimal scale.

subject: Economics
stem: A merit good is one that
options: the market over-provides|the government believes would be under-consumed if left to the market, so it subsidises or provides it (e.g. education, healthcare)|has no positive externalities|creates negative externalities only
answer: the government believes would be under-consumed if left to the market, so it subsidises or provides it (e.g. education, healthcare)
rubric: Merit goods generate positive externalities and are under-valued by consumers — government intervention corrects this.

subject: Economics
stem: A public good has two characteristics: it is
options: rival and excludable|non-rival and non-excludable|free and scarce|provided only by governments
answer: non-rival and non-excludable
rubric: Public goods (street lighting, national defence): one person's use doesn't reduce availability to others (non-rival); cannot exclude anyone (non-excludable).

subject: Economics
stem: An external cost (negative externality) is a cost
options: paid by the producer|borne by third parties not involved in the transaction (e.g. pollution)|paid by the consumer|included in the market price
answer: borne by third parties not involved in the transaction (e.g. pollution)
rubric: Externalities: costs or benefits falling on those outside the transaction. Negative externalities cause market failure.

subject: Economics
stem: The law of demand states that
options: as price rises, quantity demanded rises|as price falls, quantity demanded falls|as price rises, quantity demanded falls, ceteris paribus|demand is always constant
answer: as price rises, quantity demanded falls, ceteris paribus
rubric: Law of demand: there is an inverse (negative) relationship between price and quantity demanded, all else equal.

subject: Economics
stem: Ceteris paribus means
options: all things change|all other things remaining equal (held constant)|price only changes|quantity only changes
answer: all other things remaining equal (held constant)
rubric: Ceteris paribus: Latin for "all else equal" — used in economics to isolate the effect of one variable.

subject: Economics
stem: A demand curve slopes downward from left to right because of
options: the law of supply|the law of demand — higher prices reduce quantity demanded|rising costs|government policy
answer: the law of demand — higher prices reduce quantity demanded
rubric: Downward slope: as price increases, consumers buy less (substitution effect and income effect).

subject: Economics
stem: Which of the following would cause a RIGHTWARD (outward) shift of the demand curve?
options: A fall in consumer income (normal good)|A rise in the price of a complementary good|An increase in consumer income (normal good)|A rise in the good's own price
answer: An increase in consumer income (normal good)
rubric: Rightward shift: increase in demand from: income rise (normal good), cheaper complements, taste change favouring the good, population growth.

subject: Economics
stem: A movement along the demand curve is caused by
options: a change in income|a change in tastes|a change in the good's own price|a change in population
answer: a change in the good's own price
rubric: Movements along the demand curve: ONLY the good's own price changes; quantity demanded changes accordingly.

subject: Economics
stem: A shift of the demand curve is caused by
options: a change in the good's own price only|a change in any factor other than the good's own price (income, prices of related goods, tastes, expectations, population)|only by advertising|only by government policy
answer: a change in any factor other than the good's own price (income, prices of related goods, tastes, expectations, population)
rubric: Shifts in demand: non-price factors — PIRATES (Prices of related goods, Income, Related goods, Advertising, Tastes, Expectations, Size of population).

subject: Economics
stem: A normal good is one for which demand
options: falls as income rises|rises as income rises|is unaffected by income|is determined only by price
answer: rises as income rises
rubric: Normal goods have a positive income elasticity: as incomes rise, consumers buy more (e.g. holidays, cars).

subject: Economics
stem: An inferior good is one for which demand
options: rises as income rises|falls as income rises (consumers switch to better alternatives)|is unaffected by income|is always inelastic
answer: falls as income rises (consumers switch to better alternatives)
rubric: Inferior goods have negative income elasticity: as incomes rise, demand for them falls (e.g. public transport vs car, garri vs rice).

subject: Economics
stem: Substitute goods are goods that
options: are used together|can replace each other; a rise in the price of one increases demand for the other|have no relationship|are always of equal quality
answer: can replace each other; a rise in the price of one increases demand for the other
rubric: Substitutes: if price of good A rises, demand for substitute B increases (e.g. butter and margarine, Coke and Pepsi).

subject: Economics
stem: Complementary goods are goods that
options: are used independently|are used together; a rise in the price of one reduces demand for the other|compete in the market|have the same price
answer: are used together; a rise in the price of one reduces demand for the other
rubric: Complements are consumed jointly (e.g. cars and petrol, printers and ink). Price rise of one reduces demand for both.

subject: Economics
stem: Price elasticity of demand (PED) measures
options: how supply responds to price|the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the good's own price|how income affects quantity demanded|how supply shifts
answer: the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the good's own price
rubric: PED = % change in quantity demanded / % change in price. It measures consumer sensitivity to price changes.

subject: Economics
stem: If PED = -2, demand is described as
options: inelastic|elastic (responsive) — a 1% price rise causes a 2% fall in quantity demanded|unitary elastic|perfectly inelastic
answer: elastic (responsive) — a 1% price rise causes a 2% fall in quantity demanded
rubric: |PED| > 1: elastic. |PED| < 1: inelastic. |PED| = 1: unitary elastic.

subject: Economics
stem: If PED = -0.3, demand is
options: elastic|inelastic — quantity demanded is relatively insensitive to price changes|unitary elastic|perfectly elastic
answer: inelastic — quantity demanded is relatively insensitive to price changes
rubric: |PED| = 0.3 < 1: inelastic. Consumers continue to buy even when price rises (e.g. necessities like salt, fuel).

subject: Economics
stem: When demand is price inelastic, a firm that raises price will find that
options: total revenue falls|total revenue rises|total revenue is unchanged|quantity demanded rises
answer: total revenue rises
rubric: Inelastic demand: % fall in quantity < % rise in price → Total Revenue increases when price rises.

subject: Economics
stem: Income elasticity of demand (YED) measures
options: price sensitivity|how quantity demanded changes in response to a change in consumer income|supply responsiveness|elasticity of supply
answer: how quantity demanded changes in response to a change in consumer income
rubric: YED = % change in quantity demanded / % change in income. Positive YED = normal good; negative YED = inferior good.

subject: Economics
stem: Cross elasticity of demand (XED) measures
options: own-price sensitivity|responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another good|income sensitivity|supply sensitivity
answer: responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another good
rubric: XED: positive = substitutes; negative = complements; zero = unrelated goods.

subject: Economics
stem: Effective demand is demand backed by
options: any desire|the ability and willingness to pay at a given price|government support|advertising only
answer: the ability and willingness to pay at a given price
rubric: Effective demand: want + willingness + ability to pay. A desire without purchasing power is not effective demand.

subject: Economics
stem: The demand for labour is described as a derived demand because
options: it creates its own supply|it arises from the demand for the goods and services that labour helps produce|it is always inelastic|it is fixed by government
answer: it arises from the demand for the goods and services that labour helps produce
rubric: Derived demand: firms demand labour (and other factors) not for its own sake but to produce goods consumers want.

subject: Economics
stem: A Giffen good is one for which
options: demand falls as income rises|demand rises as its price rises (an exception to the law of demand for very inferior goods where the income effect outweighs the substitution effect)|demand is perfectly elastic|supply determines demand
answer: demand rises as its price rises (an exception to the law of demand for very inferior goods where the income effect outweighs the substitution effect)
rubric: Giffen good: very inferior good where a price rise reduces real income so much that consumers buy MORE of it (upward-sloping demand).

subject: Economics
stem: Joint demand exists when
options: two goods compete|two goods are demanded together (complements) — the demand for one generates demand for the other|one good can replace another|demand is always the same
answer: two goods are demanded together (complements) — the demand for one generates demand for the other
rubric: Joint (complementary) demand: cars and petrol, left and right shoes — demand for one implies demand for the other.

subject: Economics
stem: Composite demand exists when
options: a good has only one use|a good has many uses; demand from one sector competes with demand from another (e.g. land for housing vs farming)|a good is a complement|a good is a Giffen good
answer: a good has many uses; demand from one sector competes with demand from another (e.g. land for housing vs farming)
rubric: Composite demand: one resource (milk for cheese, butter, cream; land for farming, housing, industry) is demanded for multiple purposes.

subject: Economics
stem: A demand schedule shows the relationship between
options: income and quantity supplied|various prices and the corresponding quantities demanded, ceteris paribus|supply and price|cost and revenue
answer: various prices and the corresponding quantities demanded, ceteris paribus
rubric: A demand schedule is a table listing (price, quantity demanded) pairs; used to plot the demand curve.

subject: Economics
stem: When the price of a good falls, consumers tend to buy more because of the substitution effect. This means they
options: buy the same amount|switch to the now relatively cheaper good, replacing more expensive alternatives|buy less|stop consuming
answer: switch to the now relatively cheaper good, replacing more expensive alternatives
rubric: Substitution effect: lower price makes a good relatively cheaper than substitutes → consumers buy more of it.

subject: Economics
stem: The income effect of a price fall for a normal good means that
options: real income falls so demand falls|the fall in price increases consumers' real purchasing power, so they buy more of the normal good|demand is unchanged|the good becomes inferior
answer: the fall in price increases consumers' real purchasing power, so they buy more of the normal good
rubric: Income effect: price fall = more real income → buy more normal goods. Combined with substitution effect = law of demand.

subject: Economics
stem: Which of the following goods tends to have the most price inelastic demand?
options: Luxury holidays|Designer handbags|Salt (a necessity with no close substitutes)|Branded soft drinks
answer: Salt (a necessity with no close substitutes)
rubric: Necessities with no close substitutes, few alternatives and low income share (like salt) tend to be highly price inelastic.

subject: Economics
stem: The law of supply states that
options: as price rises, quantity supplied falls|as price rises, quantity supplied rises, ceteris paribus|supply is always constant|price and supply are unrelated
answer: as price rises, quantity supplied rises, ceteris paribus
rubric: Law of supply: positive relationship between price and quantity supplied — higher prices make production more profitable.

subject: Economics
stem: The supply curve slopes upward from left to right because
options: firms always produce more regardless of price|higher prices make production more profitable, incentivising greater output|costs never change|government sets all prices
answer: higher prices make production more profitable, incentivising greater output
rubric: As price rises, the higher profit margin attracts existing firms to produce more and new firms to enter.

subject: Economics
stem: Which of the following would cause a RIGHTWARD shift of the supply curve?
options: A rise in raw material costs|An improvement in production technology that reduces costs|A rise in wages|A tax on production
answer: An improvement in production technology that reduces costs
rubric: Rightward supply shift: costs fall (technology, cheaper inputs), subsidies, more firms enter, better weather (agricultural).

subject: Economics
stem: A movement along the supply curve is caused by
options: a change in production costs|a change in the number of producers|a change in the good's own price|a change in government policy
answer: a change in the good's own price
rubric: Movements along the supply curve: ONLY a change in the good's own price causes movement along (change in quantity supplied).

subject: Economics
stem: Price elasticity of supply (PES) measures
options: how demand responds to price|the responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price|income sensitivity|cross-price effects
answer: the responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price
rubric: PES = % change in quantity supplied / % change in price. PES > 1: elastic; PES < 1: inelastic.

subject: Economics
stem: Supply is likely to be more price elastic when
options: production takes a long time|there is spare capacity, inputs are easily available and time allows output to be varied|materials are scarce|the good is perishable only
answer: there is spare capacity, inputs are easily available and time allows output to be varied
rubric: Elastic supply: easy to scale up production — spare capacity, flexible inputs, sufficient time. Agricultural goods are inelastic.

subject: Economics
stem: A subsidy given to producers will
options: shift the supply curve leftward|shift the supply curve rightward (increase supply at every price)|raise the price|reduce output
answer: shift the supply curve rightward (increase supply at every price)
rubric: Subsidy reduces costs for producers → they can supply more at each price → supply curve shifts right.

subject: Economics
stem: An indirect tax (e.g. VAT) imposed on producers will
options: shift supply rightward|shift supply leftward (decrease supply — raises costs)|increase output|reduce price for consumers
answer: shift supply leftward (decrease supply — raises costs)
rubric: A production tax raises costs → supply falls (shifts left) → price rises and quantity falls.

subject: Economics
stem: Joint supply occurs when
options: two goods are demanded together|producing one good automatically results in the production of another (e.g. beef and leather, petrol and diesel)|supply equals demand|two firms produce the same good
answer: producing one good automatically results in the production of another (e.g. beef and leather, petrol and diesel)
rubric: Joint supply: by-products. Increasing production of one increases supply of the other, lowering its price.

subject: Economics
stem: Competitive supply exists when
options: the same resources can be used to produce either of two goods; more of one means less of the other|two goods are always produced together|supply and demand are equal|firms cooperate in production
answer: the same resources can be used to produce either of two goods; more of one means less of the other
rubric: Competitive supply: wheat and maize compete for the same land. Increasing one diverts resources from the other.

subject: Economics
stem: A supply schedule shows
options: income and quantity demanded|quantities producers are willing and able to supply at various prices, ceteris paribus|cost and profit|population and output
answer: quantities producers are willing and able to supply at various prices, ceteris paribus
rubric: A supply schedule lists (price, quantity supplied) pairs; the data points plot the supply curve.

subject: Economics
stem: Which of the following will shift the supply curve of agricultural goods rightward?
options: A drought|Increase in fertiliser cost|Favourable weather and bumper harvest|Higher wages for farm workers
answer: Favourable weather and bumper harvest
rubric: Good weather increases agricultural output at every price → rightward supply shift.

subject: Economics
stem: Perfectly inelastic supply (PES = 0) means
options: supply responds greatly to price|quantity supplied does not change regardless of price (e.g. land in a country)|price has no effect|supply is highly flexible
answer: quantity supplied does not change regardless of price (e.g. land in a country)
rubric: PES = 0: vertical supply curve. Total land in a country is fixed — price cannot increase its supply.

subject: Economics
stem: In the long run, supply tends to be more elastic than in the short run because
options: prices fall in the long run|firms have more time to adjust capacity, enter the market or change production methods|demand changes|government deregulates
answer: firms have more time to adjust capacity, enter the market or change production methods
rubric: Long-run supply is more elastic as firms can build new factories, hire more workers and new firms can enter the industry.

subject: Economics
stem: The producer surplus is the amount
options: a consumer gains from a transaction|a producer receives above the minimum price at which they were willing to supply|paid as tax|earned as wages
answer: a producer receives above the minimum price at which they were willing to supply
rubric: Producer surplus = actual price received - minimum acceptable price. It is the area above the supply curve and below the price.

subject: Economics
stem: An increase in the number of firms in a market will, ceteris paribus,
options: decrease supply|increase supply and shift the supply curve rightward|have no effect on supply|shift the demand curve
answer: increase supply and shift the supply curve rightward
rubric: More firms → more production at every price → rightward supply shift → lower equilibrium price.

subject: Economics
stem: Higher wages for workers, ceteris paribus, will affect supply by
options: shifting supply rightward|shifting supply leftward (cost of production rises, reducing profitability)|having no effect|only affecting demand
answer: shifting supply leftward (cost of production rises, reducing profitability)
rubric: Higher wages = higher production costs → supply decreases (shifts left) → price tends to rise.

subject: Economics
stem: The supply of luxury goods tends to be more elastic than agricultural goods because
options: luxury goods are grown|industrial goods can more easily expand or reduce output in response to price signals|all goods have the same elasticity|luxury goods are necessities
answer: industrial goods can more easily expand or reduce output in response to price signals
rubric: Manufactured goods can adjust production more flexibly than crops, which depend on seasons and growing periods.

subject: Economics
stem: Expectations about future prices can affect current supply; if producers expect prices to rise,
options: they may increase current supply immediately|they may withhold current supply to sell more later at the higher price|supply stays the same|demand falls
answer: they may withhold current supply to sell more later at the higher price
rubric: Expectations: anticipated price rise may cause producers to reduce current supply (withhold stock), shifting supply left now.

subject: Economics
stem: A fall in the price of a related good in competitive supply (e.g. maize falls so farmers switch to wheat) will
options: decrease supply of wheat|increase supply of wheat (farmers divert resources from maize to wheat)|increase demand for maize|have no effect
answer: increase supply of wheat (farmers divert resources from maize to wheat)
rubric: Farmers switch from cheaper maize to more profitable wheat → wheat supply increases → rightward shift for wheat.

subject: Economics
stem: Market equilibrium occurs when
options: supply exceeds demand|quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so the market clears at the equilibrium price|demand exceeds supply|price is at its minimum
answer: quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so the market clears at the equilibrium price
rubric: At equilibrium: no surplus or shortage; the market-clearing price balances the plans of buyers and sellers.

subject: Economics
stem: A market surplus (excess supply) occurs when
options: price is at equilibrium|price is above equilibrium — quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded|price is below equilibrium|supply equals demand
answer: price is above equilibrium — quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded
rubric: Surplus: at a price above equilibrium, producers supply more than consumers want; price falls toward equilibrium.

subject: Economics
stem: A market shortage (excess demand) occurs when
options: supply equals demand|price is below equilibrium — quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied|price is at equilibrium|supply is unlimited
answer: price is below equilibrium — quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied
rubric: Shortage: at a price below equilibrium, consumers want more than producers supply; price rises toward equilibrium.

subject: Economics
stem: If demand increases (shifts right) while supply stays constant, the equilibrium price will
options: fall|rise|remain the same|become negative
answer: rise
rubric: Increase in demand → at old price, shortage occurs → price rises until new equilibrium reached with higher price and quantity.

subject: Economics
stem: If supply increases (shifts right) while demand stays constant, the equilibrium price will
options: rise|fall|remain the same|become zero
answer: fall
rubric: Increase in supply → at old price, surplus occurs → price falls until new equilibrium with lower price and higher quantity.

subject: Economics
stem: A price ceiling set BELOW the equilibrium price will cause
options: a surplus|a shortage (excess demand, since price is kept too low for the market to clear)|no effect|supply to increase
answer: a shortage (excess demand, since price is kept too low for the market to clear)
rubric: Price ceiling below equilibrium: quantity demanded > quantity supplied → shortage. Used e.g. for rent control or food prices.

subject: Economics
stem: A price floor set ABOVE the equilibrium price will cause
options: a shortage|a surplus (excess supply, since the minimum price is higher than what clears the market)|no effect|demand to increase
answer: a surplus (excess supply, since the minimum price is higher than what clears the market)
rubric: Price floor above equilibrium: quantity supplied > quantity demanded → surplus (e.g. minimum wage causing unemployment in a simplified model).

subject: Economics
stem: Consumer surplus is the difference between
options: cost of production and price|what consumers are willing and able to pay and what they actually pay|the maximum and minimum prices|wages and profits
answer: what consumers are willing and able to pay and what they actually pay
rubric: Consumer surplus = willingness to pay - actual price paid. It is the area below the demand curve and above the price.

subject: Economics
stem: Which of the following best describes a free market economy?
options: The government owns all resources|Prices are set by market forces of demand and supply with minimal government intervention|The government plans all production|Only government firms operate
answer: Prices are set by market forces of demand and supply with minimal government intervention
rubric: Free market: private ownership, price mechanism, consumer sovereignty, profit motive, minimal government role.

subject: Economics
stem: Market failure occurs when
options: prices are high|the free market fails to allocate resources efficiently, leading to under/over-provision or inequity|taxes are low|the government intervenes
answer: the free market fails to allocate resources efficiently, leading to under/over-provision or inequity
rubric: Market failures: externalities, public goods, information asymmetry, monopoly power, income inequality.

subject: Economics
stem: The cobweb model describes
options: how technology changes supply|how prices fluctuate in markets where supply responds to last period's price (e.g. agriculture) rather than current price|how demand shifts|how consumers respond to advertising
answer: how prices fluctuate in markets where supply responds to last period's price (e.g. agriculture) rather than current price
rubric: Cobweb: farmers plan based on last year's price; if this year's harvest is large, prices fall, next year farmers grow less, prices rise, etc.

subject: Economics
stem: A black market arises when
options: government taxes are high|goods are bought and sold illegally, typically when official prices are controlled and do not clear the market|all goods are free|supply is unlimited
answer: goods are bought and sold illegally, typically when official prices are controlled and do not clear the market
rubric: Black markets emerge when price controls create shortages; buyers and sellers transact at illegal market-clearing prices.

subject: Economics
stem: Rationing is a method used when
options: supply exceeds demand|government distributes limited goods during a shortage to ensure fair distribution|prices are too high|profits are too large
answer: government distributes limited goods during a shortage to ensure fair distribution
rubric: Rationing (by coupons, queuing, lottery) ensures scarce goods are distributed fairly during emergencies or price controls.

subject: Economics
stem: The price mechanism allocates resources through
options: government directives|the interaction of supply and demand, which signals producers what to produce and at what price|only wages|administrative decisions only
answer: the interaction of supply and demand, which signals producers what to produce and at what price
rubric: Price mechanism (invisible hand): rising prices signal more production needed; falling prices signal oversupply — allocating resources without central planning.

subject: Economics
stem: When both demand and supply increase simultaneously, the effect on the equilibrium quantity is
options: always to decrease it|always to increase it|uncertain, depending on the relative magnitudes of the shifts|to remain constant
answer: always to increase it
rubric: Both shifts increase quantity; price effect is uncertain. If demand increases more, price rises; if supply more, price falls.

subject: Economics
stem: A mixed economy is one where
options: only the private sector operates|both the public (government) and private sectors allocate resources|only the government operates|trade is prohibited
answer: both the public (government) and private sectors allocate resources
rubric: Mixed economy: markets allocate most resources but government provides public goods, corrects market failures and redistributes income.

subject: Economics
stem: Monopoly is a market structure where
options: many firms compete|there is a single seller of a product with no close substitutes, giving it price-making power|there are two firms|there is perfect competition
answer: there is a single seller of a product with no close substitutes, giving it price-making power
rubric: Monopoly: one seller, high barriers to entry, price maker, no close substitutes. Often leads to higher prices and lower output.

subject: Economics
stem: An oligopoly is a market structure dominated by
options: one firm|two firms only|a few large firms that are interdependent in their pricing and output decisions|many small firms
answer: a few large firms that are interdependent in their pricing and output decisions
rubric: Oligopoly (e.g. telecoms, banking, airlines): few dominant firms, high barriers to entry, interdependence and possible collusion.

subject: Economics
stem: Perfect competition requires all of the following EXCEPT
options: many buyers and sellers|homogeneous products|barriers to entry|free entry and exit
answer: barriers to entry
rubric: Perfect competition: many buyers/sellers, homogeneous goods, perfect information, free entry and exit — NOT barriers to entry.

subject: Economics
stem: Price discrimination occurs when
options: all consumers pay the same price|a firm charges different prices to different groups of consumers for the same product|the government sets different prices|costs differ by region
answer: a firm charges different prices to different groups of consumers for the same product
rubric: Price discrimination (e.g. student discounts, peak vs off-peak fares): same product, different prices based on willingness/ability to pay.

subject: Economics
stem: The short run in economics is a period in which
options: all factors of production can be varied|at least one factor of production (usually capital) is fixed|no production takes place|only wages can change
answer: at least one factor of production (usually capital) is fixed
rubric: Short run: at least one input (capital/plant size) is fixed; firms can vary labour and raw materials only.

subject: Economics
stem: The long run is a period in which
options: all inputs remain fixed|all factors of production can be varied (no fixed inputs)|only prices change|only one factor changes
answer: all factors of production can be varied (no fixed inputs)
rubric: Long run: all factors variable — firms can change plant size, enter or exit the industry.

subject: Economics
stem: Fixed costs are costs that
options: change with output|do not change with output in the short run (e.g. rent, loan interest, insurance)|only occur in the long run|apply only to materials
answer: do not change with output in the short run (e.g. rent, loan interest, insurance)
rubric: Fixed costs (overheads) are incurred regardless of output: rent, machinery depreciation, management salaries.

subject: Economics
stem: Variable costs are costs that
options: remain constant regardless of output|change in direct proportion to output (e.g. raw materials, direct labour, power)|are never changed|are paid annually
answer: change in direct proportion to output (e.g. raw materials, direct labour, power)
rubric: Variable costs rise as output rises; zero output means zero variable cost.

subject: Economics
stem: Total cost (TC) equals
options: Fixed cost only|Fixed cost + Variable cost|Revenue - Profit|Profit + Revenue
answer: Fixed cost + Variable cost
rubric: TC = TFC + TVC. As output rises, TC rises because TVC rises while TFC remains constant.

subject: Economics
stem: Average cost (AC) is calculated as
options: Total Cost / Price|Total Cost / Quantity of output|Revenue / Quantity|Profit / Quantity
answer: Total Cost / Quantity of output
rubric: Average Cost (AC) = TC / Q. It represents cost per unit of output.

subject: Economics
stem: Marginal cost (MC) is
options: the average cost per unit|the additional cost of producing one more unit of output|the total cost of all output|the fixed cost per unit
answer: the additional cost of producing one more unit of output
rubric: MC = change in TC / change in Q. MC initially falls then rises as the law of diminishing returns sets in.

subject: Economics
stem: The law of diminishing returns states that
options: all inputs give the same return|as more units of a variable input are added to fixed inputs, beyond a point the marginal product of the variable input will fall|returns always increase|fixed costs rise with output
answer: as more units of a variable input are added to fixed inputs, beyond a point the marginal product of the variable input will fall
rubric: Diminishing returns (short run): adding more workers to a fixed factory eventually reduces additional output per worker.

subject: Economics
stem: The marginal cost curve intersects the average cost curve at the
options: maximum point of AC|minimum point of AC|maximum point of MC|zero output point
answer: minimum point of AC
rubric: The MC curve always crosses the AC curve at AC's lowest point: when MC < AC, AC falls; when MC > AC, AC rises.

subject: Economics
stem: Total revenue (TR) is calculated as
options: Total Cost x Profit|Price x Quantity sold|Fixed Cost + Variable Cost|Gross Profit + Expenses
answer: Price x Quantity sold
rubric: TR = P x Q. Total revenue is what the firm earns from selling its output.

subject: Economics
stem: A firm will produce in the short run as long as
options: TR > TC|Price exceeds average total cost|Price exceeds average variable cost (covering variable costs and contributing to fixed costs)|Marginal profit is negative
answer: Price exceeds average variable cost (covering variable costs and contributing to fixed costs)
rubric: Short-run shut-down condition: if P < AVC, the firm cannot cover variable costs → shuts down. If P > AVC, produces even if making a loss.

subject: Economics
stem: Profit maximisation occurs at the output where
options: TR is maximum|MC = MR (marginal cost equals marginal revenue)|TC is minimum|fixed cost equals variable cost
answer: MC = MR (marginal cost equals marginal revenue)
rubric: Profit max rule: produce where MC = MR. Beyond this, extra unit costs more than it earns; before, it earns more than it costs.

subject: Economics
stem: The break-even point is where
options: TR is maximum|TR = TC (total revenue equals total cost — neither profit nor loss)|MC = MR|AVC = AFC
answer: TR = TC (total revenue equals total cost — neither profit nor loss)
rubric: Break-even: the firm covers all costs but earns zero profit. Below break-even output, losses are made.

subject: Economics
stem: Economies of scale lead to a
options: rightward shift of the demand curve|fall in the long-run average cost as output increases|rise in short-run fixed costs|higher price in the market
answer: fall in the long-run average cost as output increases
rubric: Internal economies of scale (technical, managerial, financial, marketing) reduce average cost as the firm grows.

subject: Economics
stem: The average fixed cost (AFC) curve is
options: U-shaped|L-shaped|horizontal|constantly falling as output increases, since fixed costs are spread over more units
answer: constantly falling as output increases, since fixed costs are spread over more units
rubric: AFC = TFC / Q. As Q rises, the fixed cost is shared over more units → AFC falls continuously.

subject: Economics
stem: Normal profit is
options: extra profit above all costs|the minimum profit required to keep the entrepreneur in the current industry (included in costs as the opportunity cost of capital)|always zero|higher than supernormal profit
answer: the minimum profit required to keep the entrepreneur in the current industry (included in costs as the opportunity cost of capital)
rubric: Normal profit: the return equal to the opportunity cost of the entrepreneur's time and capital — included in average cost.

subject: Economics
stem: Supernormal (abnormal) profit occurs when
options: TR = TC|TR > TC (total revenue exceeds total costs including normal profit)|price equals AVC|the firm breaks even
answer: TR > TC (total revenue exceeds total costs including normal profit)
rubric: Supernormal profit = TR - TC (where TC includes normal profit). In perfect competition, it attracts new entrants, eroding the profit.

subject: Economics
stem: The four factors of production are
options: Land, Labour, Capital and Money|Land, Labour, Capital and Enterprise|Labour, Technology, Capital and Money|Land, Labour, Government and Enterprise
answer: Land, Labour, Capital and Enterprise
rubric: Factors of production: Land (natural resources), Labour (human effort), Capital (man-made aids to production), Enterprise (risk-taking organisation).

subject: Economics
stem: Implicit costs are
options: costs recorded in the accounts|opportunity costs of using the owner's own resources (own time, own capital) which do not involve a cash payment|government taxes|variable costs
answer: opportunity costs of using the owner's own resources (own time, own capital) which do not involve a cash payment
rubric: Implicit costs: foregone income from owner's resources used in business (own labour, own building) — not shown in accounting profit.

subject: Economics
stem: Economic profit equals
options: accounting profit|accounting profit minus implicit costs (opportunity costs)|total revenue|total cost
answer: accounting profit minus implicit costs (opportunity costs)
rubric: Economic profit = TR - (explicit + implicit costs). If economic profit = 0, the firm earns normal profit.

subject: Economics
stem: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures
options: the wealth of individuals|the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period|only exports|government spending only
answer: the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period
rubric: GDP: the most widely used measure of a country's economic output produced domestically in a year.

subject: Economics
stem: The difference between GDP and GNP (Gross National Product) is
options: GDP excludes services|GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad (income earned by residents abroad minus income earned by foreigners domestically)|GNP is always larger|they are identical
answer: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad (income earned by residents abroad minus income earned by foreigners domestically)
rubric: GNP measures output by a country's nationals regardless of location; GDP measures output within borders.

subject: Economics
stem: The expenditure approach to measuring national income adds up
options: all incomes earned|Consumer spending + Investment + Government spending + (Exports - Imports) — C+I+G+(X-M)|only wages|only profits
answer: Consumer spending + Investment + Government spending + (Exports - Imports) — C+I+G+(X-M)
rubric: Expenditure approach: Y = C + I + G + (X - M). The sum of all final expenditures equals national income.

subject: Economics
stem: The income approach to measuring national income sums up
options: total expenditure|Wages + Rent + Interest + Profit earned by all factors of production|only GDP components|only government revenue
answer: Wages + Rent + Interest + Profit earned by all factors of production
rubric: Income approach: national income = sum of factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit) from production.

subject: Economics
stem: The output (value added) approach measures national income by
options: adding total revenue of all firms|summing the value added at each stage of production to avoid double counting|subtracting profits|measuring only imports
answer: summing the value added at each stage of production to avoid double counting
rubric: Output approach: value added = output - intermediate inputs at each stage. Summing across all stages = GDP.

subject: Economics
stem: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP in that
options: real GDP uses current prices|real GDP is adjusted for inflation (using constant prices), allowing comparison of actual output over time|nominal GDP is always lower|real GDP ignores services
answer: real GDP is adjusted for inflation (using constant prices), allowing comparison of actual output over time
rubric: Real GDP removes price level effects; it measures actual volume of output, not inflated monetary value.

subject: Economics
stem: Per capita GDP is
options: total GDP|GDP divided by the population — an approximation of average income per person|GDP times population|only wages per person
answer: GDP divided by the population — an approximation of average income per person
rubric: GDP per capita: provides a rough measure of average living standard; ignores distribution of income.

subject: Economics
stem: Transfer payments (e.g. unemployment benefit, pensions) are NOT included in national income because
options: they are too small|they are payments not made in exchange for current productive activity — no good or service is produced|they are paid by banks|they are informal
answer: they are payments not made in exchange for current productive activity — no good or service is produced
rubric: Transfer payments redistribute income without adding to output; including them would double-count or inflate national income.

subject: Economics
stem: Net National Product (NNP) is calculated as
options: GDP + depreciation|GNP minus depreciation (capital consumption)|GNP + imports|GDP + exports
answer: GNP minus depreciation (capital consumption)
rubric: NNP = GNP - Depreciation. It accounts for the wear and tear on capital used in production.

subject: Economics
stem: An increase in national income always means
options: improved welfare for all citizens|GDP has risen but not necessarily welfare, as distribution, leisure and non-market activities are excluded|inflation has fallen|poverty has ended
answer: GDP has risen but not necessarily welfare, as distribution, leisure and non-market activities are excluded
rubric: GDP is an imperfect welfare measure: it ignores inequality, environmental damage, unpaid work, leisure and quality of life.

subject: Economics
stem: The circular flow of income model shows
options: only trade flows|how income flows between households and firms — households provide factors, receive income, spend on goods; firms receive revenue and pay factor incomes|only government spending|only exports
answer: how income flows between households and firms — households provide factors, receive income, spend on goods; firms receive revenue and pay factor incomes
rubric: Circular flow: households supply factors → firms pay income → households spend → firms receive revenue → cycle repeats.

subject: Economics
stem: Injections into the circular flow of income include
options: savings, taxes and imports|Investment, Government spending and Exports|only government spending|only consumer spending
answer: Investment, Government spending and Exports
rubric: Injections add to the flow: I + G + X. Leakages (withdrawals) reduce it: S + T + M.

subject: Economics
stem: Leakages (withdrawals) from the circular flow include
options: Investment, Government spending and Exports|Savings, Taxes and Imports|Only consumer spending|Only wages
answer: Savings, Taxes and Imports
rubric: Leakages: S + T + M. They reduce spending in the circular flow. Equilibrium: injections = leakages.

subject: Economics
stem: The multiplier effect states that
options: an increase in investment leads to a smaller increase in national income|an initial injection of spending leads to a proportionally larger increase in national income|taxes always increase income|savings reduce the multiplier to zero
answer: an initial injection of spending leads to a proportionally larger increase in national income
rubric: The multiplier: each injection creates rounds of additional spending; multiplier = 1 / (1 - MPC) or 1 / MPS.

subject: Economics
stem: The marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is
options: the total amount consumed|the proportion of each extra unit of income that is spent on consumption|the total income saved|the proportion of income taxed
answer: the proportion of each extra unit of income that is spent on consumption
rubric: MPC = change in consumption / change in income. MPC + MPS = 1 (from an increase in income).

subject: Economics
stem: Business cycle (trade cycle) refers to
options: annual tax cycles|fluctuations in economic activity (GDP) between boom and recession phases over time|inflation cycles|stock market cycles only
answer: fluctuations in economic activity (GDP) between boom and recession phases over time
rubric: The business cycle: Boom → Downturn → Recession (trough) → Recovery → Boom. GDP growth fluctuates around the trend.

subject: Economics
stem: A recession is typically defined as
options: one quarter of negative GDP growth|two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth|a fall in population|a rise in inflation only
answer: two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth
rubric: Recession: two consecutive quarters (6 months) of falling real GDP; associated with rising unemployment and lower investment.

subject: Economics
stem: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level; it is measured in Nigeria using the
options: Retail Wage Index|Consumer Price Index (CPI) published by the National Bureau of Statistics|Stock Market Index|Balance of Payments
answer: Consumer Price Index (CPI) published by the National Bureau of Statistics
rubric: CPI tracks the prices of a representative basket of goods and services; year-on-year change = inflation rate.

subject: Economics
stem: Unemployment occurs when
options: everyone who wants to work has a job|people who are able and willing to work at prevailing wages cannot find employment|wages are very high|production is at capacity
answer: people who are able and willing to work at prevailing wages cannot find employment
rubric: Unemployment: labour is a wasted resource; reduces national output and income; causes social problems.

subject: Economics
stem: Fiscal policy involves the use of
options: interest rates|government spending and taxation to manage aggregate demand and stabilise the economy|exchange rates|money supply only
answer: government spending and taxation to manage aggregate demand and stabilise the economy
rubric: Fiscal policy: the government uses its budget (G and T) to influence the economy — expansionary (cut taxes, raise G) or contractionary.

subject: Economics
stem: The primary function of money is to serve as
options: a store of value|a medium of exchange — enabling trade without barter|a unit of account|a standard of deferred payment
answer: a medium of exchange — enabling trade without barter
rubric: The medium of exchange function is the primary function; others (store of value, unit of account, standard of deferred payment) are secondary.

subject: Economics
stem: The four functions of money are
options: Save, Spend, Invest, Borrow|Medium of exchange, Unit of account, Store of value, Standard of deferred payment|Buy, Sell, Hold, Invest|Earn, Save, Spend, Tax
answer: Medium of exchange, Unit of account, Store of value, Standard of deferred payment
rubric: Money's four functions: (1) Medium of exchange; (2) Unit of account/measure of value; (3) Store of value; (4) Standard of deferred payment.

subject: Economics
stem: Near money (quasi-money) refers to
options: coins and notes|highly liquid assets (e.g. treasury bills, time deposits) that are close substitutes for money but not immediately usable as a medium of exchange|government bonds only|foreign currency only
answer: highly liquid assets (e.g. treasury bills, time deposits) that are close substitutes for money but not immediately usable as a medium of exchange
rubric: Near money: easily convertible to cash; not legal tender themselves; included in broader monetary aggregates (M2, M3).

subject: Economics
stem: The quantity theory of money (MV = PT) states that
options: money supply is unrelated to prices|the money supply (M) times velocity (V) equals the price level (P) times transactions (T); increasing M causes inflation|prices determine money supply|velocity is always zero
answer: the money supply (M) times velocity (V) equals the price level (P) times transactions (T); increasing M causes inflation
rubric: MV = PT: if V and T are stable, doubling M doubles P — the monetarist view that money supply growth drives inflation.

subject: Economics
stem: Commercial banks create credit (money) through
options: printing notes|the process of lending — a deposit is created when a loan is made, which can be re-deposited and re-lent|selling government bonds|collecting taxes
answer: the process of lending — a deposit is created when a loan is made, which can be re-deposited and re-lent
rubric: Credit creation: banks lend a fraction of deposits; the borrower spends it, it is deposited elsewhere, and re-lent — multiplying money.

subject: Economics
stem: The cash reserve ratio (CRR) is
options: the ratio of loans to deposits|the minimum fraction of deposits a commercial bank must hold as cash reserves with the central bank|interest rate on loans|the ratio of assets to liabilities
answer: the minimum fraction of deposits a commercial bank must hold as cash reserves with the central bank
rubric: CRR set by the CBN: banks must keep this % of deposits in reserve — limits credit creation and controls money supply.

subject: Economics
stem: If the cash reserve ratio is 10%, the money (credit) multiplier is
rubric: Credit multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.10 = 10. A N1,000 deposit supports up to N10,000 of money creation.

subject: Economics
stem: Monetary policy is used by the central bank to
options: set income taxes|control the supply of money and credit in the economy to achieve goals of price stability, full employment and growth|fix wages|manage the stock exchange
answer: control the supply of money and credit in the economy to achieve goals of price stability, full employment and growth
rubric: Monetary policy: CBN uses MPR, CRR, open market operations and liquidity ratio to influence money supply and inflation.

subject: Economics
stem: Open market operations (OMO) involve the central bank
options: printing money|buying and selling government securities (treasury bills, bonds) to expand or contract the money supply|setting interest rates directly|taxing banks
answer: buying and selling government securities (treasury bills, bonds) to expand or contract the money supply
rubric: OMO: CBN buys securities → injects money into economy (expansionary). Sells securities → withdraws money (contractionary).

subject: Economics
stem: The Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) is
options: the rate at which banks lend to customers|the benchmark interest rate at which the CBN lends to commercial banks, influencing all other interest rates|the inflation rate|the exchange rate
answer: the benchmark interest rate at which the CBN lends to commercial banks, influencing all other interest rates
rubric: The MPR (repo rate) is the CBN's signal rate; raising it makes borrowing costlier throughout the economy, reducing inflation.

subject: Economics
stem: Inflation can be caused by
options: a decrease in money supply|excess demand (demand-pull) or rising costs (cost-push) in the economy|falling wages|decreasing government spending
answer: excess demand (demand-pull) or rising costs (cost-push) in the economy
rubric: Demand-pull: too much money chasing too few goods. Cost-push: rising wages or raw material costs push up prices.

subject: Economics
stem: Hyperinflation is
options: a mild rise in prices|extremely rapid and out-of-control inflation that erodes the value of money rapidly (e.g. Zimbabwe 2008)|deflation|a one-time price rise
answer: extremely rapid and out-of-control inflation that erodes the value of money rapidly (e.g. Zimbabwe 2008)
rubric: Hyperinflation: inflation so high that money loses value very quickly; people abandon currency for barter or foreign exchange.

subject: Economics
stem: Deflation is
options: a rise in the price level|a sustained fall in the general price level, which can lead to reduced spending and recession|a fall in the exchange rate|a fall in wages only
answer: a sustained fall in the general price level, which can lead to reduced spending and recession
rubric: Deflation: falling prices discourage spending (buy later when cheaper), reduce profits, increase real debt burden.

subject: Economics
stem: The Liquidity Preference theory (Keynes) states that people demand money for three motives, which are
options: saving, investing and borrowing|transactions, precautionary and speculative motives|earning, spending and taxing|investing, earning and saving
answer: transactions, precautionary and speculative motives
rubric: Keynes: transactions motive (day-to-day spending), precautionary motive (emergencies), speculative motive (hold money vs bonds).

subject: Economics
stem: A high interest rate reduces investment because
options: it encourages saving|borrowing becomes more expensive, raising the cost of capital and discouraging firms from investing|wages fall|exchange rate rises
answer: borrowing becomes more expensive, raising the cost of capital and discouraging firms from investing
rubric: High interest: cost of borrowing rises → firms/consumers borrow less → investment and consumption fall → AD falls.

subject: Economics
stem: The exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another. A depreciation of the naira means
options: the naira buys more foreign currency|the naira buys fewer units of foreign currency (naira has weakened)|exports become cheaper|imports become cheaper
answer: the naira buys fewer units of foreign currency (naira has weakened)
rubric: Depreciation/devaluation: naira weakens → N1 buys fewer dollars → exports cheaper (competitive); imports costlier.

subject: Economics
stem: A fixed exchange rate system means
options: the exchange rate is determined solely by market forces|the government or central bank maintains the currency at a set rate against a reference currency or basket|interest rates are fixed|trade is unrestricted
answer: the government or central bank maintains the currency at a set rate against a reference currency or basket
rubric: Fixed rate: CBN intervenes to buy/sell foreign exchange to maintain the peg; requires large forex reserves.

subject: Economics
stem: A floating exchange rate is determined by
options: government decree|market forces of supply and demand for the currency with no official intervention|only interest rates|trade policy
answer: market forces of supply and demand for the currency with no official intervention
rubric: Floating rate: automatically adjusts to balance of payments positions; no need for large forex reserves.

subject: Economics
stem: M1 (narrow money) includes
options: only coins|currency in circulation plus demand deposits (current accounts) — the most liquid forms of money|all bank deposits including long-term|only government bonds
answer: currency in circulation plus demand deposits (current accounts) — the most liquid forms of money
rubric: M1 is narrow money: coins + notes + sight deposits (current accounts). M2 adds savings/time deposits. M3 adds near money.

subject: Economics
stem: The IMF (International Monetary Fund) assists member countries by
options: providing development grants|offering short-term balance of payments loans and economic policy advice to countries in financial difficulty|managing the stock exchange|setting tariffs
answer: offering short-term balance of payments loans and economic policy advice to countries in financial difficulty
rubric: IMF: lender of last resort for countries with balance of payments crises; provides loans with conditionality (structural reforms).

subject: Economics
stem: Comparative advantage states that a country should specialise in and export goods
options: in which it has an absolute advantage|it can produce at a lower opportunity cost than other countries, even if it is less efficient in absolute terms|that are most expensive|that are taxed
answer: it can produce at a lower opportunity cost than other countries, even if it is less efficient in absolute terms
rubric: Comparative advantage (Ricardo): trade benefits all countries when each specialises in its lowest opportunity cost good.

subject: Economics
stem: The balance of payments (BoP) records
options: a country's national income|all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world over a period|only trade in goods|only government borrowing
answer: all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world over a period
rubric: BoP: current account (goods/services/income/transfers) + capital account + financial account = 0 (in theory).

subject: Economics
stem: The current account of the BoP includes
options: foreign direct investment|trade in goods (visible trade), trade in services (invisible trade), income and current transfers|only exports|stock market transactions
answer: trade in goods (visible trade), trade in services (invisible trade), income and current transfers
rubric: Current account: (1) visible trade, (2) invisible trade, (3) primary income (investment income), (4) secondary income (transfers).

subject: Economics
stem: A current account deficit means
