options: exports exceed imports|a country is importing more goods, services and income than it is exporting; it is spending more than it earns from abroad|the government has a surplus|inflation is low
answer: a country is importing more goods, services and income than it is exporting; it is spending more than it earns from abroad
rubric: Current account deficit: the country owes more to the rest of the world than it earns — must be financed by borrowing or selling assets.

subject: Economics
stem: The financial account of the BoP records
options: only current transfers|flows of investment: foreign direct investment, portfolio investment and reserve asset changes|only exports|government grants
answer: flows of investment: foreign direct investment, portfolio investment and reserve asset changes
rubric: Financial account: how BoP deficits/surpluses are financed — FDI, portfolio flows, loans, reserve movements.

subject: Economics
stem: Foreign direct investment (FDI) refers to
options: short-term portfolio flows|investment where a company establishes or acquires a business with lasting control in another country|government grants|remittances only
answer: investment where a company establishes or acquires a business with lasting control in another country
rubric: FDI: cross-border investment with management control (> 10% ownership threshold). Creates jobs and transfers technology.

subject: Economics
stem: Terms of trade improve when
options: import prices rise relative to export prices|export prices rise relative to import prices — the country can buy more imports per unit of exports|the exchange rate falls|tariffs increase
answer: export prices rise relative to import prices — the country can buy more imports per unit of exports
rubric: Terms of trade index = (export price index / import price index) x 100. Improvement = exports are relatively more valuable.

subject: Economics
stem: Protectionism is the use of trade barriers to
options: increase imports|protect domestic industries from foreign competition by restricting imports|encourage foreign investment|reduce unemployment abroad
answer: protect domestic industries from foreign competition by restricting imports
rubric: Protectionist measures: tariffs, quotas, subsidies to domestic producers, import licences — to favour home industry.

subject: Economics
stem: Free trade promotes efficiency because
options: it protects domestic industries|it allows countries to specialise in comparative advantage goods, increasing global output and consumer welfare|it raises prices|it reduces competition
answer: it allows countries to specialise in comparative advantage goods, increasing global output and consumer welfare
rubric: Free trade: removes barriers, allows specialisation, lower prices, greater variety, technology transfer and economies of scale.

subject: Economics
stem: A devaluation of the exchange rate is expected to improve the current account by
options: making imports cheaper and exports dearer|making exports cheaper (more competitive) and imports dearer (reducing import demand)|increasing inflation only|reducing FDI
answer: making exports cheaper (more competitive) and imports dearer (reducing import demand)
rubric: Devaluation: export prices fall in foreign currency (demand rises); import prices rise in domestic currency (demand falls).

subject: Economics
stem: The J-curve effect describes
options: how GDP rises immediately after devaluation|why a devaluation initially worsens the current account before improving it, due to inelastic demand in the short run|why imports are always elastic|why exports never respond to price
answer: why a devaluation initially worsens the current account before improving it, due to inelastic demand in the short run
rubric: J-curve: short-run contracts are fixed in currency; the worsening trade balance forms the bottom of the J before improving.

subject: Economics
stem: The Marshall-Lerner condition states that
options: devaluation always improves the trade balance|devaluation will improve the current account only if the sum of the price elasticities of demand for exports and imports exceeds one|tariffs always work|quotas are better than tariffs
answer: devaluation will improve the current account only if the sum of the price elasticities of demand for exports and imports exceeds one
rubric: If PED exports + PED imports > 1, devaluation improves the trade balance in the long run.

subject: Economics
stem: Nigeria's main export is
options: agricultural goods|crude oil (petroleum), which accounts for the largest share of export revenues|gold|manufactured goods
answer: crude oil (petroleum), which accounts for the largest share of export revenues
rubric: Nigeria is heavily dependent on crude oil exports; this creates vulnerability to oil price fluctuations.

subject: Economics
stem: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) aims to
options: increase tariffs among African nations|create a single continental market by removing tariffs and trade barriers among African countries|limit trade to certain African countries|promote trade only with Europe
answer: create a single continental market by removing tariffs and trade barriers among African countries
rubric: AfCFTA (operational 2021): aims to boost intra-African trade, industrialisation and economic integration across 54 countries.

subject: Economics
stem: An ad valorem tariff is a tax on imports charged as
options: a fixed amount per unit|a percentage of the value of the imported good|a quantity limit|a ban
answer: a percentage of the value of the imported good
rubric: Ad valorem tariff: calculated as a % of import value (e.g. 20% of CIF price). Specific tariff: fixed amount per unit.

subject: Economics
stem: Capital flight refers to
options: investment in home country|the rapid movement of money out of a country due to political or economic instability, leading to currency depreciation|foreign direct investment|migration
answer: the rapid movement of money out of a country due to political or economic instability, leading to currency depreciation
rubric: Capital flight: investors/wealthy individuals move funds abroad quickly, worsening the BoP and weakening the currency.

subject: Economics
stem: Workers' remittances from Nigerians abroad are recorded in the BoP under
options: current account — as secondary income (current transfers)|capital account — as FDI|financial account|trade in goods
answer: current account — as secondary income (current transfers)
rubric: Remittances: transfers of income by migrant workers to their home country; recorded as secondary income in the current account.

subject: Economics
stem: The World Bank primarily provides
options: short-term balance of payments loans|long-term development finance (loans and grants) to developing countries for infrastructure, education and poverty reduction|insurance|trade arbitration
answer: long-term development finance (loans and grants) to developing countries for infrastructure, education and poverty reduction
rubric: World Bank (IBRD, IDA): funds long-term development projects in low- and middle-income countries.

subject: Economics
stem: Exchange rate appreciation means
options: a weakening of the currency|the currency buys more units of foreign currency (strengthens), making imports cheaper and exports dearer|inflation rises|trade balance improves immediately
answer: the currency buys more units of foreign currency (strengthens), making imports cheaper and exports dearer
rubric: Appreciation: naira strengthens → N1 buys more dollars → imports cheaper (demand rises), exports costlier (demand falls).

subject: Economics
stem: The principle of absolute advantage states that a country has an absolute advantage when
options: it has the lowest opportunity cost|it can produce a good using fewer resources (more efficiently) than another country in absolute terms|it has a large population|it trades freely
answer: it can produce a good using fewer resources (more efficiently) than another country in absolute terms
rubric: Absolute advantage (Adam Smith): country A produces more of a good than country B with the same resources.

subject: Economics
stem: Economic development is a broader concept than economic growth because
options: development excludes GDP|development refers to improvements in living standards, quality of life, poverty reduction, equity and capabilities — beyond just rising GDP|development is measured only by GDP|growth includes non-economic factors
answer: development refers to improvements in living standards, quality of life, poverty reduction, equity and capabilities — beyond just rising GDP
rubric: Economic growth: increase in real GDP. Development: structural transformation, better health, education, reduced poverty and inequality.

subject: Economics
stem: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite measure that combines
options: only GDP per capita|income (GNI per capita), education (years of schooling) and health (life expectancy) to measure development|only life expectancy|trade and investment only
answer: income (GNI per capita), education (years of schooling) and health (life expectancy) to measure development
rubric: HDI (UNDP): broader welfare measure than GDP alone; scores from 0 to 1 across three dimensions.

subject: Economics
stem: Sustainable development is defined as
options: maximising current economic growth|meeting the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs|using all resources now|expanding production regardless of environmental impact
answer: meeting the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
rubric: Brundtland definition (WCED 1987): sustainable development balances economic, social and environmental goals across time.

subject: Economics
stem: Population growth can be both a boon and a challenge for developing nations because
options: more people always means more poverty|it expands the labour force and consumer market (boon) but may strain resources and infrastructure (challenge)|it has no effect on the economy|it only reduces GDP
answer: it expands the labour force and consumer market (boon) but may strain resources and infrastructure (challenge)
rubric: High population: more workers and consumers, but also more to educate, employ and feed — it depends on the economic structure.

subject: Economics
stem: The dependency ratio measures
options: the ratio of exports to imports|the proportion of the non-working population (young + elderly) relative to the working-age population|the ratio of savings to investment|the ratio of debt to GDP
answer: the proportion of the non-working population (young + elderly) relative to the working-age population
rubric: Dependency ratio = (population under 15 + over 65) / working-age population. High ratio = high burden on workers.

subject: Economics
stem: Rural-urban migration in Nigeria is primarily driven by
options: better rural wages|the perceived higher wages, better services and economic opportunities in cities (push-pull factors)|only political reasons|declining urban populations
answer: the perceived higher wages, better services and economic opportunities in cities (push-pull factors)
rubric: Todaro model: people migrate if the expected urban wage (adjusted for probability of employment) exceeds rural income.

subject: Economics
stem: Absolute poverty is defined as
options: having less than others|lacking the income or resources to meet basic minimum needs for food, shelter and clothing|relative deprivation|temporary unemployment
answer: lacking the income or resources to meet basic minimum needs for food, shelter and clothing
rubric: Absolute poverty: failing to meet a fixed standard of basic needs. World Bank line: < US$2.15/day (2022 update).

subject: Economics
stem: A population pyramid with a wide base (many young people) and narrow top (few elderly) is characteristic of a country with
options: low birth rate and high life expectancy|high birth rate, high death rate and rapid population growth — typical of developing nations|stable population|falling population
answer: high birth rate, high death rate and rapid population growth — typical of developing nations
rubric: Expansive pyramid: wide base = many births, narrow top = low life expectancy — typical of low-income developing countries.

subject: Economics
stem: The demographic transition model describes how countries move through stages of population change. In Stage 2, what happens?
options: Birth rate falls, death rate falls|Birth rate remains high but death rate falls due to improved medicine and food, causing rapid population growth|Both rates are low|Death rate is higher than birth rate
answer: Birth rate remains high but death rate falls due to improved medicine and food, causing rapid population growth
rubric: Stage 2: Death rate falls (hygiene, medicine, food) while birth rate stays high → rapid natural population growth.

subject: Economics
stem: Urbanisation is the process whereby
options: people move from cities to rural areas|an increasing proportion of a country's population lives in urban (city) areas|birth rates fall|industry moves to rural areas
answer: an increasing proportion of a country's population lives in urban (city) areas
rubric: Urbanisation: driven by rural-urban migration and natural urban population growth; Nigeria is rapidly urbanising.

subject: Economics
stem: Foreign aid can assist developing economies by
options: creating dependency only|providing capital, technical expertise and humanitarian relief that supplements domestic resources|replacing trade|reducing exports
answer: providing capital, technical expertise and humanitarian relief that supplements domestic resources
rubric: Aid (bilateral, multilateral, NGO) finances infrastructure, health, education and disaster relief — complementing domestic savings.

subject: Economics
stem: The vicious cycle of poverty describes how
options: rich nations become richer|low incomes lead to low savings, low investment, low productivity and continued low incomes — trapping countries in poverty|population growth eliminates poverty|aid breaks all poverty traps
answer: low incomes lead to low savings, low investment, low productivity and continued low incomes — trapping countries in poverty
rubric: Vicious cycle: Low income → Low saving → Low investment → Low capital → Low productivity → Low income (self-reinforcing).

subject: Economics
stem: Primary commodity dependence is a challenge for many developing nations because
options: commodity prices are always stable|commodity prices are volatile and tend to decline relative to manufactured goods (Prebisch-Singer thesis), causing terms of trade to worsen|commodities are always scarce|primary goods earn more than manufactured goods always
answer: commodity prices are volatile and tend to decline relative to manufactured goods (Prebisch-Singer thesis), causing terms of trade to worsen
rubric: Developing economies relying on agriculture/minerals face price volatility and long-run deteriorating terms of trade.

subject: Economics
stem: Structural adjustment programmes (SAPs) recommended by the IMF and World Bank typically include
options: increasing government spending without limit|privatisation, trade liberalisation, currency devaluation and cuts to government subsidies|protectionism|wage increases
answer: privatisation, trade liberalisation, currency devaluation and cuts to government subsidies
rubric: SAPs: market-oriented reforms aimed at macroeconomic stabilisation; controversial due to social costs of subsidy removal and austerity.

subject: Economics
stem: Brain drain refers to
options: import of technology|the emigration of highly educated and skilled workers from a developing country to developed nations, depleting local human capital|rural-urban migration only|a fall in literacy rates
answer: the emigration of highly educated and skilled workers from a developing country to developed nations, depleting local human capital
rubric: Brain drain: Nigeria loses doctors, engineers and academics to the UK, USA and Canada — reducing domestic productivity.

subject: Economics
stem: Natural rate of population increase is calculated as
options: total population / area|Birth rate minus Death rate (ignoring migration)|Immigration minus Emigration|Birth rate plus Death rate
answer: Birth rate minus Death rate (ignoring migration)
rubric: Natural increase = crude birth rate - crude death rate. Positive value means population is growing naturally.

subject: Economics
stem: Microfinance institutions contribute to development by
options: only serving large corporations|providing small loans, savings and insurance to low-income individuals and small enterprises excluded from formal banking|replacing commercial banks|paying government taxes
answer: providing small loans, savings and insurance to low-income individuals and small enterprises excluded from formal banking
rubric: Microfinance (pioneered by Grameen Bank) increases financial inclusion, empowering entrepreneurs in developing nations.

subject: Economics
stem: Optimum population is the population size at which
options: output is minimised|output per head is maximised, given the available resources and technology|resources are exhausted|migration stops
answer: output per head is maximised, given the available resources and technology
rubric: Optimum population: the theoretical size where GDP per capita is highest. Overpopulated = beyond optimum; underpopulated = below.

subject: Economics
stem: The Gini coefficient measures
options: GDP per capita|the degree of income inequality in an economy (0 = perfect equality; 1 = maximum inequality)|the inflation rate|the level of unemployment
answer: the degree of income inequality in an economy (0 = perfect equality; 1 = maximum inequality)
rubric: Gini coefficient: derived from the Lorenz curve; higher Gini = more unequal income distribution.

subject: Economics
stem: Industrialisation is seen as a key strategy for economic development because
options: it focuses on agriculture|it creates higher-value-added jobs, increases productivity, diversifies the economy and reduces dependence on primary commodities|it increases unemployment|it reduces exports
answer: it creates higher-value-added jobs, increases productivity, diversifies the economy and reduces dependence on primary commodities
rubric: Industrialisation: structural transformation from agriculture to manufacturing and services → higher wages, productivity and growth.

subject: Economics
stem: A government budget is described as expansionary (reflationary) when
options: taxes rise and spending falls|government spending exceeds tax revenue (a deficit budget), injecting money into the economy to stimulate aggregate demand|the budget is balanced|taxes equal spending
answer: government spending exceeds tax revenue (a deficit budget), injecting money into the economy to stimulate aggregate demand
rubric: Expansionary fiscal policy: G > T (deficit) → increased AD → higher output and employment. Used in recession.

subject: Economics
stem: A contractionary (deflationary) fiscal policy involves
options: cutting taxes and raising spending|raising taxes and/or reducing government spending to reduce aggregate demand and combat inflation|maintaining a balanced budget|increasing money supply
answer: raising taxes and/or reducing government spending to reduce aggregate demand and combat inflation
rubric: Contractionary fiscal policy: T > G (surplus) → reduced AD → lower inflation. Risks slowing growth.

subject: Economics
stem: A progressive tax is one where
options: everyone pays the same amount|the average tax rate rises as income rises (higher earners pay a higher proportion)|the average tax rate falls as income rises|everyone pays the same proportion
answer: the average tax rate rises as income rises (higher earners pay a higher proportion)
rubric: Progressive tax (e.g. personal income tax with brackets): redistributes income; higher earners pay a larger % of income.

subject: Economics
stem: A regressive tax takes a
options: larger proportion of income from higher earners|larger proportion of income from lower earners (as income rises, the proportion paid falls)|equal proportion from all|fixed amount from all
answer: larger proportion of income from lower earners (as income rises, the proportion paid falls)
rubric: Regressive tax (e.g. VAT on necessities): lower-income households spend a higher proportion of income on it.

subject: Economics
stem: A proportional (flat) tax charges
options: different rates at different income levels|the same percentage (rate) of income at all income levels|a fixed amount regardless of income|only high earners
answer: the same percentage (rate) of income at all income levels
rubric: Proportional tax: everyone pays the same %, e.g. 20% flat income tax. Average rate = marginal rate throughout.

subject: Economics
stem: National debt (public debt) is the total
options: annual tax revenue|accumulated debt owed by the government from past borrowing|national savings|annual government spending
answer: accumulated debt owed by the government from past borrowing
rubric: National debt = total outstanding borrowing by the government; differs from annual budget deficit (flow vs stock).

subject: Economics
stem: The main sources of government revenue include
options: only income tax|taxes (direct and indirect), oil revenue, grants, profits from public enterprises and borrowing|only VAT|only oil revenue
answer: taxes (direct and indirect), oil revenue, grants, profits from public enterprises and borrowing
rubric: Nigeria's government revenue: petroleum profit tax, oil revenue, company income tax, VAT, customs duties, grants.

subject: Economics
stem: VAT (Value Added Tax) is an example of an
options: direct tax on income|indirect tax on consumption of goods and services|wealth tax|capital gains tax
answer: indirect tax on consumption of goods and services
rubric: VAT is indirect: levied on the value added at each production stage, ultimately paid by the final consumer.

subject: Economics
stem: The Laffer curve illustrates the relationship between
options: supply and demand|tax rates and total tax revenue — suggesting that at very high rates, raising tax rates further reduces total revenue|inflation and unemployment|exchange rates and trade
answer: tax rates and total tax revenue — suggesting that at very high rates, raising tax rates further reduces total revenue
rubric: Laffer curve: at 0% or 100% tax rate, revenue = 0. At some optimal rate, revenue is maximised; beyond that, disincentives reduce revenue.

subject: Economics
stem: Crowding out occurs when
options: government spending boosts private investment|increased government borrowing raises interest rates, thereby reducing private sector investment|taxes fall|exports increase
answer: increased government borrowing raises interest rates, thereby reducing private sector investment
rubric: Crowding out: government borrowing competes with private sector for loanable funds → higher interest rates → less private investment.

subject: Economics
stem: Automatic stabilisers are fiscal mechanisms that
options: require government action each time|automatically moderate economic fluctuations without discretionary policy changes (e.g. unemployment benefits rise in recession, tax revenue falls)|increase debt automatically|are set by the central bank
answer: automatically moderate economic fluctuations without discretionary policy changes (e.g. unemployment benefits rise in recession, tax revenue falls)
rubric: Automatic stabilisers (progressive taxes, social spending): expand in recession (stimulate AD) and contract in boom (dampen inflation).

subject: Economics
stem: Supply-side policies aim to
options: increase aggregate demand|increase the productive capacity of the economy by improving efficiency, incentives and flexibility (e.g. deregulation, privatisation, education, labour market reforms)|control inflation by reducing money supply|raise taxes
answer: increase the productive capacity of the economy by improving efficiency, incentives and flexibility (e.g. deregulation, privatisation, education, labour market reforms)
rubric: Supply-side policies shift the AS curve rightward: expand potential output, reduce structural unemployment and inflation.

subject: Economics
stem: The Nigerian government's SURE-P and similar conditional cash transfer programmes are examples of
options: trade policy|social protection programmes targeting poverty reduction among vulnerable groups|monetary policy|environmental policy
answer: social protection programmes targeting poverty reduction among vulnerable groups
rubric: Conditional cash transfers provide money to poor households contingent on behaviours like school attendance or health checks.

subject: Economics
stem: Government expenditure on education and health is justified economically because
options: they are luxury services|they generate positive externalities and increase human capital, boosting long-term productivity and growth|they are purely consumption goods|they benefit only the wealthy
answer: they generate positive externalities and increase human capital, boosting long-term productivity and growth
rubric: Education and health raise worker productivity (human capital); the social return exceeds the private return — justifying government provision.

subject: Economics
stem: The Fiscal Responsibility Act in Nigeria requires the government to
options: run a surplus always|maintain fiscal discipline, including setting limits on the fiscal deficit and expenditure levels|abolish all taxes|privatise all public enterprises
answer: maintain fiscal discipline, including setting limits on the fiscal deficit and expenditure levels
rubric: Fiscal Responsibility Act (2007): promotes transparency and accountability in government budgeting and public expenditure management.

subject: Government
stem: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was significant because it
options: introduced the elective principle|granted full independence to Nigeria|abolished the legislative council|established a federal system
answer: introduced the elective principle
rubric: The Clifford Constitution introduced elected representation to the Lagos and Calabar legislative councils.

subject: Government
stem: Which constitution introduced the federal system of government in Nigeria?
options: Richards Constitution 1946|Macpherson Constitution 1951|Lyttleton Constitution 1954|Clifford Constitution 1922
answer: Lyttleton Constitution 1954
rubric: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 formally established federalism in Nigeria.

subject: Government
stem: The Richards Constitution of 1946 was notable for
options: creating three regional groupings|granting women the right to vote|establishing the Supreme Court|creating the Senate
answer: creating three regional groupings
rubric: Richards divided Nigeria into Northern, Western and Eastern regions.

subject: Government
stem: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 introduced
options: a bicameral legislature at the center|direct elections nationwide|a unitary system|complete Nigerian self-rule
answer: a bicameral legislature at the center
rubric: The Macpherson Constitution established a House of Representatives and a Senate at the federal level.

subject: Government
stem: Nigeria became a republic in
rubric: Nigeria became a republic on October 1, 1963, replacing the Queen as head of state with a President.

subject: Government
stem: The 1979 constitution introduced a
options: presidential system|parliamentary system|military rule|confederal system
answer: presidential system
rubric: The 1979 constitution adopted a presidential system modeled partly on the United States.

subject: Government
stem: Nigeria gained independence from Britain on
options: October 1, 1960|January 1, 1960|October 1, 1963|October 1, 1979
answer: October 1, 1960
rubric: Nigeria attained independence on October 1, 1960.

subject: Government
stem: The CFRN 1999 was promulgated under the military administration of
options: Abdulsalami Abubakar|Sani Abacha|Ibrahim Babangida|Olusegun Obasanjo
answer: Abdulsalami Abubakar
rubric: The 1999 Constitution was promulgated by the Abdulsalami Abubakar administration before handing over to civilians.

subject: Government
stem: Which of these is the supreme law of Nigeria?
options: The Constitution|An Act of the National Assembly|Presidential Orders|Military Decrees
answer: The Constitution
rubric: The Constitution is the supreme law; every other law derives its validity from it.

subject: Government
stem: The Arthur Richards Constitution was enacted in
rubric: The Richards Constitution was enacted in 1946.

subject: Government
stem: Exclusive legislative list items can only be legislated upon by the
options: Federal Government|State Governments|Local Government Councils|Any tier of government
answer: Federal Government
rubric: Items on the Exclusive List are within the exclusive legislative competence of the National Assembly.

subject: Government
stem: Concurrent legislative list items can be legislated by
options: Both federal and state governments|Only the federal government|Only state governments|Local governments only
answer: Both federal and state governments
rubric: Both the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly can legislate on concurrent list items.

subject: Government
stem: The concept of fundamental human rights in Nigeria is enshrined in
options: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution|Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution|The Electoral Act|The Criminal Code
answer: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution
rubric: Chapter IV of the 1999 CFRN contains provisions on fundamental human rights.

subject: Government
stem: Which body has the power to interpret the Nigerian Constitution?
options: The Supreme Court|The National Assembly|The Executive|The Federal Executive Council
answer: The Supreme Court
rubric: The judiciary, particularly the Supreme Court, has the power of constitutional interpretation.

subject: Government
stem: Constitutional amendment in Nigeria requires
options: Two-thirds majority of the National Assembly and majority of State Houses|Simple majority in the National Assembly|Presidential decree|Referendum only
answer: Two-thirds majority of the National Assembly and majority of State Houses
rubric: Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution requires a two-thirds majority plus approval by at least 24 state assemblies.

subject: Government
stem: The 1963 Republican Constitution was based largely on the
options: 1960 Independence Constitution|Lyttleton Constitution 1954|Macpherson Constitution 1951|Richards Constitution 1946
answer: 1960 Independence Constitution
rubric: The 1963 Republican Constitution retained most of the 1960 structure, replacing the monarchy with a republic.

subject: Government
stem: Which principle ensures no single arm of government becomes too powerful?
options: Separation of powers|Supremacy of the constitution|Federalism|Rule of law
answer: Separation of powers
rubric: Separation of powers divides government into legislature, executive and judiciary to prevent abuse.

subject: Government
stem: The principle that government officials must act within the law is called
options: Rule of law|Federalism|Separation of powers|Constitutionalism
answer: Rule of law
rubric: Rule of law means everyone, including the government, is subject to the law.

subject: Government
stem: Judicial review in Nigeria means the courts can
options: declare government actions unconstitutional|make laws|appoint ministers|veto the president
answer: declare government actions unconstitutional
rubric: Judicial review allows courts to strike down laws or actions that violate the constitution.

subject: Government
stem: The preamble to the Nigerian constitution declares Nigeria a
options: Federal Republic|Unitary State|Confederation|Monarchy
answer: Federal Republic
rubric: The preamble affirms Nigeria as one indivisible and indissoluble sovereign nation under God as a Federal Republic.

subject: Government
stem: The Nigerian National Assembly consists of
options: The Senate and House of Representatives|The Senate only|The House of Representatives only|The House of Assembly and Senate
answer: The Senate and House of Representatives
rubric: The National Assembly is bicameral, comprising the Senate and the House of Representatives.

subject: Government
stem: How many senators represent each state in the Nigerian Senate?
options: Three|Two|Four|One
answer: Three
rubric: Each of the 36 states is represented by three senators, plus one senator for the FCT.

subject: Government
stem: The total number of seats in the Nigerian Senate is
rubric: The Senate has 109 seats: 3 per state (36×3=108) plus 1 for the FCT.

subject: Government
stem: The primary function of the legislature is to
options: Make laws|Execute laws|Interpret laws|Appoint ministers
answer: Make laws
rubric: The legislature makes, amends and repeals laws.

subject: Government
stem: A bill becomes law after
options: Presidential assent|Third reading in the House only|Senate approval only|Approval by the courts
answer: Presidential assent
rubric: A bill passed by both chambers must receive presidential assent to become an Act.

subject: Government
stem: The speaker of the House of Representatives presides over
options: The House of Representatives|The Senate|The National Assembly joint session|The Electoral Commission
answer: The House of Representatives
rubric: The Speaker is the presiding officer of the House of Representatives.

subject: Government
stem: The Senate President is elected by
options: Members of the Senate|The President|The National Assembly jointly|Nigerians directly
answer: Members of the Senate
rubric: The Senate elects its own President from among its members.

subject: Government
stem: Oversight function of the legislature refers to
options: Monitoring the executive|Making foreign policy|Interpreting statutes|Appointing judges
answer: Monitoring the executive
rubric: Legislature oversight involves scrutinizing executive actions, budget implementation, and policy execution.

subject: Government
stem: Appropriation bills that deal with public spending must originate from
options: The House of Representatives|The Senate|Either chamber|The Presidency
answer: The House of Representatives
rubric: Money bills must originate from the House of Representatives under the 1999 Constitution.

subject: Government
stem: A bicameral legislature has
options: Two chambers|One chamber|Three chambers|No fixed number
answer: Two chambers
rubric: A bicameral legislature has an upper and lower house.

subject: Government
stem: The term of office of a Nigerian Senator is
options: Four years|Six years|Five years|Two years
answer: Four years
rubric: Senators serve four-year terms, renewable.

subject: Government
stem: A quorum for a sitting of the Nigerian National Assembly is
options: One-third of members|Half of members|Two-thirds of members|All members
answer: One-third of members
rubric: A quorum for National Assembly business is one-third of members.

subject: Government
stem: Legislative immunity protects lawmakers from
options: Civil or criminal proceedings for speeches in the house|All criminal charges anywhere|Tax liabilities|Military service
answer: Civil or criminal proceedings for speeches in the house
rubric: Lawmakers enjoy immunity from legal proceedings for anything said or done during legislative proceedings.

subject: Government
stem: Which of these is NOT a way a bill can be initiated?
options: By the President directly|By a member of the National Assembly|By a committee report|As a government bill
answer: By the President directly
rubric: Bills are introduced by legislators; the executive influences legislation through ministers or liaison but does not directly introduce bills.

subject: Government
stem: Conference committee in the legislature is set up to
options: Resolve differences between two chambers on a bill|Impeach the president|Approve the national budget|Conduct elections
answer: Resolve differences between two chambers on a bill
rubric: A conference committee harmonizes conflicting versions of a bill passed by the two chambers.

subject: Government
stem: The power of the legislature to investigate public officials is derived from
options: Section 82 of the 1999 Constitution|The Criminal Code|Presidential directive|INEC guidelines
answer: Section 82 of the 1999 Constitution
rubric: The power of investigation is a constitutional oversight function of the legislature.

subject: Government
stem: A private member bill is a bill sponsored by
options: An individual legislator not on behalf of government|The President|The Senate President|A minister
answer: An individual legislator not on behalf of government
rubric: Private member bills are introduced by individual legislators, as distinct from government bills.

subject: Government
stem: Unicameral legislature refers to a parliament with
options: One chamber|Two chambers|Three chambers|A rotating chamber
answer: One chamber
rubric: A unicameral legislature has only one legislative chamber.

subject: Government
stem: The House of Representatives has how many seats?
rubric: The House of Representatives has 360 seats.

subject: Government
stem: Impeachment proceedings against the President begin in
options: The House of Representatives|The Senate|The Supreme Court|INEC
answer: The House of Representatives
rubric: Impeachment proceedings are initiated in the House of Representatives.

subject: Government
stem: The chief executive of Nigeria is the
options: President|Senate President|Prime Minister|Chief Justice
answer: President
rubric: The President is the head of state and chief executive of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

subject: Government
stem: The Vice President of Nigeria is elected by
options: Being on the same ticket as the President|The National Assembly|The Senate|Direct election separately
answer: Being on the same ticket as the President
rubric: The Vice President runs on a joint ticket with the presidential candidate.

subject: Government
stem: The Federal Executive Council of Nigeria comprises
options: The President, Vice President and ministers|The President alone|All elected officials|The President and Governor
answer: The President, Vice President and ministers
rubric: The FEC is chaired by the President and includes the VP and ministers.

subject: Government
stem: The primary function of the executive arm is to
options: Implement laws|Make laws|Interpret laws|Conduct elections
answer: Implement laws
rubric: The executive arm implements and enforces laws made by the legislature.

subject: Government
stem: Presidential assent refers to
options: The President signing a bill into law|The President voting in elections|The President addressing the National Assembly|The President swearing in ministers
answer: The President signing a bill into law
rubric: Presidential assent is the act of the President approving and signing a bill into law.

subject: Government
stem: The power to pardon convicted persons in Nigeria belongs to the
options: President|Chief Justice|Attorney General|Senate President
answer: President
rubric: The President exercises the power of pardon (prerogative of mercy) on the advice of the Council of State.

subject: Government
stem: Ministers in Nigeria are confirmed by
options: The Senate|The House of Representatives|The Supreme Court|INEC
answer: The Senate
rubric: Ministerial nominations by the President must be confirmed by the Senate.

subject: Government
stem: The maximum number of presidential terms in Nigeria is
options: Two terms of four years|Three terms|One term of six years|Unlimited terms
answer: Two terms of four years
rubric: The Nigerian Constitution limits the President to a maximum of two terms of four years each.

subject: Government
stem: State governors are the chief executives of their states and are elected for
options: Four-year terms renewable once|Six-year terms|Four-year terms with no limit|Two-year terms
answer: Four-year terms renewable once
rubric: Governors serve four-year terms and may be re-elected for one additional term.

subject: Government
stem: The executive arm can check the legislature through
options: The power of veto|Judicial review|Impeachment|Oversight hearings
answer: The power of veto
rubric: The President can withhold assent (veto) a bill passed by the National Assembly.

subject: Government
stem: State security service, police and military answer ultimately to the
options: President as Commander-in-Chief|Senate President|Chief Justice|Governor
answer: President as Commander-in-Chief
rubric: The President is the Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces and heads the security architecture.

subject: Government
stem: The State House of Assembly corresponds at the state level to
options: The National Assembly|The Senate|The House of Representatives|The Federal Executive Council
answer: The National Assembly
rubric: The State House of Assembly is the legislative body at the state level, equivalent to the National Assembly at the federal level.

subject: Government
stem: Cabinet system of government means ministers are
options: Collectively responsible to the legislature|Individually responsible only|Appointed for life|Elected separately
answer: Collectively responsible to the legislature
rubric: In a cabinet system, ministers are collectively responsible and resign collectively if the cabinet loses confidence.

subject: Government
stem: The Attorney General of the Federation is the
options: Chief law officer of the Federation|Head of the judiciary|Speaker of the House|Senate President
answer: Chief law officer of the Federation
rubric: The AGF is the principal legal adviser to the Federal Government.

subject: Government
stem: An executive order is
options: A directive issued by the President with immediate effect|A bill passed by the legislature|A court ruling|A constitutional amendment
answer: A directive issued by the President with immediate effect
rubric: Executive orders are directives issued by the President in the exercise of executive authority.

subject: Government
stem: Delegated legislation means
options: Subsidiary laws made by the executive|Laws made by the legislature|Constitutional amendments|International treaties
answer: Subsidiary laws made by the executive
rubric: Delegated (or subsidiary) legislation is made by the executive under powers delegated by the legislature.

subject: Government
stem: The National Economic Council is chaired by the
options: Vice President|President|Senate President|Finance Minister
answer: Vice President
rubric: The National Economic Council is chaired by the Vice President and includes all state governors.

subject: Government
stem: Which body advises the President on the exercise of the prerogative of mercy?
options: Council of State|National Security Council|Federal Executive Council|INEC
answer: Council of State
rubric: The Council of State advises on prerogatives of mercy, award of national honours, and similar matters.

subject: Government
stem: The power to declare a state of emergency in Nigeria rests with
options: The President, subject to National Assembly approval|The Governor alone|The Chief Justice|The Army Chief
answer: The President, subject to National Assembly approval
rubric: The President may proclaim a state of emergency, which must be approved by the National Assembly.

subject: Government
stem: The Presidency refers to
options: The President and all staff of the executive office|Only the President|The Cabinet|The Senate
answer: The President and all staff of the executive office
rubric: The Presidency encompasses the President, Vice President and all offices in the executive arm.

subject: Government
stem: The highest court in Nigeria is the
options: Supreme Court|Court of Appeal|Federal High Court|Sharia Court
answer: Supreme Court
rubric: The Supreme Court is the apex court in Nigeria.

subject: Government
stem: The Chief Justice of Nigeria is the head of
options: The Supreme Court|The Court of Appeal|The Federal High Court|The National Judicial Council
answer: The Supreme Court
rubric: The Chief Justice of Nigeria presides over the Supreme Court.

subject: Government
stem: Judicial independence means
options: The judiciary operates free from executive and legislative interference|Judges are elected by the public|The judiciary makes laws|The President appoints all judges
answer: The judiciary operates free from executive and legislative interference
rubric: Judicial independence safeguards the impartiality of courts by protecting them from undue influence.

subject: Government
stem: The function of the judiciary is to
options: Interpret and apply the law|Make laws|Implement government policy|Collect taxes
answer: Interpret and apply the law
rubric: The judiciary interprets the law and adjudicates disputes.

subject: Government
stem: Customary courts in Nigeria handle cases relating to
options: Customary law and traditions|Constitutional matters|Federal tax disputes|Criminal appeals
answer: Customary law and traditions
rubric: Customary courts apply indigenous customary law to resolve disputes among those who subscribe to it.

subject: Government
stem: The Court of Appeal in Nigeria hears
options: Appeals from the Federal and State High Courts|First instance criminal cases|Impeachment matters|Electoral commission disputes only
answer: Appeals from the Federal and State High Courts
rubric: The Court of Appeal is an intermediate appellate court above the high courts.

subject: Government
stem: Habeas corpus is a legal order that requires
options: A detained person to be brought before a court|The police to arrest a suspect|A minister to appear before the legislature|A court to review a statute
answer: A detained person to be brought before a court
rubric: Habeas corpus protects against unlawful detention by compelling the detaining authority to justify the detention.

subject: Government
stem: An injunction is a court order that
options: Restrains a party from taking a particular action|Imprisons a convicted person|Transfers a case to a higher court|Pardons a convict
answer: Restrains a party from taking a particular action
rubric: An injunction is an equitable remedy that stops or compels an action.

subject: Government
stem: The doctrine of precedent (stare decisis) means
options: Lower courts must follow earlier decisions of higher courts|All courts make independent decisions|The Supreme Court follows lower court decisions|Parliament overrides all court decisions
answer: Lower courts must follow earlier decisions of higher courts
rubric: Stare decisis ensures consistency and predictability in the law.

subject: Government
stem: The National Judicial Council is responsible for
options: Recommending judicial appointments and discipline|Making legislation|Conducting elections|Advising on foreign policy
answer: Recommending judicial appointments and discipline
rubric: The NJC manages judicial appointments, promotions and discipline across the federation.

subject: Government
stem: A magistrate court handles
options: Less serious criminal and civil matters|Constitutional interpretation|Death sentence cases|International disputes
answer: Less serious criminal and civil matters
rubric: Magistrate courts deal with petty offences and minor civil disputes.

subject: Government
stem: Certiorari is a writ that
options: Calls up records from a lower court for review|Releases a person from custody|Compels a public officer to perform a duty|Transfers property
answer: Calls up records from a lower court for review
rubric: Certiorari is used to review and quash decisions of lower courts or tribunals.

subject: Government
stem: The principle of nemo judex in causa sua means
options: No one should be a judge in their own case|Everyone is equal before the law|The accused is innocent until proven guilty|The law must be certain
answer: No one should be a judge in their own case
rubric: This natural justice rule requires that a judge be impartial and have no personal interest in the matter.

subject: Government
stem: The presumption of innocence means
options: An accused is innocent until proven guilty|The police can detain anyone|Confessions alone are sufficient for conviction|Witnesses need not appear in court
answer: An accused is innocent until proven guilty
rubric: The presumption of innocence is a fundamental fair trial right.

subject: Government
stem: The Federal High Court has jurisdiction over
options: Federal government matters and revenue cases|All state matters|Electoral offences only|Sharia law
answer: Federal government matters and revenue cases
rubric: The Federal High Court handles cases involving the federal government, federal revenue, admiralty and similar matters.

subject: Government
stem: Security of tenure for judges means
options: Judges cannot be removed except through a prescribed process|Judges serve only one year|The President can remove any judge|Judges are elected
answer: Judges cannot be removed except through a prescribed process
rubric: Security of tenure protects judicial independence by preventing arbitrary removal of judges.

subject: Government
stem: Judicial activism refers to
options: Courts interpreting the law broadly to address social needs|Courts refusing to hear cases|Judges campaigning for office|The legislature appointing judges
answer: Courts interpreting the law broadly to address social needs
rubric: Judicial activism involves courts taking a proactive role in interpreting the constitution to advance rights.

subject: Government
stem: The Sharia Court of Appeal in Northern Nigeria handles
options: Appeals in Islamic personal law matters|Federal criminal matters|Constitutional cases|All civil cases
answer: Appeals in Islamic personal law matters
rubric: The Sharia Court of Appeal has jurisdiction over Islamic personal law matters in Northern states.

subject: Government
stem: Locus standi refers to
options: The right of a party to bring a matter before the court|The location of the court|Judicial precedent|The duration of a court session
answer: The right of a party to bring a matter before the court
rubric: Locus standi determines who has sufficient interest to commence proceedings in court.

subject: Government
stem: An election petition tribunal in Nigeria handles
options: Disputes arising from elections|Criminal cases|Revenue disputes|Human rights cases
answer: Disputes arising from elections
rubric: Election petition tribunals adjudicate challenges to the results of elections.

subject: Government
stem: Federalism is a system of government in which
options: Power is divided between central and state governments|All power resides at the centre|State governments have no power|Local governments control everything
answer: Power is divided between central and state governments
rubric: Federalism distributes sovereign powers between national and subnational governments.

subject: Government
stem: Nigeria operates a
options: Federal system|Unitary system|Confederate system|Presidential unitary system
answer: Federal system
rubric: Nigeria is a federal state with three tiers: federal, state and local government.

subject: Government
stem: The residual legislative list belongs to
options: State governments|The federal government|Local governments|The judiciary
answer: State governments
rubric: Items not on the exclusive or concurrent lists fall under the residual powers of state governments.

subject: Government
stem: One advantage of federalism is that it
options: Allows diversity to be accommodated within one nation|Concentrates power at the center|Eliminates regional differences|Reduces the number of governments
answer: Allows diversity to be accommodated within one nation
rubric: Federalism enables nations with diverse ethnic, religious or regional groups to coexist under one government.

subject: Government
stem: Revenue allocation in Nigeria refers to
options: The sharing of federally collected revenue among the three tiers|Tax collection by states|Local government spending|IMF grants to Nigeria
answer: The sharing of federally collected revenue among the three tiers
rubric: The revenue allocation formula determines how the Federation Account is distributed among federal, state and local governments.

subject: Government
stem: The Federation Account holds
options: Revenue from federally collected taxes and resource proceeds|Only oil revenue|Only tax from Lagos|State government deposits only
answer: Revenue from federally collected taxes and resource proceeds
rubric: The Federation Account pools all federally collected revenue for sharing among all tiers.

subject: Government
stem: Intergovernmental relations in federalism refers to
options: Interactions and cooperation between different levels of government|Relations between Nigeria and other countries|Relations between the arms of government|Trade between states
answer: Interactions and cooperation between different levels of government
rubric: Intergovernmental relations manage coordination and conflict resolution between federal and state/local governments.

subject: Government
stem: A unitary state differs from a federal state in that
options: All power is concentrated at the centre|Power is divided between tiers|Local governments have autonomy|States can secede
answer: All power is concentrated at the centre
rubric: In a unitary state, subnational governments only exercise powers delegated by the central government.

subject: Government
stem: Devolution of power in a federation means
options: Delegating certain powers from the centre to regions|Removing all power from regions|Centralizing all functions|Merging state governments
answer: Delegating certain powers from the centre to regions
rubric: Devolution transfers specific functions and responsibilities to lower levels of government.

subject: Government
stem: Nigeria currently has how many states?
rubric: Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory.

subject: Government
stem: The principle of fiscal federalism relates to
options: Distribution of financial resources among levels of government|Judicial independence|Foreign exchange policy|Military funding
answer: Distribution of financial resources among levels of government
rubric: Fiscal federalism concerns how revenues and expenditure responsibilities are assigned across tiers of government.

subject: Government
stem: A confederation differs from a federation in that
options: Member states retain sovereignty|The central government is supreme|Member states have no independent power|It has only two tiers
answer: Member states retain sovereignty
rubric: In a confederation, member states retain their sovereignty and delegate limited powers to the central body.

subject: Government
stem: One problem of Nigerian federalism is
options: Imbalance in revenue allocation|Too many tiers of government|Absence of a constitution|Lack of a legislature
answer: Imbalance in revenue allocation
rubric: Revenue allocation disputes between the federal, state and local governments have been a persistent problem in Nigerian federalism.

subject: Government
stem: The principle of derivation in revenue allocation means
options: States receive a portion of revenue from resources found in their territory|Revenue is shared equally|Revenue goes only to the federal government|States pay taxes to the center
answer: States receive a portion of revenue from resources found in their territory
rubric: The derivation principle gives resource-producing states a percentage (currently 13%) of natural resource revenue.

subject: Government
stem: State creation in Nigeria is handled by
options: The National Assembly and a referendum in the affected area|The President alone|The state governor|INEC
answer: The National Assembly and a referendum in the affected area
rubric: Creating a new state requires an act of the National Assembly supported by a referendum of affected communities.

subject: Government
stem: The Federal Character principle in Nigeria ensures
options: Equitable representation of all states and groups in government|Only majority groups are represented|One region dominates government|Representation by merit only
answer: Equitable representation of all states and groups in government
rubric: The Federal Character principle guards against any state or group dominating federal appointments.

subject: Government
stem: Concurrent powers in Nigerian federalism means these powers
options: Can be exercised by both federal and state governments|Belong exclusively to the federal government|Are exercised only by states|Are reserved for local governments
answer: Can be exercised by both federal and state governments
rubric: Concurrent list items can be legislated on by both tiers, with federal law prevailing in case of conflict.

subject: Government
stem: Which institution manages the sharing of federally collected revenue in Nigeria?
options: Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission|CBN|FIRS|Debt Management Office
answer: Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission
rubric: RMAFC determines and reviews the revenue allocation formula.

subject: Government
stem: The principle of supremacy of the constitution in Nigerian federalism means
options: The constitution is the highest law and prevails over all other laws|States can override the constitution|Local governments can nullify federal laws|Parliament can overrule the constitution
answer: The constitution is the highest law and prevails over all other laws
rubric: Constitutional supremacy means any law inconsistent with the constitution is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

subject: Government
stem: The Joint Account between state and local governments relates to
options: Sharing of federally allocated revenue between state and local governments in a state|A federal government account|Revenue from foreign aid|Tax revenue only
answer: Sharing of federally allocated revenue between state and local governments in a state
rubric: The State-Local Government Joint Account pools funds for distribution between state and LG councils.

subject: Government
stem: INEC stands for
options: Independent National Electoral Commission|Internal Nigerian Electoral Commission|Independent National Election Committee|Integrated Nigerian Electoral Commission
answer: Independent National Electoral Commission
rubric: INEC is the body responsible for conducting elections in Nigeria.

subject: Government
stem: Universal adult suffrage means
options: All adults have the right to vote|Only educated citizens can vote|Only property owners vote|Men alone can vote
answer: All adults have the right to vote
rubric: Universal adult suffrage extends the right to vote to all adults regardless of sex, class or education.

subject: Government
stem: The minimum voting age in Nigeria is
options: 18 years|21 years|16 years|25 years
answer: 18 years
rubric: Nigerian citizens from age 18 are eligible to register and vote.

subject: Government
stem: Primary election in a Nigerian political party is the process by which
options: Party members choose their candidates|The general public votes for a party|INEC registers candidates|The President is inaugurated
answer: Party members choose their candidates
rubric: Primary elections (or primaries) are internal party processes to select candidates for general elections.

subject: Government
stem: Proportional representation is an electoral system in which
options: Parties win seats in proportion to their share of votes|The winner takes all seats|Only two parties compete|Votes are not counted
answer: Parties win seats in proportion to their share of votes
rubric: Proportional representation links the number of seats won to the share of the total vote received.

subject: Government
stem: The first-past-the-post electoral system means
options: The candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins|A candidate needs more than 50% to win|A runoff election is always held|All parties share seats
answer: The candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins
rubric: First-past-the-post (simple plurality) elects whoever gets the highest number of votes.

subject: Government
stem: Gerrymandering refers to
options: Manipulating constituency boundaries to favour a party|Ballot stuffing|Voter intimidation|Cancelling election results
answer: Manipulating constituency boundaries to favour a party
rubric: Gerrymandering involves drawing electoral boundaries to give one party an unfair advantage.

subject: Government
stem: The minimum age to contest for the Nigerian presidency is
options: 40 years|35 years|30 years|45 years
answer: 40 years
rubric: The 1999 Constitution requires presidential candidates to be at least 40 years old.

subject: Government
stem: For a presidential candidate in Nigeria to win in the first round, they must obtain
options: 25% of votes in two-thirds of all states plus the overall majority|Simple majority|50% plus one of all votes|Two-thirds of all votes
answer: 25% of votes in two-thirds of all states plus the overall majority
rubric: Section 134 of the 1999 Constitution requires the winner to have the majority of votes AND at least 25% in at least 24 states.

subject: Government
stem: A political party manifesto is
options: A document stating a party's policies and intentions|A voter registration card|The ballot paper|An election petition
answer: A document stating a party's policies and intentions
rubric: A manifesto outlines a party's plans and policy positions for voters to evaluate.

subject: Government
stem: The role of opposition parties in a democracy is to
options: Check the ruling party and offer policy alternatives|Support everything the government does|Overthrow the government|Boycott all elections
answer: Check the ruling party and offer policy alternatives
rubric: Opposition parties scrutinize government, debate policies and present themselves as an alternative government.

subject: Government
stem: An incumbent is
options: A current holder of a political office|A new candidate|A party agent|A registered voter
answer: A current holder of a political office
rubric: An incumbent is someone currently serving in an elected position who may seek re-election.

subject: Government
stem: Voter apathy refers to
options: Lack of interest by eligible voters in participating in elections|Rigging of elections|Excessive voter turnout|The cancellation of results
answer: Lack of interest by eligible voters in participating in elections
rubric: Voter apathy is a significant problem where eligible voters choose not to register or vote.

subject: Government
stem: A by-election is conducted when
options: A seat becomes vacant before the end of a term|The general election results are disputed|A new state is created|A party loses its primary
answer: A seat becomes vacant before the end of a term
rubric: A by-election fills a vacancy that arises due to death, resignation or disqualification of a sitting member.

subject: Government
stem: The Electoral Act regulates
options: The conduct of elections in Nigeria|How parties choose their symbols|International relations|The judiciary
answer: The conduct of elections in Nigeria
rubric: The Electoral Act provides the legal framework for conducting elections administered by INEC.

subject: Government
stem: Political socialization is the process by which
options: Individuals acquire political values and attitudes|Parties are registered|Electoral results are announced|Votes are counted
answer: Individuals acquire political values and attitudes
rubric: Political socialization involves learning political orientations through family, education, media and peers.

subject: Government
stem: A two-party system means
options: Two dominant parties compete for government|Only two parties are allowed by law|Two parties always form a coalition|One party is allowed
answer: Two dominant parties compete for government
rubric: In a two-party system, two major parties dominate elections though others may exist.

subject: Government
stem: Pressure groups differ from political parties in that they
options: Do not seek to form government directly|Contest all elections|Have no public agenda|Are funded by government
answer: Do not seek to form government directly
rubric: Pressure groups aim to influence policy without seeking political office, unlike political parties.

subject: Government
stem: Franchise means
options: The right to vote|The right to contest elections|Citizenship|Party membership
answer: The right to vote
rubric: Franchise (or suffrage) is the right to vote in public elections.

subject: Government
stem: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is established by
options: The 1999 Constitution|An Act of Parliament only|Presidential decree|The political parties
answer: The 1999 Constitution
rubric: INEC is a constitutional body established under the Third Schedule of the 1999 Constitution.

subject: Government
stem: Electoral malpractice includes
options: Ballot stuffing, voter intimidation and falsifying results|Only ballot stuffing|Campaign financing alone|Holding primary elections
answer: Ballot stuffing, voter intimidation and falsifying results
rubric: Electoral malpractice encompasses any illegal act that distorts the true outcome of elections.

subject: Government
stem: A runoff election occurs when
options: No candidate wins the required majority in the first round|The first round produces a clear winner|A candidate withdraws|Results are declared invalid
answer: No candidate wins the required majority in the first round
rubric: A runoff (second ballot) is held between the top two candidates when no one obtains the required majority.

subject: Government
stem: The Permanent Voter Card (PVC) is used in Nigeria for
options: Accreditation and voting during elections|Tax payment|Court identification|Travel abroad
answer: Accreditation and voting during elections
rubric: The PVC is the official voter identification card issued by INEC to registered voters.

subject: Government
stem: Which of these best describes a multi-party system?
options: Many political parties compete in elections|Only two parties exist|One party rules indefinitely|Parties are banned
answer: Many political parties compete in elections
rubric: A multi-party system allows many parties to contest elections, often resulting in coalition governments.

subject: Government
stem: The role of party agents at polling units is to
options: Monitor voting and collation on behalf of their party|Distribute ballot papers|Chair the polling unit|Count all ballots alone
answer: Monitor voting and collation on behalf of their party
rubric: Party agents observe electoral processes to detect irregularities and protect their party's interests.

subject: Government
stem: A citizen by birth in Nigeria is one who
options: Has at least one Nigerian parent|Was born anywhere in the world|Is naturalized|Is a permanent resident
answer: Has at least one Nigerian parent
rubric: Section 25 of the 1999 Constitution confers citizenship by birth on those born in Nigeria whose parents or grandparents were citizens.

subject: Government
stem: Naturalization is the process by which
options: A foreigner becomes a citizen|A citizen loses citizenship|Citizens vote|Citizens pay taxes
answer: A foreigner becomes a citizen
rubric: Naturalization grants citizenship to non-citizens who meet residency and other requirements.

subject: Government
stem: Dual citizenship means
options: Holding citizenship of two countries simultaneously|Having two passports but one citizenship|Being stateless|Changing nationality
answer: Holding citizenship of two countries simultaneously
rubric: Dual citizenship allows an individual to be a national of two countries at the same time.

subject: Government
stem: Which of the following is a duty of a citizen?
options: Paying taxes and obeying the law|Holding a public office|Traveling abroad|Speaking only the official language
answer: Paying taxes and obeying the law
rubric: Citizens have duties including paying taxes, obeying the law, military service when required, and jury duty.

subject: Government
stem: The right to freedom of expression is protected under
options: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution|The Electoral Act|The Criminal Code|Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution
answer: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution
rubric: Freedom of expression is a fundamental right enshrined in Chapter IV of the 1999 CFRN.

subject: Government
stem: The right to life may be derogated from
options: In execution of a court sentence for a capital offence|Whenever a police officer decides|By executive order|During elections
answer: In execution of a court sentence for a capital offence
rubric: Section 33(2)(a) allows deprivation of life in execution of a sentence of a court in respect of a criminal offence.

subject: Government
stem: The right to personal liberty is protected under Section
options: 35 of the 1999 Constitution|25 of the 1999 Constitution|40 of the 1999 Constitution|14 of the Criminal Code
answer: 35 of the 1999 Constitution
rubric: Section 35 guarantees the right to personal liberty, including protections against arbitrary arrest.

subject: Government
stem: Derogation from rights is permissible
options: During a state of emergency|At any time the government wishes|Only during elections|When it is profitable
answer: During a state of emergency
rubric: Certain rights may be suspended during a legally declared state of emergency.

subject: Government
stem: Non-discrimination on grounds of tribe, religion or sex is protected under
options: Section 42 of the 1999 Constitution|Section 10 of the 1999 Constitution|The Penal Code|The Immigration Act
answer: Section 42 of the 1999 Constitution
rubric: Section 42 prohibits discrimination on grounds of community, ethnic group, place of origin, sex, religion or political opinion.

subject: Government
stem: Statelessness refers to
options: A condition where a person has no nationality|Dual citizenship|Loss of voting rights|A person living abroad
answer: A condition where a person has no nationality
rubric: A stateless person is not recognized as a national by any state, leaving them without legal protections.

subject: Government
stem: The right to education is classified in Nigeria as
options: A directive principle (Chapter II) not directly enforceable|A fundamental right (Chapter IV)|An absolute right|A criminal law provision
answer: A directive principle (Chapter II) not directly enforceable
rubric: Chapter II (Fundamental Objectives) including education are not directly justiciable under the 1999 Constitution.

subject: Government
stem: Freedom of religion in Nigeria means
options: Every person is free to choose and practice their religion|Only Christianity and Islam are recognised|The government chooses the state religion|Religious practice requires a licence
answer: Every person is free to choose and practice their religion
rubric: Section 38 protects freedom of thought, conscience and religion.

subject: Government
stem: A refugee under international law is a person who
options: Has fled their country due to persecution|Is studying abroad|Works in another country|Has dual citizenship
answer: Has fled their country due to persecution
rubric: The 1951 Refugee Convention defines a refugee as someone outside their country due to well-founded fear of persecution.

subject: Government
stem: Rights are considered inalienable because
options: They cannot be taken away or surrendered|They can be bought and sold|Only the rich enjoy them|They change with each government
answer: They cannot be taken away or surrendered
rubric: Inalienable rights belong to individuals inherently and cannot be permanently taken away.

subject: Government
stem: The right to a fair hearing includes
options: Being informed of charges and having adequate time to prepare a defence|Being tried in private|A judge deciding without hearing evidence|No right to legal representation
answer: Being informed of charges and having adequate time to prepare a defence
rubric: Section 36 guarantees fair hearing including the right to know charges, be heard and be represented.

subject: Government
stem: Civil rights are
options: Rights that protect individuals from discrimination and ensure equal treatment|Military rights|Rights given only to government officials|Rights to carry arms
answer: Rights that protect individuals from discrimination and ensure equal treatment
rubric: Civil rights are the rights of individuals to receive equal treatment in various settings.

subject: Government
stem: Political rights include
options: The right to vote and contest elections|Rights to social welfare only|Economic rights only|Rights to own property
answer: The right to vote and contest elections
rubric: Political rights are rights related to participation in the civic and political life of a state.

subject: Government
stem: Human rights are described as universal because
options: They belong to every person regardless of nationality, race or religion|Only citizens of democratic states have them|They are granted by governments|Only adults hold them
answer: They belong to every person regardless of nationality, race or religion
rubric: Universality is a core attribute of human rights, meaning they apply to all people everywhere.

subject: Government
stem: The body that enforces human rights in Nigeria judicially is the
options: Courts|INEC|The National Human Rights Commission|The Police
answer: Courts
rubric: Human rights are enforced through the judicial system, particularly the Federal and State High Courts.

subject: Government
stem: Loss of Nigerian citizenship can occur through
options: Renunciation or deprivation by court order|Mere absence from the country|Change of religion|Marriage to a foreigner
answer: Renunciation or deprivation by court order
rubric: A citizen may renounce citizenship voluntarily or be deprived by an order of court in specified circumstances.

subject: Government
stem: The United Nations was established in
rubric: The United Nations was founded on October 24, 1945 after World War II.

subject: Government
stem: The principal organ of the UN responsible for international peace and security is
options: The Security Council|The General Assembly|The Secretariat|The International Court of Justice
answer: The Security Council
rubric: The Security Council has primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security.

subject: Government
stem: The African Union (AU) replaced which organisation?
options: Organisation of African Unity (OAU)|Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)|African Development Bank|Commonwealth of Nations
answer: Organisation of African Unity (OAU)
rubric: The African Union replaced the OAU in 2002, maintaining similar goals but with stronger integration mechanisms.

subject: Government
stem: ECOWAS stands for
options: Economic Community of West African States|East-Central Organisation for West African Security|Economic Cooperation of West African States|European Community of Western African States
answer: Economic Community of West African States
rubric: ECOWAS is the regional economic bloc for West Africa, headquartered in Abuja.

subject: Government
stem: The headquarters of the United Nations is in
options: New York City|London|Geneva|Washington D.C.
answer: New York City
rubric: The UN headquarters is located in New York City, USA.

subject: Government
stem: The permanent members of the UN Security Council are
options: USA, UK, France, Russia and China|USA, Germany, France, Russia and China|USA, UK, Japan, Russia and China|USA, UK, France, India and China
answer: USA, UK, France, Russia and China
rubric: The five permanent members (P5) each have veto power in the Security Council.

subject: Government
stem: The Commonwealth of Nations is an association of
options: Former British colonies and territories|African nations only|EU member states|NATO members
answer: Former British colonies and territories
rubric: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of 56 nations, mostly former territories of the British Empire.

subject: Government
stem: OPEC is concerned with
options: Oil production and pricing policy|Agricultural development|Military alliances|Refugee management
answer: Oil production and pricing policy
rubric: OPEC (Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) coordinates the oil output and pricing of member states.

subject: Government
stem: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) settles
options: Disputes between states|Criminal cases involving individuals|Electoral disputes|Internal trade disputes
answer: Disputes between states
rubric: The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the UN, settling legal disputes submitted by states.

subject: Government
stem: The African Development Bank (AfDB) is headquartered in
options: Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire|Addis Ababa, Ethiopia|Abuja, Nigeria|Cairo, Egypt
answer: Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire
rubric: The AfDB is headquartered in Abidjan, though it temporarily relocated during Cote d'Ivoire's civil conflict.

subject: Government
stem: The AU headquarters is located in
options: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia|Nairobi, Kenya|Lagos, Nigeria|Cairo, Egypt
answer: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
rubric: The African Union Commission is headquartered in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

subject: Government
stem: NATO is primarily a
options: Military alliance|Economic community|Human rights organisation|Environmental body
answer: Military alliance
rubric: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) is a military alliance for collective defence.

subject: Government
stem: The World Bank primarily provides
options: Development loans and assistance to developing countries|Military aid|Currency exchange|Oil production quotas
answer: Development loans and assistance to developing countries
rubric: The World Bank provides loans and grants to developing countries for the purposes of pursuing capital projects.

subject: Government
stem: The IMF stands for
options: International Monetary Fund|International Military Fund|Inter-ministerial Finance body|International Market Federation
answer: International Monetary Fund
rubric: The IMF promotes international monetary cooperation and provides financial assistance to member states.

subject: Government
stem: The Non-Aligned Movement was formed by countries that
options: Refused to align with either the USA or USSR during the Cold War|Opposed nuclear weapons|Supported decolonisation in Africa|Formed a military alliance
answer: Refused to align with either the USA or USSR during the Cold War
rubric: The Non-Aligned Movement emerged during the Cold War as a group of states neutral between the Western and Eastern blocs.

subject: Government
stem: UN peacekeeping forces are deployed to
options: Conflict zones to maintain or restore peace|Protect oil facilities|Promote trade|Monitor elections only
answer: Conflict zones to maintain or restore peace
rubric: UN peacekeeping operations are mandated to protect civilians, facilitate political transitions and build durable peace.

subject: Government
stem: Nigeria has been a member of the United Nations since
rubric: Nigeria joined the UN in 1960 following independence.

subject: Government
stem: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in
rubric: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly on December 10, 1948.

subject: Government
stem: The WTO regulates
