answer: It determines how much foreign currency a domestic currency can buy
rubric: Exchange rate fluctuations affect the price competitiveness of imports and exports.

subject: Marketing
stem: Franchising as an entry mode in international marketing involves
options: A firm granting rights to a foreign operator to use its brand and system|A firm building its own factory abroad|Two governments signing a trade deal|A firm donating products abroad
answer: A firm granting rights to a foreign operator to use its brand and system
rubric: International franchising allows rapid expansion with lower capital outlay than wholly-owned subsidiaries.

subject: Marketing
stem: Marketing ethics refers to
options: Applying moral principles to marketing decisions and practices|Setting prices fairly only|Advertising freely|Ignoring consumer complaints
answer: Applying moral principles to marketing decisions and practices
rubric: Marketing ethics involves making decisions that are honest, fair and respectful of consumers and society.

subject: Marketing
stem: False advertising is an example of
options: Unethical marketing practice|Ethical promotion|A legal advertising strategy|A form of public relations
answer: Unethical marketing practice
rubric: False advertising involves misleading claims about a product, which is both unethical and illegal.

subject: Marketing
stem: Consumer protection laws in Nigeria are designed to
options: Safeguard buyers from unfair trade practices and unsafe products|Regulate advertising only|Set product prices|Control imports
answer: Safeguard buyers from unfair trade practices and unsafe products
rubric: Consumer protection legislation ensures that buyers have recourse against exploitation and dangerous goods.

subject: Marketing
stem: The Consumer Protection Council (CPC) in Nigeria
options: Handles consumer complaints and enforces consumer rights|Manufactures goods|Sets import tariffs|Controls foreign exchange
answer: Handles consumer complaints and enforces consumer rights
rubric: The CPC investigates complaints, mediates disputes and takes action against businesses that violate consumer rights.

subject: Marketing
stem: Caveat emptor is a legal principle meaning
options: Let the buyer beware|The seller is always responsible|Products must carry guarantees|Refunds are mandatory
answer: Let the buyer beware
rubric: Caveat emptor places responsibility on buyers to check goods before purchase; modern consumer law has reduced its scope.

subject: Marketing
stem: A product recall is when
options: A manufacturer withdraws a defective product from sale and from consumers|A retailer increases a product's price|A wholesaler returns goods to the manufacturer|A consumer returns goods for a refund
answer: A manufacturer withdraws a defective product from sale and from consumers
rubric: Product recalls protect consumers from harm by removing unsafe goods from circulation.

subject: Marketing
stem: Green marketing involves
options: Promoting products as environmentally friendly or sustainable|Using green-coloured packaging|Selling only agricultural products|Marketing in rural areas
answer: Promoting products as environmentally friendly or sustainable
rubric: Green marketing emphasises environmental benefits and sustainability in products and corporate practice.

subject: Marketing
stem: Greenwashing refers to
options: Making misleading environmental claims about a product|Genuine environmental marketing|Using recycled packaging|Selling organic food
answer: Making misleading environmental claims about a product
rubric: Greenwashing is an unethical practice where firms exaggerate or fabricate environmental credentials.

subject: Marketing
stem: The right of consumers to choose means
options: Consumers should have access to a variety of goods at competitive prices|Consumers must buy from one source|Government picks goods for consumers|Prices are fixed
answer: Consumers should have access to a variety of goods at competitive prices
rubric: The right to choose is a core consumer right: competition ensures variety and fair pricing.

subject: Marketing
stem: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in marketing means
options: A firm contributes positively to society beyond profit-making|A firm maximises profit at any cost|A firm advertises freely|A firm sells only to corporations
answer: A firm contributes positively to society beyond profit-making
rubric: CSR integrates social, ethical and environmental considerations into business strategy.

subject: Marketing
stem: Bait-and-switch advertising is
options: Advertising a product at a low price then pressuring consumers to buy a higher-priced item|A legitimate sales promotion|A form of discount pricing|A loyalty reward scheme
answer: Advertising a product at a low price then pressuring consumers to buy a higher-priced item
rubric: Bait-and-switch lures consumers with an attractive offer and then substitutes a more expensive product.

subject: Marketing
stem: NAFDAC protects Nigerian consumers by
options: Regulating the manufacture, import and distribution of food, drugs and cosmetics|Setting retail prices|Managing advertising standards|Controlling foreign trade
answer: Regulating the manufacture, import and distribution of food, drugs and cosmetics
rubric: NAFDAC ensures that food, drugs and related products meet safety and quality standards.

subject: Marketing
stem: Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) is responsible for
options: Setting and enforcing product quality standards|Regulating food safety|Controlling imports|Managing the stock exchange
answer: Setting and enforcing product quality standards
rubric: SON develops and enforces standards for manufactured goods to protect consumers and industry.

subject: Marketing
stem: Deceptive pricing occurs when
options: A seller creates a false impression of a price advantage|A seller offers genuine discounts|A seller sets market-rate prices|A seller raises prices openly
answer: A seller creates a false impression of a price advantage
rubric: Deceptive pricing tactics include fake markdowns and misleading price comparisons.

subject: Marketing
stem: The right to safety as a consumer right means
options: Consumers are protected from products that are dangerous to health|Consumers can return any product|Sellers must offer the lowest price|Consumers choose freely
answer: Consumers are protected from products that are dangerous to health
rubric: The right to safety requires that goods be safe for intended use and that hazardous products be taken off the market.

subject: Marketing
stem: Planned obsolescence is
options: Deliberately designing products to become outdated to encourage repeat purchases|Making durable products only|A form of product recall|A distribution strategy
answer: Deliberately designing products to become outdated to encourage repeat purchases
rubric: Planned obsolescence is an ethical controversy in marketing, particularly in electronics and fashion.

subject: Marketing
stem: The right to be informed as a consumer means
options: Consumers must receive accurate information about products to make sound decisions|Sellers need not disclose ingredients|Advertising can be misleading|Prices need not be displayed
answer: Consumers must receive accurate information about products to make sound decisions
rubric: The right to information underpins consumer protection: labelling, disclosure and truthful advertising are required.

subject: Marketing
stem: A warranty is
options: A seller's written or implied promise that a product will perform as described|A type of discount|A product return policy|A marketing strategy
answer: A seller's written or implied promise that a product will perform as described
rubric: Warranties provide consumers with assurance and legal recourse if a product fails to meet stated standards.

subject: Marketing
stem: Price fixing is illegal because
options: It eliminates competition and harms consumers by artificially raising prices|It lowers prices for consumers|It increases product quality|It is a form of discount pricing
answer: It eliminates competition and harms consumers by artificially raising prices
rubric: Price fixing (collusion among competitors to set prices) is an anti-competitive practice prohibited by law.

subject: Marketing
stem: Ethical sourcing in marketing means
options: Ensuring that products are obtained from suppliers who follow fair labour and environmental standards|Buying the cheapest raw materials|Sourcing only from local suppliers|Importing all raw materials
answer: Ensuring that products are obtained from suppliers who follow fair labour and environmental standards
rubric: Ethical sourcing addresses labour rights, environmental impact and fair trade in the supply chain.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A metaphor is a figure of speech that
options: Directly compares two unlike things without using "like" or "as"|Compares two things using "like" or "as"|Gives human qualities to non-human things|Overstates something for effect
answer: Directly compares two unlike things without using "like" or "as"
rubric: A metaphor makes an implicit comparison: "Life is a journey."

subject: Literature in English
stem: A simile compares two things using
options: Like or as|Without any connecting word|Onomatopoeia|Alliteration
answer: Like or as
rubric: A simile is an explicit comparison: "She runs like the wind."

subject: Literature in English
stem: Personification is
options: Attributing human qualities to non-human entities|Comparing two human characters|Overstating a fact|Using sound to suggest meaning
answer: Attributing human qualities to non-human entities
rubric: Personification: "The trees whispered in the wind."

subject: Literature in English
stem: Hyperbole is a figure of speech that
options: Exaggerates for emphasis or effect|Understates to create irony|Uses sound words|Compares two unlike things
answer: Exaggerates for emphasis or effect
rubric: Hyperbole: "I have told you a million times."

subject: Literature in English
stem: Irony occurs when
options: The actual meaning is the opposite of the literal meaning|The meaning is exactly what is said|Sounds echo meanings|Sentences are very short
answer: The actual meaning is the opposite of the literal meaning
rubric: Verbal irony involves saying one thing while meaning another, often for humorous or satirical effect.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An oxymoron is
options: The combination of contradictory words in a phrase|A figure of comparison|A sound device|An extended metaphor
answer: The combination of contradictory words in a phrase
rubric: Oxymoron: "deafening silence", "bitter sweet."

subject: Literature in English
stem: Onomatopoeia is the use of
options: Words that imitate the sounds they describe|Contradictory terms together|Exaggerated comparisons|Human qualities for objects
answer: Words that imitate the sounds they describe
rubric: Onomatopoeia: "buzz", "hiss", "clang", "thud."

subject: Literature in English
stem: Alliteration is
options: The repetition of the same consonant sound at the beginning of nearby words|Repetition of vowel sounds|A figure of contrast|An overstatement
answer: The repetition of the same consonant sound at the beginning of nearby words
rubric: Alliteration: "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers."

subject: Literature in English
stem: An allusion is
options: An indirect reference to a well-known person, event or work|A direct quotation|A type of rhyme|A narrative technique
answer: An indirect reference to a well-known person, event or work
rubric: Allusions assume shared knowledge, e.g., calling someone a "Good Samaritan" alludes to the Bible.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The theme of a literary work is
options: The central idea or message explored in the work|The plot summary|The setting of the story|The main character
answer: The central idea or message explored in the work
rubric: Theme is the underlying message (e.g., love, betrayal, justice) that pervades the work.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The plot of a story is
options: The sequence of events and their causal relationships|The message of the story|The setting|The characters involved
answer: The sequence of events and their causal relationships
rubric: Plot is the structured series of events that drive the narrative forward.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A protagonist is
options: The main character who drives the story|The villain of the story|The narrator|A minor character
answer: The main character who drives the story
rubric: The protagonist is the central figure around whom the story revolves.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An antagonist is
options: The character or force that opposes the protagonist|The main character|The narrator|A supporting character
answer: The character or force that opposes the protagonist
rubric: The antagonist creates conflict by opposing the goals of the protagonist.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Flashback is a narrative technique where
options: Events from the past are inserted into the present narrative|Events are told in chronological order|The ending is revealed first|Future events are hinted at
answer: Events from the past are inserted into the present narrative
rubric: Flashback (analepsis) interrupts the current timeline to reveal past events.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Foreshadowing is a technique where
options: Hints are given about future events in the story|Past events are recalled|The plot is summarised at the start|A character speaks directly to the reader
answer: Hints are given about future events in the story
rubric: Foreshadowing creates suspense and prepares the reader for what is to come.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Satire is a literary technique that
options: Uses humour, irony or exaggeration to criticise society or individuals|Only tells funny stories|Praises the subject|Describes nature beautifully
answer: Uses humour, irony or exaggeration to criticise society or individuals
rubric: Satire aims to expose folly, vice or corruption through ridicule.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Symbolism in literature means
options: Using objects, persons or events to represent abstract ideas|Only using metaphors|Telling stories about symbols|Listing objects in a poem
answer: Using objects, persons or events to represent abstract ideas
rubric: A symbol carries a deeper meaning beyond its literal significance, e.g., a dove symbolising peace.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Point of view in a narrative refers to
options: The perspective from which the story is told|The author's biography|The setting of the story|The genre of the work
answer: The perspective from which the story is told
rubric: Point of view (first person, third person, omniscient) determines what the narrator knows and shares.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A soliloquy is
options: A dramatic speech in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud when alone|A conversation between two characters|A poem within a play|A stage direction
answer: A dramatic speech in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud when alone
rubric: Soliloquy reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An aside in drama is
options: A remark spoken by a character to the audience, unheard by other characters|A long speech|A stage direction|A conversation between actors
answer: A remark spoken by a character to the audience, unheard by other characters
rubric: An aside gives the audience privileged insight into a character's private thoughts.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Dramatic irony occurs when
options: The audience knows something that characters in the play do not|The author contradicts himself|Two characters disagree|The play has a sad ending
answer: The audience knows something that characters in the play do not
rubric: Dramatic irony creates tension or humour because the audience anticipates consequences the characters cannot.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The climax of a story is
options: The point of highest tension or turning point in the plot|The opening event|The resolution of the conflict|The character's backstory
answer: The point of highest tension or turning point in the plot
rubric: The climax is the decisive moment where the central conflict reaches its peak.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Diction refers to
options: The choice and use of words by an author|The punctuation in a text|The plot structure|The rhyme scheme
answer: The choice and use of words by an author
rubric: Diction encompasses vocabulary, tone and register choices that shape a text's style and effect.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Tone in literature is
options: The author's attitude toward the subject or audience as expressed in the writing|The rhyme scheme|The plot summary|The setting
answer: The author's attitude toward the subject or audience as expressed in the writing
rubric: Tone may be ironic, solemn, humorous, angry, etc., shaping the reader's emotional response.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Setting in a literary work refers to
options: The time and place in which the story occurs|The main character|The central theme|The narrative voice
answer: The time and place in which the story occurs
rubric: Setting provides the physical and temporal context for the narrative.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A sonnet is a poem of
options: 14 lines|8 lines|12 lines|16 lines
answer: 14 lines
rubric: The sonnet is a 14-line poem, traditionally written in iambic pentameter.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An ode is
options: A lyric poem that praises or addresses a person, place or thing|A poem that tells a story|A short, witty poem|A humorous verse about death
answer: A lyric poem that praises or addresses a person, place or thing
rubric: An ode is a formal, often elaborate lyric poem written in celebration or tribute.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A stanza is
options: A group of lines in a poem|A single line of verse|The rhyme scheme|A type of metre
answer: A group of lines in a poem
rubric: A stanza is a unit of lines in poetry, equivalent to a paragraph in prose.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Rhyme in poetry is
options: The repetition of similar sounds at the end of lines|The rhythm pattern|The subject matter|The number of syllables
answer: The repetition of similar sounds at the end of lines
rubric: Rhyme creates musicality and structure in poetry.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Free verse is poetry that
options: Has no fixed rhyme scheme or metrical pattern|Always rhymes|Is written in exactly 14 lines|Uses only metaphors
answer: Has no fixed rhyme scheme or metrical pattern
rubric: Free verse abandons traditional constraints of metre and rhyme while maintaining poetic intensity.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Imagery in poetry refers to
options: Descriptive language that appeals to the senses|The rhyme scheme|The length of the poem|The number of stanzas
answer: Descriptive language that appeals to the senses
rubric: Imagery uses vivid sensory description to create mental pictures and emotional responses.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Assonance is
options: The repetition of vowel sounds within nearby words|Repetition of consonant sounds at the start of words|A type of rhyme at line ends|A figure of exaggeration
answer: The repetition of vowel sounds within nearby words
rubric: Assonance: "The rain in Spain stays mainly on the plain."

subject: Literature in English
stem: Rhythm in poetry refers to
options: The pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables|The rhyme at line ends|The number of lines|The use of metaphor
answer: The pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables
rubric: Rhythm gives poetry its musical quality through the recurrence of stressed beats.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An elegy is
options: A mournful poem lamenting a death|A poem praising a person|A humorous verse|A love poem
answer: A mournful poem lamenting a death
rubric: An elegy is a lyric poem of mourning for someone who has died.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An epic poem is
options: A long narrative poem about the deeds of a heroic figure|A short lyric poem|A poem with 14 lines|A poem without rhyme
answer: A long narrative poem about the deeds of a heroic figure
rubric: Epics (e.g., Homer's Iliad, Virgil's Aeneid) celebrate heroes and involve supernatural forces.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A couplet is
options: Two consecutive lines of poetry that rhyme|A poem of four lines|A stanza of six lines|A poem without rhyme
answer: Two consecutive lines of poetry that rhyme
rubric: A couplet is the simplest stanza form: two lines with matching end rhymes.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A ballad is
options: A narrative poem or song that tells a story, often about love or adventure|A lyric poem praising nature|A 14-line poem|A poem of mourning
answer: A narrative poem or song that tells a story, often about love or adventure
rubric: Ballads are traditional storytelling poems with a strong rhythm and often a refrain.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The persona in a poem is
options: The voice or character adopted by the poet to speak the poem|The poet's real identity|The theme of the poem|The rhyme scheme
answer: The voice or character adopted by the poet to speak the poem
rubric: The persona allows the poet to adopt a different identity, creating distance from the author's own views.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Refrain in poetry is
options: A line or group of lines repeated at regular intervals|A type of rhyme scheme|The closing couplet|The opening line
answer: A line or group of lines repeated at regular intervals
rubric: A refrain (chorus) reinforces the poem's theme and creates rhythm through repetition.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The mood of a poem refers to
options: The emotional atmosphere created by the poem|The subject of the poem|The length of the poem|The poet's biography
answer: The emotional atmosphere created by the poem
rubric: Mood is the feeling evoked in the reader, shaped by diction, imagery and tone.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Repetition in poetry is used to
options: Emphasise an idea or create rhythm|Introduce a new idea|Show character development|Describe the setting
answer: Emphasise an idea or create rhythm
rubric: Repetition reinforces meaning, creates emphasis and contributes to the musical quality of verse.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Caesura in poetry is
options: A pause within a line of verse|The end of a line|A type of rhyme|A stanza break
answer: A pause within a line of verse
rubric: A caesura is a rhythmic pause within a line, often marked by punctuation.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The octave of a Petrarchan sonnet consists of
options: The first eight lines|The last six lines|The final couplet|The entire poem
answer: The first eight lines
rubric: The Petrarchan sonnet is divided into an octave (8 lines) that poses a problem and a sestet (6 lines) that resolves it.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Euphony in poetry refers to
options: Pleasant, harmonious sounds that create a melodious effect|Harsh, discordant sounds|The use of rhyme only|Repetition of vowels
answer: Pleasant, harmonious sounds that create a melodious effect
rubric: Euphony uses soft consonants and open vowels to create a pleasing auditory effect.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A haiku is a poem of Japanese origin with
options: Three lines of 5, 7 and 5 syllables|14 lines|Four stanzas|Free verse only
answer: Three lines of 5, 7 and 5 syllables
rubric: A haiku captures a single moment or image in three lines: 5-7-5 syllables.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The volta in a sonnet is
options: The turn or shift in thought or argument|The opening line|The rhyme scheme|The final couplet only
answer: The turn or shift in thought or argument
rubric: The volta marks a pivotal change in perspective or argument within the sonnet.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A lament is a poem that
options: Expresses grief and sorrow|Celebrates a victory|Tells a story|Praises nature
answer: Expresses grief and sorrow
rubric: A lament mourns a loss, similar to an elegy but more personal and emotional in expression.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Enjambment is
options: The continuation of a sentence beyond the end of a line without a pause|A full stop at the end of every line|A type of rhyme scheme|Repetition of a line
answer: The continuation of a sentence beyond the end of a line without a pause
rubric: Enjambment carries meaning and rhythm across line breaks, creating forward momentum.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An acrostic poem is one where
options: The first letters of each line spell out a word or message|Every line rhymes|Lines are of equal length|The poem has no punctuation
answer: The first letters of each line spell out a word or message
rubric: An acrostic encodes a hidden message in the initial letters of each line.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Lyric poetry is primarily concerned with
options: Expressing personal feelings and emotions|Telling a heroic story|Describing a historical event|Satirising society
answer: Expressing personal feelings and emotions
rubric: Lyric poetry is subjective and musical, voicing the thoughts and feelings of a single speaker.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A novel is
options: A long work of prose fiction with complex characters and plot|A short story|A collection of poems|A dramatic work
answer: A long work of prose fiction with complex characters and plot
rubric: A novel is an extended narrative prose work that explores character, conflict and theme in depth.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A short story is characterised by
options: Brevity, a single main conflict and a limited number of characters|Multiple subplots and a large cast|Verse form|Historical facts only
answer: Brevity, a single main conflict and a limited number of characters
rubric: A short story is a concise prose narrative focused on one central event or character.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Character development in fiction means
options: How a character grows or changes over the course of a narrative|The physical description of a character|The character's first appearance|The number of characters
answer: How a character grows or changes over the course of a narrative
rubric: Character development traces the psychological and moral journey of characters.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A flat character in fiction is
options: One with a single, unchanging trait|A character who changes significantly|The protagonist of the story|A character with many dimensions
answer: One with a single, unchanging trait
rubric: Flat characters are simple, one-dimensional and do not develop across the narrative.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A round character is
options: Complex, multi-dimensional and capable of surprising the reader|Simple with one trait|Always the villain|Never the main character
answer: Complex, multi-dimensional and capable of surprising the reader
rubric: Round characters feel realistic because of their complexity and capacity for growth.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Conflict in a story is
options: A struggle between opposing forces that drives the plot|The setting of the story|The author's tone|The narrator's background
answer: A struggle between opposing forces that drives the plot
rubric: Conflict (person vs person, person vs nature, person vs self) is the engine of narrative.

subject: Literature in English
stem: First-person narration uses
options: "I" as the narrator who is also a character in the story|"He/She/They" throughout|An omniscient perspective|A collective "we" only
answer: "I" as the narrator who is also a character in the story
rubric: First-person narration gives an intimate, subjective perspective limited to what the narrator knows.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Omniscient narration means
options: The narrator knows the thoughts and feelings of all characters|The narrator knows only one character's thoughts|The story is told in first person|The narrator is unreliable
answer: The narrator knows the thoughts and feelings of all characters
rubric: An omniscient narrator has unlimited access to characters' internal states and any event in the story.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The exposition in a story
options: Introduces the setting, characters and background information|Is the climax of the story|Resolves the conflict|Introduces the antagonist only
answer: Introduces the setting, characters and background information
rubric: The exposition establishes the context and background needed to understand the story.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The denouement is
options: The final resolution and untangling of the plot after the climax|The rising action|The conflict itself|The opening of the story
answer: The final resolution and untangling of the plot after the climax
rubric: The denouement (French for "untying") brings the story to a satisfying close by resolving remaining questions.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Suspense in fiction is
options: A feeling of excitement or anxiety about what will happen next|The opening paragraph|A character description|The theme of the story
answer: A feeling of excitement or anxiety about what will happen next
rubric: Suspense keeps readers engaged by creating uncertainty about the outcome of events.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An unreliable narrator is one
options: Whose account of events is questionable or biased|Who knows everything|Who tells the story truthfully|Who is always the protagonist
answer: Whose account of events is questionable or biased
rubric: An unreliable narrator may be self-deceived, biased or deliberately misleading, requiring the reader to read critically.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Interior monologue is
options: A narrative technique that presents a character's thoughts as they occur|A formal speech|A dialogue between two characters|A description of setting
answer: A narrative technique that presents a character's thoughts as they occur
rubric: Interior monologue (stream of consciousness) reveals unfiltered thoughts, associated with modernist fiction.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Dialogue in fiction is
options: Direct speech between characters|The narrator's description|A poem within the novel|A stage direction
answer: Direct speech between characters
rubric: Dialogue reveals character, advances plot and creates realism through the characters' own words.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The resolution of a story is
options: The part where the conflict is resolved|The opening scene|The climax|The introduction of the antagonist
answer: The part where the conflict is resolved
rubric: Resolution brings the narrative conflict to a conclusion, whether happy, tragic or ambiguous.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Foreshadowing in prose fiction
options: Hints at events that will occur later in the story|Recalls past events|Summarises the plot|Describes the setting in detail
answer: Hints at events that will occur later in the story
rubric: Foreshadowing plants clues that prepare readers for future events.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A motif is
options: A recurring element (image, symbol or idea) throughout a work|A character who appears once|The rhyme scheme|A type of conflict
answer: A recurring element (image, symbol or idea) throughout a work
rubric: Motifs reinforce theme through repetition of a significant element.

subject: Literature in English
stem: In Chinua Achebe's "Things Fall Apart", Okonkwo is best described as
options: A tragic hero brought down by his own flaws|A complete villain|A minor character|A comic character
answer: A tragic hero brought down by his own flaws
rubric: "Things Fall Apart" charts Okonkwo's downfall resulting from his fear of weakness and the disruption of Igbo society.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The novel "Weep Not, Child" by Ngugi wa Thiongo is set during
options: The Mau Mau uprising in Kenya|The Nigerian Civil War|The apartheid era in South Africa|The Rwandan genocide
answer: The Mau Mau uprising in Kenya
rubric: "Weep Not, Child" explores the impact of British colonialism and the Mau Mau uprising on a Kenyan family.

subject: Literature in English
stem: In fiction, irony of situation (situational irony) occurs when
options: The outcome is the opposite of what is expected|A character says one thing and means another|The audience knows more than the characters|Two characters misunderstand each other
answer: The outcome is the opposite of what is expected
rubric: Situational irony creates surprise and often humour when events turn out contrary to expectations.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The rising action in a story is
options: The series of events building tension toward the climax|The resolution|The opening scene|The denouement
answer: The series of events building tension toward the climax
rubric: Rising action increases suspense by developing conflict and moving toward the climactic turning point.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A foil character is
options: A character who contrasts with another to highlight their qualities|The main villain|The omniscient narrator|A comic character
answer: A character who contrasts with another to highlight their qualities
rubric: A foil's contrasting traits illuminate the qualities of another character, usually the protagonist.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Stream of consciousness technique in fiction is
options: A narrative method that captures the continuous flow of a character's thoughts|A method of describing physical action|A type of dialogue|A way of describing setting
answer: A narrative method that captures the continuous flow of a character's thoughts
rubric: Stream of consciousness (as used by Woolf and Joyce) presents thought in its natural, associative form.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Characterisation is the method by which
options: An author creates and develops characters in a narrative|The plot is constructed|The setting is described|The theme is introduced
answer: An author creates and develops characters in a narrative
rubric: Characterisation uses action, dialogue, description and other characters' reactions to build personalities.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An allegory is
options: A narrative in which characters and events symbolise deeper moral or political meanings|A poem with a fixed rhyme scheme|A type of short story|A comedy of manners
answer: A narrative in which characters and events symbolise deeper moral or political meanings
rubric: An allegory operates on two levels: literal narrative and a symbolic layer carrying a broader message.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A play script is distinguished from prose fiction primarily by
options: Dialogue and stage directions|Description of characters|Use of themes|Length of the work
answer: Dialogue and stage directions
rubric: A play script is written primarily in dialogue with stage directions to guide performance.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A tragedy is a form of drama that
options: Ends with the downfall or death of the protagonist|Always has a happy ending|Is comic throughout|Involves only minor conflicts
answer: Ends with the downfall or death of the protagonist
rubric: Tragedy explores serious themes and ends in catastrophe, often caused by the hero's own flaws.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A comedy in drama typically
options: Ends happily and uses humour to explore human foibles|Is about tragic events|Deals with death|Focuses on historical events alone
answer: Ends happily and uses humour to explore human foibles
rubric: Comedy employs wit, misunderstanding and comic situations, traditionally ending in reconciliation or marriage.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A prologue in drama is
options: An introductory section before the main action begins|The final speech|The climax scene|A stage direction
answer: An introductory section before the main action begins
rubric: A prologue provides context, background or thematic framing before the play begins.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An epilogue in drama is
options: A concluding section that follows the main action|The opening scene|A stage direction|A character's soliloquy at the climax
answer: A concluding section that follows the main action
rubric: An epilogue wraps up loose ends or offers a final comment after the play's main action.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Catharsis in tragedy refers to
options: The emotional purification experienced by the audience through pity and fear|The death of the protagonist|A comic resolution|The climax of the play
answer: The emotional purification experienced by the audience through pity and fear
rubric: Aristotle described catharsis as the emotional release tragedy provides for its audience.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The tragic flaw (hamartia) is
options: A fatal weakness in the protagonist that leads to their downfall|A strength of the protagonist|A minor character flaw|The villain's weakness
answer: A fatal weakness in the protagonist that leads to their downfall
rubric: Hamartia is the error of judgment or character defect that triggers the tragic hero's downfall.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A Deus ex machina is
options: An improbable plot device used to resolve a conflict suddenly|A type of stage direction|A dramatic soliloquy|A chorus in Greek drama
answer: An improbable plot device used to resolve a conflict suddenly
rubric: Deus ex machina (god from the machine) refers to an artificially introduced resolution to an unresolvable plot.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Greek drama traditionally used a chorus to
options: Comment on the action and provide background to the audience|Perform the main action|Play the antagonist|Represent individual characters
answer: Comment on the action and provide background to the audience
rubric: The Greek chorus was a group of performers who commented on events, voiced community opinion and set the moral tone.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An act in a play is
options: A major division of the play|A single scene|A stage direction|An actor's monologue
answer: A major division of the play
rubric: Acts are the main structural units of a play, subdivided into scenes.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A scene in drama is
options: A subdivision of an act marked by a change in setting or action|The entire play|The opening monologue|A stage direction
answer: A subdivision of an act marked by a change in setting or action
rubric: Scenes divide acts into smaller units, each with its own location and segment of action.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Conflict in drama is essential because
options: It creates tension and drives the plot|It provides comic relief|It describes the setting|It introduces the theme in the prologue

answer: Direct quotations and specific references from the text
rubric: Textual evidence anchors literary analysis to what the work actually says.

subject: Literature in English
stem: When comparing two poems, a student should examine
options: Similarities and differences in theme, form, language and effect|Only the themes|Only the lengths|Only the poets' names
answer: Similarities and differences in theme, form, language and effect
rubric: Comparative analysis evaluates both shared concerns and contrasting approaches across the texts.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A literary evaluation states
options: Whether the writer achieves their intended purpose and how effectively|A personal preference only|A factual summary|A list of characters
answer: Whether the writer achieves their intended purpose and how effectively
rubric: Evaluation goes beyond description to assess the quality and effectiveness of the writing.

subject: Literature in English
stem: In critical appreciation, a candidate should avoid
options: Retelling the story without comment on language or technique|Quoting from the text|Using technical literary terms|Writing in paragraphs
answer: Retelling the story without comment on language or technique
rubric: Mere narration (story-telling) rather than literary analysis is the most common weakness in critical appreciation answers.

subject: Literature in English
stem: An empathetic reading of a character means
options: Attempting to understand the character's feelings and motivations from within their perspective|Agreeing with everything the character does|Criticising the character|Describing the character's appearance
answer: Attempting to understand the character's feelings and motivations from within their perspective
rubric: Empathetic reading helps in understanding why characters behave as they do.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The historical context of a literary work refers to
options: The social, political and cultural circumstances in which it was written|The length of the text|The number of editions published|The author's age
answer: The social, political and cultural circumstances in which it was written
rubric: Historical context illuminates why certain themes, characters and settings appear in a work.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Irony as an effect in critical appreciation is best described as
options: A gap between what is said or shown and what is actually meant or true|Simple humour|A type of comparison|Repetition for emphasis
answer: A gap between what is said or shown and what is actually meant or true
rubric: Irony creates layers of meaning by exploiting the distance between appearance and reality.

subject: Literature in English
stem: In discussing the effectiveness of a writer's style, a student should comment on
options: Word choice, sentence structure, use of figurative language and effect on the reader|Only the plot|The number of pages|The publisher
answer: Word choice, sentence structure, use of figurative language and effect on the reader
rubric: Style analysis examines how the writer's linguistic choices achieve their communicative purpose.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Skimming is a reading technique used to
options: Get a general overview of a text quickly|Read every word carefully|Memorise details|Identify every figure of speech
answer: Get a general overview of a text quickly
rubric: Skimming involves reading quickly to grasp the main ideas without focusing on detail.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Scanning is a reading technique used to
options: Locate specific information in a text quickly|Read for general understanding|Analyse literary devices|Memorise the text
answer: Locate specific information in a text quickly
rubric: Scanning involves moving the eye rapidly over the text to find a specific fact or figure.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Intensive reading is
options: Reading carefully and in detail for full comprehension|Reading quickly for main ideas|Skipping difficult words|Reading only the introduction
answer: Reading carefully and in detail for full comprehension
rubric: Intensive reading is used for academic texts where close understanding of every sentence is required.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Extensive reading is
options: Reading widely for pleasure and general understanding|Reading every word carefully|Reading only literary texts|Reading only past examination papers
answer: Reading widely for pleasure and general understanding
rubric: Extensive reading builds vocabulary and fluency through exposure to large amounts of text.

subject: Literature in English
stem: The SQ3R reading strategy stands for
options: Survey, Question, Read, Recite and Review|Skim, Question, Read, Revise and Record|Study, Question, Read, Recall and Revise|Scan, Question, Read, React and Review
answer: Survey, Question, Read, Recite and Review
rubric: SQ3R is a structured reading strategy that enhances comprehension and retention.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Predicting while reading means
options: Using clues in the text to anticipate what will come next|Memorising the text|Reading backwards|Skipping difficult passages
answer: Using clues in the text to anticipate what will come next
rubric: Prediction is an active reading strategy that improves engagement and comprehension.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Making connections while reading involves
options: Linking what is read to personal experience, other texts or the wider world|Reading the text repeatedly|Using a dictionary constantly|Avoiding difficult passages
answer: Linking what is read to personal experience, other texts or the wider world
rubric: Making connections deepens understanding by placing the text in a broader context.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Visualising as a reading strategy means
options: Creating mental images of what is described in the text|Drawing pictures in a book|Watching a film|Memorising vocabulary
answer: Creating mental images of what is described in the text
rubric: Visualisation enhances comprehension and memory by turning verbal descriptions into mental pictures.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Note-taking while reading is useful because
options: It helps organise key information and aids memory|It lengthens reading time only|It replaces the need to re-read|It is only for examination purposes
answer: It helps organise key information and aids memory
rubric: Effective note-taking captures the most important ideas in an organised form for review.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A reading journal is
options: A record of texts read, personal reactions and key ideas|A list of vocabulary words only|A grammar exercise book|A writing exercise book
answer: A record of texts read, personal reactions and key ideas
rubric: A reading journal promotes reflective reading and builds critical thinking skills.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Finding the topic sentence of a paragraph helps because
options: It states the main idea that the rest of the paragraph develops|It is always the last sentence|It contains only details|It is never important for comprehension
answer: It states the main idea that the rest of the paragraph develops
rubric: The topic sentence (usually the first) announces the paragraph's central idea.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Distinguishing between fact and opinion in a text means
options: Identifying statements that are objectively verifiable versus those that express views|Reading only for facts|Reading only for opinions|Reading the author's biography
answer: Identifying statements that are objectively verifiable versus those that express views
rubric: Critical reading requires distinguishing evidence-based claims from personal or subjective statements.

subject: Literature in English
stem: A transitional word like "however" in a passage signals
options: A contrast or shift in the argument|An addition to a previous point|A conclusion|An example
answer: A contrast or shift in the argument
rubric: Transitional words guide readers through the logical structure of a text.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Previewing a text before reading involves
options: Looking at headings, subheadings, pictures and the introduction to anticipate content|Reading every word from the beginning|Memorising the title|Skipping to the conclusion
answer: Looking at headings, subheadings, pictures and the introduction to anticipate content
rubric: Previewing activates prior knowledge and sets a purpose for reading.

subject: Literature in English
stem: Metacognition in reading means
options: Thinking about and monitoring your own reading process and comprehension|Reading without thinking|Summarising after reading|Memorising vocabulary lists
answer: Thinking about and monitoring your own reading process and comprehension
rubric: Metacognitive readers self-monitor their understanding and apply strategies when comprehension breaks down.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Physical Education is defined as
options: Education through and for physical activity that develops the whole person|Only competitive sports training|Only classroom health theory|Military drill training
answer: Education through and for physical activity that develops the whole person
rubric: PHE develops physical, mental, emotional and social well-being through movement and sport.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The ancient Olympic Games were first held in
options: Olympia, Greece|Athens, Greece|Rome, Italy|Sparta, Greece
answer: Olympia, Greece
rubric: The ancient Olympics began in 776 BC in Olympia, dedicated to Zeus.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The modern Olympic Games were revived by
options: Pierre de Coubertin|Jesse Owens|Avery Brundage|Thomas Arnold
answer: Pierre de Coubertin
rubric: Baron Pierre de Coubertin founded the International Olympic Committee and revived the Olympics in 1896.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The first modern Olympic Games were held in
options: Athens, Greece in 1896|Paris in 1900|London in 1908|Stockholm in 1912
answer: Athens, Greece in 1896
rubric: The first modern Games were held in Athens in 1896.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The motto of the Olympic Games is
options: Faster, Higher, Stronger|Play Fair, Win Well|Swifter, Stronger, Brighter|Run, Jump, Throw
answer: Faster, Higher, Stronger
rubric: The Olympic motto "Citius, Altius, Fortius" means Faster, Higher, Stronger.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Physical Education was introduced into Nigerian schools primarily by
options: British colonial administration|Indigenous leaders|American missionaries|French influence
answer: British colonial administration
rubric: PHE was introduced into Nigerian schools by British colonial administrators as part of the formal curriculum.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The objectives of Physical Education include
options: Physical development, social development and mental development|Only competitive success|Only fitness testing|Only recreation
answer: Physical development, social development and mental development
rubric: PHE objectives span physical, cognitive, social, emotional and moral development.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Sport is best described as
options: A competitive physical activity governed by rules|Any leisure activity|A form of exercise only|A government programme
answer: A competitive physical activity governed by rules
rubric: Sport involves structured competition, rules, physical skill and often institutions.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The All Africa Games is a multi-sport event held
options: Every four years involving African nations|Annually for West Africa only|Every two years in South Africa only|Biannually in Nigeria
answer: Every four years involving African nations
rubric: The All Africa Games (African Games) is a continental multi-sport event held every four years.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Nigeria won its first Olympic gold medal in
options: Atlanta 1996 (football)|Mexico 1968|Sydney 2000|Barcelona 1992
answer: Atlanta 1996 (football)
rubric: The Nigerian Super Eagles won gold at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics football tournament.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The Commonwealth Games is a multi-sport event involving
options: Nations that were formerly part of the British Empire|Only African nations|Only European nations|Only Asian nations
answer: Nations that were formerly part of the British Empire
rubric: The Commonwealth Games takes place every four years among Commonwealth member nations.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Physical fitness is defined as
options: The ability of the body to carry out daily tasks efficiently without undue fatigue|Only speed and strength|Only weight management|Flexibility alone
answer: The ability of the body to carry out daily tasks efficiently without undue fatigue
rubric: Physical fitness encompasses cardiorespiratory endurance, strength, flexibility, body composition and more.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Recreation is
options: Voluntary activity done in leisure time for enjoyment and refreshment|Compulsory exercise|A form of competitive sport|A school subject only
answer: Voluntary activity done in leisure time for enjoyment and refreshment
rubric: Recreation restores energy and well-being through pleasurable, freely chosen activity.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The Nigeria Olympic Committee (NOC) is responsible for
options: Coordinating Nigeria's participation in the Olympic Games|Governing football in Nigeria|Setting school PE curricula|Managing professional basketball
answer: Coordinating Nigeria's participation in the Olympic Games
rubric: The NOC selects and sends athletes to the Olympic, Commonwealth and All Africa Games on behalf of Nigeria.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The National Sports Commission in Nigeria is responsible for
options: Overseeing and developing sports at the national level|Setting school curriculum only|Managing Olympic finances|Organising local recreation
answer: Overseeing and developing sports at the national level
rubric: The National Sports Commission/Ministry of Sports oversees sports policy, funding and development in Nigeria.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The human skeleton performs which of the following functions?
options: Support, protection, movement, blood cell production and mineral storage|Only support and protection|Only movement|Only mineral storage
answer: Support, protection, movement, blood cell production and mineral storage
rubric: The skeleton provides structural support, protects organs, enables movement via muscle attachment and produces blood cells.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The femur is the bone located in the
options: Thigh|Upper arm|Lower leg|Forearm
answer: Thigh
rubric: The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, located in the thigh.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A joint is
options: The point where two or more bones meet|A type of muscle|A bone in the spine|A ligament
answer: The point where two or more bones meet
rubric: Joints allow movement and are classified by structure and range of motion.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A ball-and-socket joint allows
options: Movement in all directions|Movement in one plane only|No movement|Only rotation
answer: Movement in all directions
rubric: Ball-and-socket joints (hip, shoulder) allow flexion, extension, abduction, adduction and rotation.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A hinge joint allows movement in
options: One plane (flexion and extension only)|All directions|Only rotation|No movement
answer: One plane (flexion and extension only)
rubric: Hinge joints (elbow, knee) act like a door hinge, allowing only flexion and extension.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Ligaments connect
options: Bone to bone|Muscle to bone|Muscle to muscle|Skin to bone
answer: Bone to bone
rubric: Ligaments are fibrous connective tissues that hold bones together at joints.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Tendons connect
options: Muscle to bone|Bone to bone|Muscle to muscle|Bone to skin
answer: Muscle to bone
rubric: Tendons transmit the force generated by muscles to move bones.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cartilage in a joint acts as
options: A smooth, shock-absorbing surface between bones|A type of ligament|A bone that grows|A muscle attachment
answer: A smooth, shock-absorbing surface between bones
rubric: Articular cartilage reduces friction and absorbs impact in joints.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The three types of muscle tissue are
options: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac|Voluntary, involuntary and mixed|Fast, slow and mixed|Flexor, extensor and rotator
answer: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac
rubric: Skeletal muscle moves bones, smooth muscle lines organs and cardiac muscle forms the heart.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Skeletal muscles are described as voluntary because
options: They are under conscious control|They work automatically|They are found in organs|They never tire
answer: They are under conscious control
rubric: Skeletal (striated) muscles contract in response to conscious nerve signals.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Muscle hypertrophy means
options: An increase in muscle size due to training|A reduction in muscle size|Muscle injury|Muscle fatigue
answer: An increase in muscle size due to training
rubric: Hypertrophy results from resistance training stimulating protein synthesis and muscle fibre enlargement.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The antagonist muscle in a movement is
options: The muscle that opposes or relaxes while the agonist contracts|The main muscle producing the movement|A muscle attached to the spine|A muscle in the forearm only
answer: The muscle that opposes or relaxes while the agonist contracts
rubric: Agonist and antagonist pairs work together to produce controlled movement.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The spine (vertebral column) consists of how many vertebrae?
rubric: The vertebral column has 33 vertebrae: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 fused sacral and 4 fused coccygeal.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Osteoporosis is a condition in which
options: Bones become weak and brittle due to reduced bone density|Muscles enlarge|Joints become inflamed|The spine curves forward
answer: Bones become weak and brittle due to reduced bone density
rubric: Osteoporosis increases fracture risk, especially in older adults; weight-bearing exercise helps prevent it.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The synovial fluid in a joint functions to
options: Lubricate the joint and reduce friction|Connect muscles to bones|Produce blood cells|Carry oxygen to the joint
answer: Lubricate the joint and reduce friction
rubric: Synovial fluid nourishes cartilage and minimises wear on joint surfaces.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Flexion is a movement that
options: Decreases the angle at a joint|Increases the angle at a joint|Moves a limb away from the midline|Moves a limb toward the midline
answer: Decreases the angle at a joint
rubric: Flexion reduces the angle between body segments (e.g., bending the elbow).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Extension is a movement that
options: Increases the angle at a joint|Decreases the angle at a joint|Rotates a limb|Moves a limb sideways
answer: Increases the angle at a joint
rubric: Extension increases the joint angle (e.g., straightening the knee).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Abduction is
options: Moving a limb away from the midline of the body|Moving a limb toward the midline|Decreasing a joint angle|Rotating a limb
answer: Moving a limb away from the midline of the body
rubric: Abduction moves a segment away from the body centre; adduction brings it back.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The biceps brachii is the prime mover for
options: Flexion of the elbow|Extension of the knee|Abduction of the shoulder|Rotation of the hip
answer: Flexion of the elbow
rubric: The biceps brachii contracts to flex the elbow, e.g., during a bicep curl.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Red bone marrow is responsible for
options: Producing red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets|Storing fat|Absorbing calcium|Producing hormones
answer: Producing red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets
rubric: Red bone marrow is the site of haematopoiesis (blood cell production).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The health-related components of physical fitness include
options: Cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition|Only speed and agility|Only strength and power|Only balance and coordination
answer: Cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition
rubric: Health-related fitness components directly affect overall health and quality of life.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cardiorespiratory endurance is the ability of
options: The heart, lungs and circulatory system to supply oxygen during prolonged exercise|The muscles to exert maximum force|The body to move through a full range of motion|The body to maintain balance
answer: The heart, lungs and circulatory system to supply oxygen during prolonged exercise
rubric: Cardiorespiratory endurance is measured by VO2 max and improved by aerobic training.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Muscular strength is
options: The maximum force a muscle can exert in a single effort|The ability to repeat muscular contractions|Flexibility of the muscle|Speed of muscular contraction
answer: The maximum force a muscle can exert in a single effort
rubric: Muscular strength is developed through resistance training with high loads and low repetitions.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Muscular endurance is
options: The ability of a muscle to sustain repeated contractions over time|Maximum force in one effort|Range of joint motion|Speed of reaction
answer: The ability of a muscle to sustain repeated contractions over time
rubric: Muscular endurance is trained with lower resistance and higher repetitions.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Flexibility is
options: The range of motion available at a joint|Maximum force of a muscle|Speed of movement|Cardiorespiratory fitness
answer: The range of motion available at a joint
rubric: Flexibility is improved by stretching exercises and is important for injury prevention and performance.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Body composition refers to
options: The proportion of fat mass to lean mass in the body|The shape of the body|The height and weight ratio only|The amount of water in the body
answer: The proportion of fat mass to lean mass in the body
rubric: Body composition distinguishes fat tissue from muscle, bone and other lean tissue.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: BMI (Body Mass Index) is calculated as
options: Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared|Height divided by weight|Weight multiplied by height|Waist circumference divided by height
answer: Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared
rubric: BMI = kg/m^2, providing a simple screening index for weight status.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Aerobic exercise is
options: Exercise sustained for a long period using oxygen to produce energy|Short, explosive bursts of maximum effort|Stretching exercises|Breathing exercises only
answer: Exercise sustained for a long period using oxygen to produce energy
rubric: Aerobic (with oxygen) exercise includes jogging, swimming and cycling; it improves cardiorespiratory endurance.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Anaerobic exercise involves
options: High-intensity exercise where energy is produced without oxygen|Low-intensity long-duration activity|Breathing exercises|Flexibility training
answer: High-intensity exercise where energy is produced without oxygen
rubric: Anaerobic exercise (sprinting, weight lifting) relies on stored ATP and glycolysis rather than oxygen.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The FITT principle in exercise programming stands for
options: Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type|Fitness, Intensity, Training and Technique|Flexibility, Interval, Time and Type|Frequency, Interval, Technique and Training
answer: Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type
rubric: FITT guides exercise prescription by defining how often, how hard, how long and what type of activity.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The principle of overload in training means
options: The body must be challenged beyond its current level to improve|The body must be rested more than it is exercised|Training must stay at the same level|Exercise must be done every day
answer: The body must be challenged beyond its current level to improve
rubric: Progressive overload gradually increases training stimulus to drive adaptation.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The principle of specificity states that
options: Training adaptations are specific to the type of exercise performed|All exercise produces the same results|Only aerobic training is beneficial|Strength training improves flexibility
answer: Training adaptations are specific to the type of exercise performed
rubric: Specificity means a sprinter must do sprint training, not only endurance running, to improve.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Warm-up before exercise is important to
options: Gradually increase heart rate, blood flow and muscle temperature to reduce injury risk|Improve strength immediately|Replace the main workout|Cool down the body
answer: Gradually increase heart rate, blood flow and muscle temperature to reduce injury risk
rubric: Warming up prepares the cardiovascular and musculoskeletal systems for the demands of exercise.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cool-down after exercise helps to
options: Gradually return the body to its resting state and prevent blood pooling|Increase heart rate|Prepare for the next set|Increase muscle soreness
answer: Gradually return the body to its resting state and prevent blood pooling
rubric: Cool-down (low-intensity movement and stretching) aids recovery and reduces post-exercise stiffness.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: VO2 max is
options: The maximum rate at which the body can consume oxygen during intense exercise|The maximum speed of running|The maximum weight a person can lift|The maximum number of sit-ups
answer: The maximum rate at which the body can consume oxygen during intense exercise
rubric: VO2 max is the gold standard measure of aerobic fitness capacity.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The skill-related components of fitness include
options: Speed, agility, balance, coordination, reaction time and power|Only strength and endurance|Only flexibility|Only body composition
answer: Speed, agility, balance, coordination, reaction time and power
rubric: Skill-related fitness components are important for sports performance and motor skill acquisition.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Agility is
options: The ability to change direction quickly and accurately|Maximum running speed|Muscular strength|Cardiovascular endurance
answer: The ability to change direction quickly and accurately
rubric: Agility combines speed, balance and coordination to enable rapid directional changes.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Power in sports refers to
options: The combination of strength and speed (force x velocity)|Endurance alone|Flexibility only|Reaction time only
answer: The combination of strength and speed (force x velocity)
rubric: Power = force x velocity; it is critical in jumping, throwing and sprinting.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Reaction time is
options: The time between a stimulus and the initiation of a response|The time to run 100 metres|The time to complete a workout|The time to recover after exercise
answer: The time between a stimulus and the initiation of a response
rubric: Reaction time is critical in many sports and is partly innate but can be improved with practice.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Circuit training is
options: A form of training where different exercises are performed at stations with minimal rest|Training only in the gym|Only swimming laps|Only running long distances
answer: A form of training where different exercises are performed at stations with minimal rest
rubric: Circuit training develops multiple fitness components by combining strength and endurance exercises.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The standard distance for the 100 metres sprint is
options: 100 metres on a straight track|One lap of the track|200 metres|400 metres
answer: 100 metres on a straight track
rubric: The 100m is the shortest standard sprint, run in a straight line on the track.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A relay race involves
options: A team of four athletes each running a leg and passing a baton|One athlete running four laps|Two athletes alternating laps|A race with hurdles
answer: A team of four athletes each running a leg and passing a baton
rubric: Relay races (4x100m, 4x400m) require baton exchanges within a designated zone.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The baton exchange zone in a relay race is
options: 20 metres long|10 metres long|30 metres long|40 metres long
answer: 20 metres long
rubric: The exchange zone is 20 metres; the outgoing runner must receive the baton within this zone.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In a hurdles race, the athlete must
options: Clear the hurdles without knocking them over (though knocking them is not disqualifying)|Jump over all hurdles without touching them|Only sprint between hurdles|Carry the hurdle to the finish
answer: Clear the hurdles without knocking them over (though knocking them is not disqualifying)
rubric: Hitting a hurdle is not automatic disqualification, but it costs time and may unbalance the athlete.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The men's 110m hurdles event uses hurdles of height
options: 1.067 metres (3.5 feet)|1.0 metre|0.84 metres|0.91 metres
answer: 1.067 metres (3.5 feet)
rubric: Men's 110m hurdles use hurdles set at 1.067m; women's 100m hurdles are set at 0.84m.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The staggered start in sprint races is used to
options: Ensure all runners cover the same distance, compensating for the curve|Give slower runners an advantage|Allow runners to start at different times|Reduce the length of the race
answer: Ensure all runners cover the same distance, compensating for the curve
rubric: Staggered starts offset runners in outer lanes so all travel the same total distance.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Disqualification in a sprint occurs if
options: A runner makes two false starts (under current IAAF rules, one false start leads to disqualification)|A runner stumbles|A runner runs in the wrong lane by accident|A runner slows before the finish
answer: A runner makes two false starts (under current IAAF rules, one false start leads to disqualification)
rubric: Under current IAAF rules, any athlete who false-starts is disqualified.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The 400m race is run
options: Once around a standard 400m track|Twice around the track|On a straight only|For four laps
answer: Once around a standard 400m track
rubric: The 400m is one complete lap of a standard athletics track.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In a 4x100m relay, the baton must be passed
options: Within the 20-metre exchange zone|Anywhere on the track|Only at the start|Between the 200m and 300m marks
answer: Within the 20-metre exchange zone
rubric: A baton passed outside the exchange zone results in disqualification.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Starting blocks are used by sprinters to
options: Provide a firm surface for a powerful explosive start|Slow the runner at the start|Mark the finish line|Serve as hurdles
answer: Provide a firm surface for a powerful explosive start
rubric: Starting blocks allow sprinters to drive off with maximum force at the gun.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The marathon is a road race of approximately
options: 42.195 kilometres|26 miles and 385 yards (same as 42.195 km)|10 kilometres|21 kilometres
answer: 42.195 kilometres
rubric: The marathon distance of 42.195km commemorates the legendary run of Pheidippides from Marathon to Athens.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Track events are measured from
options: The inside edge of the runner's lane|The outside edge|The centre of the track|The finish line backwards
answer: The inside edge of the runner's lane
rubric: Track distances are measured 0.3m from the inner edge of each lane.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The 1500m race is often called
options: The metric mile|The half marathon|The quarter mile|The sprint
answer: The metric mile
rubric: The 1500m is approximately one mile (1609m) and is commonly called the "metric mile."

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In the 3000m steeplechase, athletes must clear
options: Water jumps and barriers placed on the track|Only hurdles|Only water jumps|No obstacles
answer: Water jumps and barriers placed on the track
rubric: The steeplechase includes fixed barriers and a water jump on each lap.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The photo finish in sprint races is used to
options: Determine the exact finishing order when athletes are very close|Allow athletes to slow down|Provide a record of technique|Determine false starts
answer: Determine the exact finishing order when athletes are very close
rubric: Photo finish technology captures the exact moment athletes cross the finish line to determine placements.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A standard athletics track has how many lanes?
rubric: A standard IAAF competition track has 8 lanes.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The 800m race is run
options: For two laps of a standard 400m track|For one lap|For four laps|On a straight only
answer: For two laps of a standard 400m track
rubric: The 800m is a middle-distance event covering two laps of the standard track.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Walking events in athletics require
options: One foot to remain in contact with the ground at all times|Alternate hopping|Running occasionally|No specific foot rule
answer: One foot to remain in contact with the ground at all times
rubric: Race walking has a strict rule that one foot must always be on the ground.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The finishing line in a race is
options: Where the torso (not the head or limbs) first crosses the finish|Where the feet first cross|Where the head first crosses|Where any part of the body first crosses
answer: Where the torso (not the head or limbs) first crosses the finish
rubric: IAAF rules state that the winner is determined by which torso crosses the finish line first.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cross-country running differs from track events in that
options: It is run over natural terrain|It uses a synthetic track|It uses hurdles|It is always 100 metres
answer: It is run over natural terrain
rubric: Cross-country involves running over varied natural surfaces including grass, mud and hills.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Field events in athletics are divided into
options: Jumping and throwing events|Only running events|Only hurdle events|Only relay events
answer: Jumping and throwing events
rubric: Field events include long jump, high jump, triple jump, pole vault, shot put, discus, hammer and javelin.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The Fosbury Flop is a technique used in
options: High jump|Long jump|Triple jump|Pole vault
answer: High jump
rubric: The Fosbury Flop (back-first over the bar) was invented by Dick Fosbury and revolutionised high jumping.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In the long jump, the athlete takes off from
options: A take-off board|Any position on the runway|A sandpit|A springboard
answer: A take-off board
rubric: The long jumper must take off from behind the plasticine-edged take-off board; overstepping is a foul.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The triple jump consists of
options: A hop, a step and a jump|Three long jumps|A run, a jump and a land|A jump, a spin and a land
answer: A hop, a step and a jump
rubric: The triple jump sequence is hop (same foot landing), step (other foot) and jump (into the pit).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The shot put involves
options: Putting a heavy metal ball as far as possible from a circular throwing area|Throwing a disc|Throwing a javelin|Jumping as far as possible
answer: Putting a heavy metal ball as far as possible from a circular throwing area
rubric: The shot is pushed (not thrown) from the shoulder from within a 2.135m circle.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The discus is thrown from
options: A circular throwing area with a cage|A straight runway|A sandpit|A pole vault area
answer: A circular throwing area with a cage
rubric: The discus throw uses a 2.5m circle surrounded by a cage to protect spectators.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The javelin must land
options: Point first within the landing sector|Flat on the ground|Outside the sector|On its tail end
answer: Point first within the landing sector
rubric: A valid javelin throw requires the tip to touch the ground first within the sector.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In field events, athletes are typically given
options: Three attempts in qualifying and three more in the final for top athletes|Only one attempt|Six attempts in all rounds|Two attempts only
answer: Three attempts in qualifying and three more in the final for top athletes
rubric: Top athletes from qualifying get three additional throws/jumps in the final.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Pole vault is an event where
options: Athletes use a flexible pole to propel themselves over a high bar|Athletes vault over a net|Athletes jump from a springboard|Athletes use a rigid pole
answer: Athletes use a flexible pole to propel themselves over a high bar
rubric: The pole vaulter uses the pole's flexion to convert horizontal momentum into vertical height.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In the high jump, what constitutes a failed attempt?
options: Dislodging the crossbar|Touching the mat without attempting|Running past the bar|Taking more than 30 seconds
answer: Dislodging the crossbar
rubric: A failed high jump attempt occurs when the crossbar is displaced by the athlete during the jump.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The hammer throw uses
options: A metal ball attached to a wire and handle, thrown from a circle|A wooden disc|A metal spear|A shot put ball with a rope
answer: A metal ball attached to a wire and handle, thrown from a circle
rubric: The hammer is a 7.26kg (men) or 4kg (women) metal ball on a steel wire.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A no-throw in throwing events occurs when
options: The athlete steps outside the circle before the implement lands|The throw lands outside the sector|The throw is too short|The implement lands in the sector
answer: The athlete steps outside the circle before the implement lands
rubric: Any contact with the top edge or outside of the circle before the implement lands is a foul.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The decathlon in athletics consists of
options: Ten events spread over two days|Five events in one day|Twenty events|Eight events
answer: Ten events spread over two days
rubric: The decathlon (men) combines 100m, long jump, shot put, high jump, 400m on day one and 110m hurdles, discus, pole vault, javelin, 1500m on day two.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The heptathlon is
options: A women's multi-event competition of seven events|A men's ten-event competition|A relay competition|A combined road and track event
answer: A women's multi-event competition of seven events
rubric: The women's heptathlon comprises 100m hurdles, high jump, shot put, 200m, long jump, javelin and 800m.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The landing area for the long jump and triple jump is filled with
