options: Sand|Rubber mats|Grass|Water
answer: Sand
rubric: The sand pit provides a safe landing surface and enables measurement of jump distance.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In association football, a match consists of
options: Two halves of 45 minutes each|Two halves of 40 minutes|Four quarters of 15 minutes|Three periods of 30 minutes
answer: Two halves of 45 minutes each
rubric: A standard football match is 90 minutes (2 x 45 minutes) with added time.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A football team has how many players on the field?
rubric: Each team fields 11 players including a goalkeeper.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The offside rule in football means
options: A player is in an offside position if they are nearer to the opponent's goal than the ball and the second-to-last defender|A player cannot cross the halfway line|Players must stay in their half|There is no such rule
answer: A player is in an offside position if they are nearer to the opponent's goal than the ball and the second-to-last defender
rubric: Offside is one of football's most important rules, preventing players from camping near the opponent's goal.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A penalty kick in football is awarded for
options: A foul committed by a defending player inside their own penalty area|Any foul anywhere on the pitch|A foul outside the penalty area|Offside near the goal
answer: A foul committed by a defending player inside their own penalty area
rubric: Penalty kicks are taken from the penalty spot, 12 yards from goal.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In basketball, a field goal from inside the three-point line scores
options: 2 points|1 point|3 points|4 points
answer: 2 points
rubric: Baskets made from inside the arc score 2 points; from outside score 3; free throws score 1.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The duration of a standard basketball game (NBA) is
options: Four quarters of 12 minutes each|Two halves of 20 minutes|Two halves of 40 minutes|Four quarters of 10 minutes
answer: Four quarters of 12 minutes each
rubric: NBA games consist of four 12-minute quarters; FIBA games use four 10-minute quarters.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In volleyball, a team scores when
options: The ball touches the floor in the opponent's court or the opponent commits a fault|A player hits the ball twice|A player touches the net|The ball goes out on your side
answer: The ball touches the floor in the opponent's court or the opponent commits a fault
rubric: Rally-point scoring means every rally results in a point for the winning team.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A volleyball team is allowed how many contacts before returning the ball?
options: Three|Two|Four|One
answer: Three
rubric: A team may touch the ball a maximum of three times (typically: dig, set, spike) before sending it over.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In basketball, travelling refers to
options: Moving with the ball without dribbling|Shooting from outside the key|Fouling a player|Running faster than opponents
answer: Moving with the ball without dribbling
rubric: Travelling is a violation where a player takes more than the allowed steps without dribbling.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The goalkeeper in football is the only player allowed to
options: Handle the ball with their hands (within the penalty area)|Tackle from behind|Score directly from kick-off|Carry the ball to the centre circle
answer: Handle the ball with their hands (within the penalty area)
rubric: The goalkeeper may use their hands to stop or catch the ball only within their penalty area.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In netball, the goal shooter (GS) can only enter which areas?
options: The goal circle and goal third of the court|The entire court|The centre and goal thirds|The centre third only
answer: The goal circle and goal third of the court
rubric: Each netball position has designated court areas; GS is restricted to the goal circle and attacking goal third.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A free kick in football that goes directly into the goal is called
options: A direct free kick goal|An indirect free kick goal|A penalty|A corner kick
answer: A direct free kick goal
rubric: A direct free kick can result in a goal without another player touching the ball.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In volleyball, a block counts as
options: The first of the three allowed contacts|Not a contact|The second contact only|Two contacts
answer: The first of the three allowed contacts
rubric: Under FIVB rules, a block touch counts as the team's first contact.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The libero in volleyball is
options: A specialised defensive player who cannot serve or attack above the net|A player who only serves|The team captain|A player who only attacks
answer: A specialised defensive player who cannot serve or attack above the net
rubric: The libero wears a different colour jersey and specialises in back-row defence and reception.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A yellow card in football is a warning for
options: Unsporting behaviour or serious foul play|A minor infringement|An offside offence|Missing a penalty
answer: Unsporting behaviour or serious foul play
rubric: Yellow cards are cautions; two yellow cards in one match result in a red card (dismissal).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In basketball, a personal foul that puts a player over the limit results in
options: The opponent shooting free throws|A penalty kick|A corner kick|A disqualification immediately
answer: The opponent shooting free throws
rubric: When a team accumulates team fouls beyond the limit, subsequent fouls result in free throws.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The dimensions of a standard football pitch length are between
options: 100 and 110 metres|60 and 80 metres|50 and 70 metres|120 and 140 metres
answer: 100 and 110 metres
rubric: FIFA regulations allow pitches between 100-110m long and 64-75m wide for international matches.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Serving in volleyball must be performed
options: From behind the end line|From the centre of the court|From within the three-metre line|From any position
answer: From behind the end line
rubric: The server must stand behind the end line (baseline) during the serve.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In football, a corner kick is awarded when
options: The ball crosses the goal line last touched by a defending player|The ball crosses the goal line last touched by an attacker|The goalkeeper holds the ball too long|A penalty is saved
answer: The ball crosses the goal line last touched by a defending player
rubric: When a defender last touches the ball before it goes out over their own goal line, a corner kick is awarded.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A hat-trick in football means
options: One player scores three goals in a single match|A team scores three goals|Three different players score|A player scores with a header
answer: One player scores three goals in a single match
rubric: A hat-trick is three goals by the same player in one game.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Health is defined by the World Health Organization as
options: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease|The absence of illness only|Physical fitness only|Emotional happiness alone
answer: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease
rubric: The WHO 1948 definition broadens health beyond the absence of disease to encompass holistic well-being.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Personal hygiene includes
options: Regular bathing, dental care, handwashing and clean clothing|Only bathing|Only dental care|Only handwashing
answer: Regular bathing, dental care, handwashing and clean clothing
rubric: Personal hygiene practices prevent infection and promote physical and social well-being.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Communicable diseases are
options: Diseases that can be passed from one person to another|Diseases caused only by diet|Diseases that are always fatal|Non-infectious conditions
answer: Diseases that can be passed from one person to another
rubric: Communicable (infectious) diseases are transmitted by pathogens: bacteria, viruses, fungi, parasites.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Malaria is transmitted by
options: The bite of a female Anopheles mosquito|Contaminated water|Direct contact with an infected person|Airborne droplets
answer: The bite of a female Anopheles mosquito
rubric: The Plasmodium parasite causing malaria is injected into the bloodstream by the female Anopheles mosquito.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: HIV stands for
options: Human Immunodeficiency Virus|High Immunity Virus|Human Infectious Virus|Health Immunity Virus
answer: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
rubric: HIV attacks and weakens the immune system, potentially leading to AIDS.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: AIDS is the advanced stage of HIV infection where
options: The immune system is severely damaged and the person is vulnerable to opportunistic infections|The person is first exposed to HIV|HIV is transmitted|HIV is cured
answer: The immune system is severely damaged and the person is vulnerable to opportunistic infections
rubric: AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) is diagnosed when CD4 count falls below 200/mm3 or an AIDS-defining illness occurs.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The primary mode of HIV transmission is
options: Unprotected sexual intercourse|Casual contact such as handshaking|Sharing food|Mosquito bites
answer: Unprotected sexual intercourse
rubric: HIV is mainly transmitted through unprotected sex, sharing needles and mother-to-child transmission.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Vaccination works by
options: Stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies against a specific disease|Curing a disease after infection|Killing all bacteria in the body|Replacing damaged cells
answer: Stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies against a specific disease
rubric: Vaccines introduce antigens that train the immune system to recognise and fight specific pathogens.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Drug abuse refers to
options: Using a substance in a way not intended or prescribed, causing harm|Taking prescribed medication correctly|Drinking water|Using sunscreen
answer: Using a substance in a way not intended or prescribed, causing harm
rubric: Drug abuse involves misuse of legal or illegal substances in harmful ways.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The effects of alcohol abuse include
options: Liver damage, impaired judgment and addiction|Improved concentration|Increased physical fitness|Better sleep only
answer: Liver damage, impaired judgment and addiction
rubric: Chronic alcohol abuse damages the liver, brain and cardiovascular system and leads to dependency.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cholera is caused by
options: Vibrio cholerae bacteria, spread through contaminated water and food|A virus spread by mosquitoes|A fungal infection|Direct person-to-person skin contact
answer: Vibrio cholerae bacteria, spread through contaminated water and food
rubric: Cholera spreads through the faecal-oral route via contaminated water supplies.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The importance of immunization in public health is that it
options: Prevents the spread of infectious diseases and protects communities|Only helps the individual vaccinated|Cures all diseases|Replaces good hygiene
answer: Prevents the spread of infectious diseases and protects communities
rubric: Immunisation creates herd immunity, reducing disease transmission even among the unvaccinated.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) include
options: Gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydia and HIV|Only HIV|Only herpes|Only malaria
answer: Gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydia and HIV
rubric: STIs are infections primarily transmitted through sexual contact; some can also be transmitted by blood or during birth.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Environmental health is concerned with
options: Factors in the environment that affect human health, such as water, sanitation and air quality|Only physical fitness|Only mental health|Only diet
answer: Factors in the environment that affect human health, such as water, sanitation and air quality
rubric: Environmental health addresses the impact of physical, chemical and biological environmental factors on human health.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Safe drinking water prevents
options: Waterborne diseases like cholera, typhoid and dysentery|Only malaria|Only skin diseases|STIs
answer: Waterborne diseases like cholera, typhoid and dysentery
rubric: Access to clean water is fundamental to preventing faecal-oral route infections.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Tobacco smoking is a risk factor for
options: Lung cancer, cardiovascular disease and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease|Only bad breath|Only yellow teeth|Only stress
answer: Lung cancer, cardiovascular disease and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
rubric: Tobacco smoke contains over 70 carcinogens and is the leading preventable cause of cancer.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: NAFDAC in Nigeria is responsible for
options: Regulating food, drugs and cosmetics to protect public health|Building hospitals|Training doctors|Conducting elections
answer: Regulating food, drugs and cosmetics to protect public health
rubric: NAFDAC inspects, registers and monitors food, drugs and related products to prevent harm.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Mental health refers to
options: Emotional, psychological and social well-being|Only the absence of mental illness|Physical fitness only|Academic performance only
answer: Emotional, psychological and social well-being
rubric: Mental health affects how we think, feel and act; it encompasses positive functioning, not just the absence of disorder.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Exercise contributes to mental health by
options: Reducing stress, anxiety and depression through the release of endorphins|Increasing stress levels|Having no effect on mental health|Only improving sleep
answer: Reducing stress, anxiety and depression through the release of endorphins
rubric: Physical activity stimulates endorphin release, improves mood and reduces symptoms of anxiety and depression.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Adequate sleep is important for health because
options: It allows the body and brain to repair, consolidate memory and regulate hormones|It is only for children|It has no health benefit|It reduces physical fitness
answer: It allows the body and brain to repair, consolidate memory and regulate hormones
rubric: Sleep deprivation impairs cognition, immunity and emotional regulation.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Peer pressure in relation to drug use means
options: Being influenced by friends or age-mates to use drugs or alcohol|Using drugs alone|A parent forcing drug use|A medical prescription
answer: Being influenced by friends or age-mates to use drugs or alcohol
rubric: Peer pressure is a major factor in adolescent drug initiation; resistance skills are a key prevention strategy.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are
options: Chronic conditions not transmitted between people, such as diabetes, hypertension and cancer|Infectious diseases|Only genetic disorders|Only childhood diseases
answer: Chronic conditions not transmitted between people, such as diabetes, hypertension and cancer
rubric: NCDs are largely driven by lifestyle factors (diet, physical inactivity, smoking, alcohol).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A balanced diet provides
options: All essential nutrients in the right proportions for health|Only proteins|Only carbohydrates|Only vitamins and minerals
answer: All essential nutrients in the right proportions for health
rubric: A balanced diet includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water in appropriate amounts.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The spread of tuberculosis (TB) occurs mainly through
options: Inhaling airborne droplets expelled by an infected person|Contaminated water|Mosquito bites|Direct skin contact
answer: Inhaling airborne droplets expelled by an infected person
rubric: Tuberculosis is spread when an infected person coughs, sneezes or speaks, releasing airborne bacteria.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Primary prevention of disease focuses on
options: Preventing disease before it occurs through vaccination, hygiene and lifestyle modification|Treating disease after it occurs|Rehabilitating patients|Diagnosing disease early
answer: Preventing disease before it occurs through vaccination, hygiene and lifestyle modification
rubric: Primary prevention eliminates risk factors before disease develops.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: First aid is
options: The immediate care given to an injured or ill person before professional medical help arrives|Definitive medical treatment|A substitute for hospital care|Only CPR
answer: The immediate care given to an injured or ill person before professional medical help arrives
rubric: First aid is emergency care provided at the scene to preserve life, prevent worsening and promote recovery.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The aims of first aid can be summarised as
options: Preserve life, prevent worsening and promote recovery (the 3 Ps)|Diagnose disease, prescribe medicine and perform surgery|Only stop bleeding|Only give CPR
answer: Preserve life, prevent worsening and promote recovery (the 3 Ps)
rubric: The three P's guide all first aid priorities.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: CPR stands for
options: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation|Cardio-Pulmonary Recovery|Central Pressure Response|Controlled Pulse Restoration
answer: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
rubric: CPR combines chest compressions and rescue breaths to maintain circulation in cardiac arrest.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The recovery position is used to
options: Place an unconscious but breathing person on their side to prevent choking|Treat fractures|Stop bleeding|Treat burns
answer: Place an unconscious but breathing person on their side to prevent choking
rubric: The recovery position maintains the airway and allows fluid to drain, preventing aspiration.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: RICE stands for the first aid treatment for soft tissue injuries, meaning
options: Rest, Ice, Compression and Elevation|Resistance, Intensity, Core and Exercise|Relax, Immobilise, Cool and Elevate|Rest, Immobilise, Care and Exercise
answer: Rest, Ice, Compression and Elevation
rubric: RICE reduces swelling and pain in sprains and strains in the acute phase of injury.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A fracture is
options: A break or crack in a bone|A muscle tear|A joint dislocation|A bruise on the skin
answer: A break or crack in a bone
rubric: Fractures range from hairline cracks to complete breaks; management includes immobilisation.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A sprain is
options: An injury to a ligament caused by overstretching|A bone fracture|A muscle tear|A nerve injury
answer: An injury to a ligament caused by overstretching
rubric: Sprains occur when ligaments are stretched or torn, most commonly at the ankle.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A strain is
options: An injury to a muscle or tendon caused by overstretching|A ligament injury|A bone fracture|A joint dislocation
answer: An injury to a muscle or tendon caused by overstretching
rubric: Strains affect muscles or their tendons and are common in the hamstring and lower back.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: To control bleeding from a wound, the first step is
options: Apply direct pressure to the wound|Remove any object embedded in the wound|Apply a tourniquet immediately|Elevate the wound only
answer: Apply direct pressure to the wound
rubric: Direct pressure is the first and most effective means of controlling external bleeding.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A first-degree burn involves
options: Redness and pain of the outer skin layer only|Blistering and deeper tissue damage|Destruction of all skin layers|Charring of tissue
answer: Redness and pain of the outer skin layer only
rubric: First-degree (superficial) burns affect only the epidermis and heal quickly.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: For a minor burn, the first aid action is
options: Cool the burn under running water for at least 10 minutes|Apply butter or oil|Burst any blisters|Cover with an airtight bandage
answer: Cool the burn under running water for at least 10 minutes
rubric: Cooling reduces pain, limits tissue damage and prevents the burn from deepening.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Choking first aid for a conscious adult involves
options: Giving up to five back blows followed by up to five abdominal thrusts (Heimlich manoeuvre)|Laying the person flat|Giving water to drink|Waiting for natural resolution
answer: Giving up to five back blows followed by up to five abdominal thrusts (Heimlich manoeuvre)
rubric: The combination of back blows and abdominal thrusts dislodges a foreign body from the airway.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The Heimlich manoeuvre is used to
options: Relieve choking by delivering abdominal thrusts to expel a foreign object|Restart the heart|Treat snake bites|Reduce fracture pain
answer: Relieve choking by delivering abdominal thrusts to expel a foreign object
rubric: The Heimlich manoeuvre uses an upward thrust below the diaphragm to force air through the airway.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Hypothermia occurs when
options: The body's core temperature drops dangerously low|The body temperature rises above normal|A person is dehydrated|A person has heat stroke
answer: The body's core temperature drops dangerously low
rubric: Hypothermia sets in when core temperature falls below 35 degrees Celsius.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Heat stroke is a medical emergency because
options: The body's temperature regulation fails and core temperature rises dangerously|It causes only mild discomfort|It is the same as sunburn|It only affects athletes
answer: The body's temperature regulation fails and core temperature rises dangerously
rubric: Heat stroke can be fatal; it requires immediate cooling and emergency medical care.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: An epileptic seizure first aid measure is
options: Protect the person from injury and time the seizure; do not restrain them|Force something between their teeth|Hold the person down tightly|Give water immediately
answer: Protect the person from injury and time the seizure; do not restrain them
rubric: Restraining a person having a seizure can cause injury; the priority is to keep the environment safe.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A defibrillator (AED) is used to
options: Deliver an electric shock to restore normal heart rhythm in cardiac arrest|Give medications|Measure blood pressure|Perform CPR automatically
answer: Deliver an electric shock to restore normal heart rhythm in cardiac arrest
rubric: An AED analyses heart rhythm and delivers a shock to correct ventricular fibrillation.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: For a suspected spinal injury, the first aider should
options: Keep the casualty still and do not move them unless immediate danger exists|Move the casualty immediately|Flex the casualty's neck|Have the casualty sit up
answer: Keep the casualty still and do not move them unless immediate danger exists
rubric: Moving a casualty with a spinal injury can cause permanent paralysis; immobilisation is essential.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A sling is used in first aid to
options: Support and immobilise an injured arm or shoulder|Stop bleeding|Treat burns|Perform CPR
answer: Support and immobilise an injured arm or shoulder
rubric: A triangular bandage sling suspends the arm to reduce movement and pain at fracture or shoulder injuries.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The purpose of a first aid kit is
options: To provide the equipment and materials needed to give emergency treatment|To replace the hospital|To treat all diseases|To diagnose medical conditions
answer: To provide the equipment and materials needed to give emergency treatment
rubric: A first aid kit contains bandages, plasters, antiseptic, scissors and other essentials for emergency care.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Carbohydrates serve as the body's
options: Primary source of energy|Main structural material|Primary source of hormones|Main source of vitamins
answer: Primary source of energy
rubric: Carbohydrates are broken down to glucose, the body's preferred fuel.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Proteins are essential for
options: Growth, repair and maintenance of body tissues|Energy production only|Lubricating joints|Producing digestive enzymes only
answer: Growth, repair and maintenance of body tissues
rubric: Proteins are the body's building blocks, needed for muscle, enzymes, hormones and immune function.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Fats in the diet provide
options: A concentrated source of energy and fat-soluble vitamins|Structural material for bones|Fibre for digestion|Only cholesterol
answer: A concentrated source of energy and fat-soluble vitamins
rubric: Dietary fats supply 9 kcal/g, carry fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and are essential cell membrane components.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Vitamin C deficiency causes
options: Scurvy, characterised by bleeding gums and poor wound healing|Rickets|Night blindness|Anaemia
answer: Scurvy, characterised by bleeding gums and poor wound healing
rubric: Scurvy results from insufficient Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), which is needed for collagen synthesis.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Vitamin D deficiency in children causes
options: Rickets, a condition of soft and deformed bones|Scurvy|Night blindness|Pellagra
answer: Rickets, a condition of soft and deformed bones
rubric: Vitamin D is required for calcium absorption; deficiency leads to soft bones (rickets in children, osteomalacia in adults).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Anaemia can be caused by deficiency of
options: Iron, Vitamin B12 or folic acid|Vitamin C only|Vitamin D only|Calcium only
answer: Iron, Vitamin B12 or folic acid
rubric: Anaemia results from reduced haemoglobin; iron-deficiency, B12 deficiency and folate deficiency are common causes.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Dietary fibre is important because it
options: Aids digestion, prevents constipation and reduces risk of colorectal cancer|Provides large amounts of energy|Builds muscle|Produces hormones
answer: Aids digestion, prevents constipation and reduces risk of colorectal cancer
rubric: Dietary fibre (roughage) promotes healthy bowel function and has protective effects against certain diseases.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Water constitutes approximately what percentage of the human body?
rubric: Water makes up about 60-70% of body weight and is essential for every physiological process.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Dehydration during exercise impairs
options: Performance, concentration and temperature regulation|Only muscular strength|Only lung capacity|Only bone density
answer: Performance, concentration and temperature regulation
rubric: Even mild dehydration (1-2% body weight) reduces aerobic performance and cognitive function.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Obesity is primarily caused by
options: Consuming more calories than are expended over time|Only eating fatty foods|Only lack of exercise|Only genetic factors
answer: Consuming more calories than are expended over time
rubric: Obesity results from a sustained energy imbalance; diet, physical activity, genetics and environment all contribute.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Sports nutrition recommends consuming carbohydrates before exercise to
options: Top up glycogen stores and provide readily available fuel|Build muscle|Reduce hydration needs|Increase recovery time
answer: Top up glycogen stores and provide readily available fuel
rubric: Pre-exercise carbohydrate loading maximises glycogen stores, delaying fatigue in endurance events.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Calcium is essential for
options: Bone and teeth strength, and muscle contraction|Energy production only|Vitamin absorption only|Blood clotting only
answer: Bone and teeth strength, and muscle contraction
rubric: Calcium is the primary mineral in bones and teeth and is critical for muscle and nerve function.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The main function of iron in the body is
options: Forming haemoglobin to carry oxygen in the blood|Building bones|Producing energy directly|Maintaining fluid balance
answer: Forming haemoglobin to carry oxygen in the blood
rubric: Iron is a component of haemoglobin; deficiency leads to anaemia and reduced oxygen-carrying capacity.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of
options: Vitamin A|Vitamin C|Vitamin D|Iron
answer: Vitamin A
rubric: Vitamin A (retinol) is required for the production of rhodopsin in the eye; deficiency impairs vision in low light.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A sports drink is most beneficial during
options: Prolonged exercise exceeding one hour where electrolytes and carbohydrates need replacing|All exercise regardless of duration|Short 10-minute workouts|Only after exercise
answer: Prolonged exercise exceeding one hour where electrolytes and carbohydrates need replacing
rubric: Sports drinks replenish carbohydrates and electrolytes (sodium, potassium) lost during sustained exercise.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Leisure is
options: Free time available after work, sleep and essential duties, used as the individual chooses|Time spent working|Time spent exercising only|Compulsory rest time
answer: Free time available after work, sleep and essential duties, used as the individual chooses
rubric: Leisure is discretionary time used for rest, recreation, hobbies and personal development.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The benefits of recreational activities include
options: Physical health, mental refreshment, social bonding and stress reduction|Only physical fitness|Only competitive achievement|Only weight management
answer: Physical health, mental refreshment, social bonding and stress reduction
rubric: Recreation restores energy and well-being and fosters social connections.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Outdoor recreation activities include
options: Hiking, swimming, camping and cycling|Only watching television|Only video games|Only reading
answer: Hiking, swimming, camping and cycling
rubric: Outdoor recreation activities take place in natural settings and combine physical activity with environmental engagement.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Active recreation involves
options: Physical engagement such as sports, dancing and aerobics|Only passive entertainment|Only watching sports|Only reading
answer: Physical engagement such as sports, dancing and aerobics
rubric: Active recreation contributes to physical fitness while providing enjoyment and social interaction.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Passive recreation involves
options: Activities such as reading, watching films or listening to music that require little physical effort|Competitive sport|Athletics training|Heavy physical labour
answer: Activities such as reading, watching films or listening to music that require little physical effort
rubric: Passive recreation provides mental stimulation and relaxation without strenuous physical activity.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Play in physical education is important for children because
options: It develops physical, cognitive, social and emotional skills|It only entertains children|It replaces formal education|It is always competitive
answer: It develops physical, cognitive, social and emotional skills
rubric: Free play is essential for childhood development across all domains.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A national park or game reserve contributes to recreation by
options: Providing natural settings for eco-tourism, wildlife viewing and outdoor activities|Generating revenue only|Serving as farmland|Providing industrial space
answer: Providing natural settings for eco-tourism, wildlife viewing and outdoor activities
rubric: Natural reserves offer opportunities for nature-based recreation that also promotes conservation awareness.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The concept of wellness encompasses
options: Physical, mental, social, emotional and spiritual dimensions of health|Only physical fitness|Only the absence of disease|Only mental health
answer: Physical, mental, social, emotional and spiritual dimensions of health
rubric: Wellness is a proactive, multidimensional approach to living a healthy and fulfilling life.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Therapeutic recreation is
options: Using recreational activities to help people with disabilities or illness improve their quality of life|Competitive sport only|Only outdoor recreation|Only aquatics
answer: Using recreational activities to help people with disabilities or illness improve their quality of life
rubric: Therapeutic recreation uses leisure as a medium to achieve health outcomes and improve functioning.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Dance as a recreational and cultural activity is important because
options: It promotes fitness, self-expression, cultural identity and social bonding|It is only for entertainment|It is only a competitive sport|It replaces formal exercise
answer: It promotes fitness, self-expression, cultural identity and social bonding
rubric: Dance combines aerobic exercise with artistic and cultural expression.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Swimming as a recreational activity benefits the body by
options: Providing full-body low-impact aerobic exercise|Only strengthening legs|Only reducing weight|Only cooling the body
answer: Providing full-body low-impact aerobic exercise
rubric: Swimming engages all major muscle groups with minimal joint stress, making it ideal for all ages.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The role of schools in promoting recreation includes
options: Providing sports facilities, physical education classes and extracurricular activities|Only providing academic lessons|Restricting outdoor activity|Only providing a library
answer: Providing sports facilities, physical education classes and extracurricular activities
rubric: Schools are key settings for developing recreational habits and physical literacy in young people.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Socialisation through sport and recreation refers to
options: Learning social values, roles and norms through participation in physical activity|Playing alone only|Competing against others only|Watching sport only
answer: Learning social values, roles and norms through participation in physical activity
rubric: Sport socialises participants into values of teamwork, fair play, respect and discipline.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Intramural sports are
options: Sporting competitions organised within a single institution|International competitions|Inter-school competitions|Professional league competitions
answer: Sporting competitions organised within a single institution
rubric: Intramural sports promote participation and recreation among students within one school or college.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The primary aim of recreational programming in communities is
options: To provide enjoyable activities that improve quality of life for all residents|To train elite athletes|To maximise profit|To reduce school attendance
answer: To provide enjoyable activities that improve quality of life for all residents
rubric: Community recreation programmes promote inclusive participation, health and social cohesion.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The IAAF (now World Athletics) governs which sport?
options: Athletics (track and field)|Football|Swimming|Basketball
answer: Athletics (track and field)
rubric: World Athletics is the international governing body for track and field, road running and race walking.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Interschool sports competitions in Nigeria are primarily organised by
options: State and federal ministries of education and their sports councils|NAFDAC|INEC|The Central Bank of Nigeria
answer: State and federal ministries of education and their sports councils
rubric: Education authorities organise interschool games to promote sport among secondary school students.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The West African School Certificate (WASC) sports festival promotes
options: Competition and physical development among secondary school students in West Africa|Professional athletics only|University sport only|Primary school sport only
answer: Competition and physical development among secondary school students in West Africa
rubric: The WASC games build sportsmanship and regional unity among West African secondary school students.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Thomas Arnold is associated with the development of Physical Education because
options: He introduced organised games and sport into English public schools|He invented the modern Olympic Games|He wrote the rules of football|He founded the IOC
answer: He introduced organised games and sport into English public schools
rubric: Thomas Arnold, headmaster of Rugby School, formalised competitive sport as part of education in the 19th century.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A school sports day serves the educational purpose of
options: Promoting physical fitness, healthy competition and school community spirit|Replacing normal academic lessons|Testing athletic talent only|Training professional athletes
answer: Promoting physical fitness, healthy competition and school community spirit
rubric: Sports days encourage participation, fair play and social cohesion among students.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The high jump bar is placed on
options: Pegs or cups on upright standards|A fixed pole|A suspended wire|The ground
answer: Pegs or cups on upright standards
rubric: The crossbar rests on pegs; it must fall for the jump to be a failure.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In the shot put, the implement must land inside
options: A marked sector of 34.92 degrees|A circle|A sandpit|Any flat area
answer: A marked sector of 34.92 degrees
rubric: The throwing sector is a marked 34.92-degree wedge; throws landing outside are fouls.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The Straddle technique in high jump involves
options: Going over the bar face down|Going over the bar back first|Jumping from both feet|Using a pole
answer: Going over the bar face down
rubric: The straddle (Western Roll) preceded the Fosbury Flop; the jumper goes face-down over the bar.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Field event judges measure a throw or jump from
options: The nearest mark made by the implement or body in the landing area to the take-off line|The furthest mark|The average of three attempts|The first attempt only
answer: The nearest mark made by the implement or body in the landing area to the take-off line
rubric: Measurement is always from the nearest break in the landing surface to the take-off line or circle.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: An athlete is allowed a maximum of three attempts in the qualifying round of a field event, and the best
options: Valid performance determines whether the athlete advances to the final|Attempt is always the first|Attempt counts as zero|Attempt is discarded
answer: Valid performance determines whether the athlete advances to the final
rubric: The best valid mark from qualifying determines advancement; athletes may stop after reaching the qualifying standard.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Kwashiorkor is a nutritional deficiency caused by
options: Severe protein deficiency despite adequate or excessive caloric intake|Vitamin C deficiency|Iron deficiency|Vitamin D deficiency
answer: Severe protein deficiency despite adequate or excessive caloric intake
rubric: Kwashiorkor is characterised by oedema, pot belly and hair discolouration and is common in children.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Marasmus is a severe form of malnutrition caused by
options: Deficiency of both protein and total calories (energy)|Protein deficiency alone|Vitamin A deficiency|Iron deficiency
answer: Deficiency of both protein and total calories (energy)
rubric: Marasmus results in extreme wasting; unlike kwashiorkor, oedema is absent.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The glycaemic index (GI) of a food indicates
options: How quickly it raises blood sugar levels|Its protein content|Its fat content|Its fibre content
answer: How quickly it raises blood sugar levels
rubric: Low-GI foods cause a slower, steadier rise in blood sugar, which is beneficial for endurance performance.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Post-exercise recovery nutrition should ideally include
options: Carbohydrates and protein consumed within 30-60 minutes of exercise|Only water|Only fat|Only vitamins
answer: Carbohydrates and protein consumed within 30-60 minutes of exercise
rubric: Post-exercise carbohydrate replenishes glycogen while protein promotes muscle repair during the recovery window.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: An athlete who avoids all animal products follows a
options: Vegan diet|Vegetarian diet|Pescatarian diet|Omnivore diet
answer: Vegan diet
rubric: Vegans exclude all animal-derived foods; athletes must plan carefully to meet protein, iron, B12 and calcium needs.
